editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked every prose paragraph against the English, including the last 40% (the BasicMapper section): the TransformationPass/AnalysisPass contrast ("Transformation 패스는 Circuit을 수정하도록 설계된 반면, Analysis 패스는 이후 패스에서 사용할 정보를 추출하기 위한 용도입니다"), the layer definition ("서로 겹치지 않는 qubit 집합에 작용하는 연산들이 포함되어 독립적으로 실행될 수 있습니다"), the apply_operation_front nuance ("실질적으로 첫 번째로 실행되는 연산이 됩니다"), and the substitute_node_with_dag caveat ("나머지 Circuit과의 연결은 유지합니다") are all preserved with no inverted condition, swapped quantity, dropped caveat or added claim. The one thing a native technical editor would change is a within-file split on "transpiler": the title/description use the Korean 트랜스파일러 패스 / 트랜스파일 단계, while every body mention keeps the English form (Transpiler 패스, 커스텀 Transpiler 패스 작성, Transpiler 파이프라인) — the concept stays perfectly identifiable, so this is cosmetic, not misleading. Register is the standard 합니다체 with 하세요-form imperatives (사용하세요, 설치하세요, 참고하세요), consistent and never 하십시오체/드리-.

examples.source: Work with DAGs in transpiler passes / write custom transpiler passes / This is how the transpiler pipeline operates
examples.translation: 트랜스파일러 패스에서 DAG 사용하기 (title) … 커스텀 Transpiler 패스를 작성하는 (line 19) … Transpiler 파이프라인이 동작하는 방식입니다 (line 164)
examples.suggested: Use one rendering of "transpiler" throughout — either 트랜스파일러 패스 everywhere, or the kept English Transpiler everywhere, matching the ko glossary.
examples.why: The same core term appears in two forms on one page (Korean transliteration in the title/description, English in every body sentence). The concept remains unambiguous, so this is a MINOR consistency slip, not something that misleads a learner.

editor_note: Both delta entries are semantically faithful heading translations — nothing misleading, and 카탈로그 함수 / 사용자 정의 함수 are correct renderings of "Catalog Functions" / "Custom Functions". The defect is within-file consistency: these two H4 headings are now translated, but the prose directly beneath each one, and everywhere else on the page, keeps the terms in English — line 499 reads "인스턴스에서 Catalog Functions를 제거하려면…", line 524 "…동일하게 Catalog Functions가 지워집니다", line 528 "인스턴스에서 Custom Functions를 제거하려면…", and line 412 "Catalog Functions 및 Custom Functions에 대한 액세스를 부여하도록…". The page otherwise treats these as product names alongside untranslated "Qiskit Functions" and "Functions 액세스 구성", so a reader jumps from a Korean heading to an English term for the same thing one line later. Recommend aligning the headings with the body — either keep "Catalog Functions"/"Custom Functions" in the headings too, or gloss once (e.g. 카탈로그 함수(Catalog Functions)) and stay consistent.

examples.source: Custom Functions {#custom-functions}

examples.suggested: Custom Functions (or 사용자 정의 함수(Custom Functions)) — matching the body text
examples.why: Line 528 immediately below says "인스턴스에서 Custom Functions를 제거하려면" and line 553 says "custom functions가 지워집니다", so the translated heading is out of step with the English term used in the surrounding prose and with the `custom_functions` field name it maps to.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — every card description tracks the English claim exactly (e.g. "인접하지 않은 Qubit 간의 얽힘 Gate를 분해하여 Transpiler된 Circuit의 깊이를 줄입니다", "노이즈 모델 정보를 흡수한 대상 관측량을 측정하여 기댓값을 완화합니다"), and the caveat in "일반적으로 샘플링 오버헤드가 증가합니다" is kept rather than softened. Core domain terms are correct and consistent (observable→관측량, expectation value→기댓값, Hamiltonian→해밀토니안, subspace→부분 공간, fidelity→충실도). Two things a native technical editor would still change: "bitstring" is rendered two ways in adjacent cards — 비트 문자열 (post-selection card) vs 비트스트링 (M3 card) — and "An HPC-ready implementation" becomes "HPC 지원 구현", which reads as "HPC-supporting" rather than "ready to run on HPC" (HPC 환경에 바로 사용할 수 있는 구현 would be closer). Neither would mislead a learner about the physics or the tooling.

examples.source: Filter out non-Markovian noise in sampled bitstrings … / … a reduced subspace defined by noisy bitstrings.
examples.translation: 샘플링된 비트 문자열에서 비마르코프 노이즈를 필터링합니다. / 노이즈가 있는 비트스트링으로 정의된 축소된 부분 공간에서…
examples.suggested: Use 비트스트링 in both cards (or 비트 문자열 in both).
examples.why: The same source term 'bitstring' is rendered two different ways in two cards of the same section; the concept stays identifiable, so this is a consistency slip rather than a comprehension risk.

examples.source: An HPC-ready implementation of the SQD addon
examples.translation: SQD 애드온의 HPC 지원 구현으로
examples.suggested: HPC 환경에 바로 사용할 수 있는 SQD 애드온 구현으로
examples.why: 'HPC 지원' reads as 'supports HPC' (a feature the package offers) rather than 'ready for HPC use'; a Korean HPC engineer would phrase readiness, not support.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful across the technical core — the `layout_mode` options (keep/improve/optimize), the `replace_only_if_better=False` caveat, block-size limits (9 / 65-33-27 / 6 qubit blocks), the "cores plus four" thread default, and the "raise a warning and leave the original sub-circuit unchanged" fallback are all rendered correctly, so nothing here teaches a false concept. Four editorial defects remain. (1) In the opening paragraph the parenthetical is attached to the wrong noun: "기존 휴리스틱 알고리즘(낮은 깊이 및 CNOT 수 등)보다" reads as "heuristic algorithms such as low depth and CNOT count", whereas the English "(such as lower depth and CNOT count)" exemplifies the *better results*; the metric-vs-algorithm distinction is garbled. (2) In the AI circuit synthesis intro the source lists four circuit types — Clifford, Linear Function, Permutation, **Pauli Network** — and the Korean drops "Pauli Network" from the enumeration, even though *AIPauliNetworkSynthesis* appears in the pass list below. (3) "Boolean satisfiability solver" is rendered "불리언 만족도 해석기" — 만족도 means "degree of satisfaction" and 해석기 means interpreter/parser; the conventional term is 부울/불리언 충족가능성 솔버 (or SAT 솔버). The inline English gloss keeps it identifiable, hence minor. (4) Within-file inconsistency: "sub-circuit" is 서브 Circuit everywhere except the *CollectPauliNetworks* bullet, which says 원본 서브 회로.

examples.source: They often produce better results than existing heuristic algorithms (such as lower depth and CNOT count), but are also much faster than optimization algorithms such as Boolean satisfiability solvers.
examples.translation: 기존 휴리스틱 알고리즘(낮은 깊이 및 CNOT 수 등)보다 더 나은 결과를 자주 도출하며, 불리언 만족도 해석기(Boolean satisfiability solver)와 같은 최적화 알고리즘보다 훨씬 빠릅니다.
examples.suggested: 기존 휴리스틱 알고리즘보다 더 나은 결과(예: 더 낮은 깊이와 CNOT 수)를 내는 경우가 많으며, 불리언 충족가능성 솔버(Boolean satisfiability solver)와 같은 최적화 알고리즘보다 훨씬 빠릅니다.
examples.why: The parenthetical modifies "better results" in the source, but in Korean it is glued to 기존 휴리스틱 알고리즘, so it reads as naming kinds of heuristic algorithm and the reader loses which metrics the improvement is measured in. Same sentence also mistranslates "satisfiability solver" as 만족도 해석기 (satisfaction-degree interpreter).

examples.source: The AI circuit synthesis passes allow you to optimize pieces of different circuit types (Clifford, Linear Function, Permutation, Pauli Network) by re-synthesizing them.
examples.translation: AI Circuit 합성 패스를 사용하면 다양한 Circuit 유형([Clifford](...), [Linear Function](...), [Permutation](...))의 일부를 재합성하여 최적화할 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: ... 다양한 Circuit 유형([Clifford](...), [Linear Function](...), [Permutation](...), Pauli Network)의 일부를 재합성하여 ...
examples.why: "Pauli Network" is dropped from the enumeration of supported circuit types, so the intro implicitly excludes a type that the bullet list below (AIPauliNetworkSynthesis, CollectPauliNetworks) does support.

examples.source: CollectPauliNetworks: Collects Pauli Network blocks and stores the original sub-circuit to compare against it after synthesis.
examples.translation: *CollectPauliNetworks*: Pauli Network 블록을 수집하고 원본 서브 회로를 저장하여 합성 후 비교합니다.
examples.suggested: *CollectPauliNetworks*: Pauli Network 블록을 수집하고, 합성 후 비교를 위해 원래 서브 Circuit을 저장합니다.
examples.why: Every other occurrence in the file uses 서브 Circuit (and the 합성 후 비교를 위해 … 저장합니다 pattern); this one bullet switches to 서브 회로 and reorders the clause, breaking the parallelism of the three sibling bullets.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination; the tricky bullet "For the Flex Plan… unless the limit has been increased or, for the Premium Plan, after the next usage window starts" is correctly disentangled into two sentences that keep both plan conditions intact, and the "할당량이 한도로 설정되지 않은 경우, 인스턴스는 할당된 시간을 초과하여 사용할 수 있다" caveat is preserved. What a native editor would change is the literal window vocabulary: "rolling time window" → "28일 롤링 시간 창" and "usage window" → "사용 창" both calque English "window" as 창 (a pane), where Korean cloud/quantum docs say 기간 or 윈도우; 창 reads distinctly like MT here. Two smaller slips: "priority in the queue" loses its 큐에서의 qualifier (just "우선순위"), and the "minimize job usage" link is retitled "작업의 양자 시간을 최소화", inserting 양자 that the source link text does not have. Terminology is otherwise correct and consistent (워크로드 vs 작업 kept distinct, 공정 배분 알고리즘/스케줄러 consistent, QPU/Premium/Flex kept in English).

examples.source: a rolling time window of 28 days … after the next usage window starts
examples.translation: 28일 롤링 시간 창(Premium 플랜 사용자의 경우) … 다음 사용 창이 시작되면
examples.suggested: 28일 롤링 기간(…) … 다음 사용 기간이 시작되면
examples.why: 'window' is calqued as 창, which in Korean reads as a physical/UI window pane. Korean cloud and quantum docs render this as 기간 (or 윈도우 when transliterating). Recognizable in context, so not misleading, but it is the clearest MT tell in the file.

examples.source: used by the fair-share algorithm to determine the priority in the queue

examples.source: Review suggestions to [minimize job usage](minimize-time).
examples.translation: [작업의 양자 시간을 최소화](minimize-time)하기 위한 제안을 검토하세요.
examples.suggested: [작업 사용량을 최소화](minimize-time)하기 위한 제안을 검토하세요.
examples.why: The link text adds 양자 (quantum), which is not in the source's 'job usage'. It happens to match the target page's topic so it does not mislead, but it is an unsourced addition to the anchor text.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: the single prose sentence ("액세스를 할당하는 데 도움이 되도록 사용 가능한 역할과 각 역할에 매핑된 작업을 검토하세요…") faithfully carries the English, 해요체 holds throughout (검토하세요/참조하세요/알아보세요), and every one of the 41 permission→endpoint table rows maps 1:1 to the source with no swapped or dropped entry. Two editorial slips remain. (1) The two parallel service names are handled inconsistently: "IBM Quantum Compute Service" is left untranslated in the H2 while the sibling "IBM Quantum System Service" becomes "IBM Quantum 시스템 서비스" — one file, two conventions for the same class of product name. (2) The table header "Required by" is rendered "필요한 대상" ("the target that needs it"), which inverts the reading direction a Korean reader expects; the column actually lists the API calls that require the permission, so "필요한 작업" or "이 권한이 필요한 API" would be the natural technical-writer choice. Neither would mislead a learner about the API itself.

examples.source: ## IBM Quantum Compute Service … ## IBM Quantum System Service
examples.translation: ## IBM Quantum Compute Service … ## IBM Quantum 시스템 서비스
examples.suggested: Keep both as product names in English ("IBM Quantum Compute Service" / "IBM Quantum System Service"), or translate both consistently.
examples.why: The two headings are a parallel pair naming the same class of IBM service; translating only the second one breaks the visual and terminological parallel inside a single short page.

examples.source: | Permission | Required by |
examples.translation: | 권한 | 필요한 대상 |
examples.suggested: | 권한 | 이 권한이 필요한 작업 | (or 필요한 API 호출)
examples.why: '필요한 대상' reads as 'the object that is needed/required', which points the wrong way; the column lists the endpoints that require the permission. A Korean technical writer would spell out the relation rather than use the bare noun 대상.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout, including the order-sensitive claims that matter most here: 비트 $0$은 최하위 비트(least significant bit), 비트 $n-1$은 최상위 비트, the string rule (비트 $n-1$은 가장 왼쪽 비트이고 비트 $0$은 가장 오른쪽 비트), the `reverse_bits` 인수 caveat ("생성된 다이어그램에만 영향을 미치며 Circuit 자체에는 영향을 주지 않습니다"), and the closing contrast that in the new circuit X-Gate는 qubit $1$에 작용한다; terminology (제어/타겟, 계산 기저 상태, 진폭, 십진수 정수) is conventional and consistent, and the 합니다체 + 하세요 register matches the rest of the ko locale (hello-world.mdx, guides/index.mdx).

No misleading content: every quantitative and conditional statement survives intact — the reset bullet keeps the direction ("확률 `p_reset`으로 0 대신 1로 리셋합니다"), the $T_2 \le 2T_1$ constraint is stated as a hard requirement, the tensor-vs-expand ordering distinction and the qubit-order caveat ("qubit [0, 1]에 적용되는 오류와 qubit [1, 0]에 적용되는 오류는 서로 다릅니다") are all correct, and the non-local-error workaround paragraph is faithful. What a native technical editor would change is terminology consistency: "relaxation" is rendered two ways in the same file — 완화 in the `thermal_relaxation_error` table row ("열적 완화 채널", "완화 시간 상수") but 이완 in the Example-2 section ("T1/T2 열 이완", "열 이완 시간 상수"); likewise "composition" appears as 조합(composition) in the lead-in and 합성 in the bullet immediately below it. Two smaller precision slips: "excited state thermal population $p_1$" becomes "여기 상태 열적 분포" (thermal *distribution*, where the conventional Korean is 점유수/점유 확률), and "include functions for many common error types" is flattened to "많은 오류 유형을 지원합니다" ("supports"), which is about the module rather than about the helper functions. Register (합니다체 declaratives + -세요 imperatives) matches the ko corpus convention and is fine.

examples.source: thermal relaxation ... relaxation time constants $T_1$, $T_2$ ... / T1/T2 thermal relaxation ... a thermal relaxation time constant $T_1$
examples.translation: 열적 완화 채널 / 완화 시간 상수  …  T1/T2 열 이완 / 열 이완 시간 상수
examples.suggested: Pick one and use it throughout — 열 이완 / 이완 시간 상수 (the more common physics rendering) in both the table row and the Example-2 section.
examples.why: The same concept (thermal relaxation) is split between 완화 and 이완 inside one page; a learner scanning the table and then the T1/T2 section cannot tell they are the same channel. Recognizable, so MINOR, not misleading.

examples.source: can be combined by using composition, tensor product, and tensor expansion … * Composition: $\cal{E}(\rho)=\cal{E_2}(\cal{E_1}(\rho))$
examples.translation: 조합(composition), 텐서 곱, 텐서 확장(역순 텐서 곱)을 사용하여 … * 합성: …
examples.suggested: Use 합성 in both places (합성(composition), 텐서 곱, 텐서 확장 … * 합성:).
examples.why: The gloss line calls the operation 조합 and the bullet two lines later calls it 합성 — an avoidable within-file split on a term the reader must match to `compose()`.

examples.source: and excited state thermal population $p_1$
examples.translation: 여기 상태 열적 분포 $p_1$
examples.suggested: 여기 상태 열적 점유 확률 $p_1$ (or 여기 상태 열적 점유수)
examples.why: 'Population' here is the occupation probability of the excited state, not a distribution; 분포 is a defensible-sounding but imprecise rendering that repeats in three table rows.

examples.source: These are contained in the `noise` module and include functions for many common error types used in quantum computing research.
examples.translation: 이 함수들은 `noise` 모듈에 포함되어 있으며, 양자 컴퓨팅 연구에서 일반적으로 사용되는 많은 오류 유형을 지원합니다.
examples.suggested: … `noise` 모듈에 포함되어 있으며, 양자 컴퓨팅 연구에서 일반적으로 사용되는 여러 오류 유형에 대한 함수를 제공합니다.
examples.why: 'include functions for' is flattened into '지원합니다' (supports), shifting the subject from the set of helper functions to a vaguer support claim. Harmless for comprehension, but it loses the one-function-per-error-type framing the table then illustrates.

editor_note: Prose is fluent and faithful overall — the monitoring/calibration/benchmarking flow, the "하루 2시간 미만" Heron figure, "결맞음 시간" for coherence times, and the whole scheduling bullet list all match the English exactly. Three word-choice defects a native technical editor would fix: (1) "ideal values" is rendered "이상값" in "파라미터가 이상값에서 벗어난 것" — in Korean engineering prose 이상값 reads first as 異常값 (outlier/abnormal value), so the trigger condition can be parsed backwards; it should be "이상적인 값" or "최적값". (2) "the best 100-qubit length string" (a chain/path of qubits) becomes "100-Qubit 길이 문자열", i.e. a *text* string — the correct rendering is 사슬/체인/연결선. (3) the hedge in "(and could include pausing calibrations)" is flattened to a flat "(캘리브레이션 일시 중지 포함)", turning a possibility into a stated inclusion. None of these invert a whole claim, so the page still teaches correctly, but all three are worth correcting.

examples.source: Calibrations are triggered whenever monitoring jobs indicate that parameters such as pulse amplitudes or angles have deviated from their ideal values.
examples.translation: 캘리브레이션은 모니터링 작업에서 펄스 진폭이나 각도와 같은 파라미터가 이상값에서 벗어난 것이 감지될 때마다 트리거됩니다.
examples.suggested: … 파라미터가 이상적인 값(최적값)에서 벗어난 것이 감지될 때마다 트리거됩니다.
examples.why: '이상값' is the standard Korean word for an outlier/abnormal value (異常値). Read that way, the sentence says calibration fires when a parameter deviates *from the anomalous value* — the opposite of the intended 'deviates from its ideal value'. 이상적인 값 or 최적값 removes the homograph.

examples.source: Layer fidelity (EPLG), for the best 100-qubit length string
examples.translation: 레이어 충실도 (EPLG) — 최적의 100-Qubit 길이 문자열 기준
examples.suggested: 레이어 충실도 (EPLG) — 최적의 100큐비트 길이 사슬(체인) 기준
examples.why: 'string' here is a physical chain of connected qubits on the device, not a character string; 문자열 is specifically a text string in Korean and points the reader at the wrong object for the EPLG metric.

examples.source: the calibration strategy for gates associated with affected qubits might be automatically modified (and could include pausing calibrations)
examples.translation: …캘리브레이션 전략이 자동으로 수정될 수 있으며(캘리브레이션 일시 중지 포함), TLS 활동이 허용 수준으로 감소할 때까지 유지됩니다.
examples.suggested: …자동으로 수정될 수 있으며(캘리브레이션 일시 중지가 포함될 수도 있습니다), …
examples.why: 'could include' is a hedge about one possible form the modification takes; the bare '포함' states it as something the modification does include, mildly strengthening the claim.

editor_note: Meaning is sound throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat: "error detection" is correctly 오류 감지 (not 정정), the PNA sentence keeps the full chain "Pauli 전파를 사용하여 학습된 노이즈 채널의 역을 관측 가능량(observables)에 흡수시킴으로써 기댓값의 오류를 완화", and "with reduced variance" survives as "분산을 줄이면서". Three editor-level items remain. (1) "how to get started today" is literalized to a calendar day — "오늘 시작하는 방법은 … 확인하세요" reads as "how to start on today's date"; a native writer would use "지금 바로 시작하는 방법". (2) "more tightly bound the sensitivity to errors" → "오류 민감도를 더 엄격하게 제한합니다" shifts *bounding an estimate* toward *restricting the quantity itself*; "민감도의 상한을 더 엄격하게 한정합니다" would be exact (the following sentence keeps the intent, so it is not misleading). (3) Register: the file is consistently 합니다체 (소개합니다 / 출시했습니다 / 기법입니다 / 제한합니다) plus humble 저희, not the project's 해요체 — standard for Korean docs and internally consistent, so flagged only as a convention slip.

examples.source: Check out the [blog] and [documentation] for how to get started today.
examples.translation: 오늘 시작하는 방법은 [블로그]와 [문서]를 확인하세요.
examples.suggested: 지금 바로 시작하는 방법은 [블로그]와 [문서]를 확인해 보세요.
examples.why: "today" here is idiomatic emphasis ("get started today"), not a date. 오늘 makes it sound like instructions valid for the current day; 지금 바로 carries the call-to-action a Korean technical writer would use.

examples.source: uses classical simulations to more tightly bound the sensitivity to errors throughout the circuit
examples.translation: 고전 시뮬레이션을 사용하여 Circuit 전반에 걸친 오류 민감도를 더 엄격하게 제한합니다
examples.suggested: 고전 시뮬레이션을 사용하여 Circuit 전반의 오류 민감도 상한을 더 엄격하게 한정합니다
examples.why: English "bound" = tighten the estimated upper bound; 제한하다 reads as actually restricting/reducing the sensitivity itself, which is a different mechanism. Mild — the next sentence (더 효율적이고 표적화된 PEC 적용) restores the intent, so it does not mislead.

examples.source: Introducing Qiskit Paulice … We recently released two new addons
examples.translation: …새로운 애드온인 Qiskit Paulice를 소개합니다 … 저희는 최근 … 두 가지 새로운 애드온을 출시했습니다
examples.suggested: …Qiskit Paulice를 소개해요 … 최근 … 두 가지 새로운 애드온을 출시했어요
examples.why: The file is uniformly 합니다체 with humble 저희 rather than the project's 해요체 convention. Consistent and idiomatic for Korean documentation, so a convention slip only — not a comprehension problem.

editor_note: Meaning is fully faithful across all four prose paragraphs: the discontinuation notice ("프리뷰 서비스가 중단되었으며 … 확장이 보관 처리되었습니다"), the rationale sentence ("피드백과 사용 패턴을 바탕으로, 더 많은 사용자가 … 로컬에서 실행하고"), the "models remain available for local use" caveat, and the two 28 October 2025 bullets ("더 새로운 … 모델로 업데이트했습니다", "로컬 추론을 위한 두 개의 새로운 모델을 Hugging Face에 오픈 소스로 공개했습니다") all carry the English claims with no inverted, softened or added assertions. The one thing a Korean technical editor would change is that the two date headings are left verbatim in English ("## 29 May 2026", "### 28 October 2025") instead of the conventional "2026년 5월 29일" / "2025년 10월 28일" — visible body text, not just an anchor, so a Korean reader gets English date strings in an otherwise fully localized changelog. Nothing here misleads; terminology ("확장" for VS Code extensions, "로컬 추론", "워크플로") is conventional and consistent, and register is uniform 합니다체 with 해요체 imperatives ("참조하세요"), which is the right documentation voice.

examples.why: Date headings are user-visible prose left untranslated; Korean docs write dates as 연-월-일. The heading anchors ({#29-may-2026}) are explicit and unaffected, so localizing the visible text breaks no links.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the July 2026 pre-flight block keeps all three checks in order (런타임 용량 / 지정한 백엔드 접근 / 사용 가능한 백엔드 하나 이상), the four new methods map correctly (usage()→남은 런타임 용량, least_busy()→대기 작업이 가장 적은 백엔드), and the dense 2024 circuit/application-function paragraphs are accurate, including TEM/PEC ("PEC(확률적 오류 상쇄) 방법보다 적은 샷으로 추정량을 얻기 위한 … TEM(텐서 네트워크 오류 완화)"). Two small editorial slips: the Quantum Portfolio Optimizer sentence flips the axis order of "Sharpe ratio versus return" into "샤프 비율 대비 수익률" (reads as return relative to Sharpe ratio), and "Over the coming weeks, every function will give…" becomes "앞으로 몇 주 동안 … 제공합니다", which reads as a few-week window rather than a progressive rollout. Terminology is consistent (회로 함수 / 애플리케이션 함수, 오류 억제·오류 완화, 트랜스파일, 관측량, 샷); register is a consistent 합니다체 with -세요 imperatives (참조하세요, 살펴보세요) and no humble 드리- forms, which is a defensible docs convention rather than a defect.

examples.source: this function calculates a portfolio's Sharpe ratio versus return across a specified time period
examples.translation: 지정된 기간 동안 포트폴리오의 샤프 비율 대비 수익률을 계산합니다
examples.suggested: 지정된 기간 동안 포트폴리오의 수익률 대비 샤프 비율을 계산합니다
examples.why: ‘A 대비 B’ in Korean reads as B measured against A, so the rendering reverses the English pairing (Sharpe ratio against return). Not concept-breaking, but a quant-finance reader would read the axes the wrong way round.

examples.source: Over the coming weeks, every function will give detailed information to help you run, debug, and analyze your workflows.
examples.translation: 앞으로 몇 주 동안 모든 함수는 워크플로를 실행, 디버그 및 분석하는 데 도움이 되는 자세한 정보를 제공합니다.
examples.suggested: 앞으로 몇 주에 걸쳐 모든 함수가 워크플로를 실행, 디버그 및 분석하는 데 도움이 되는 자세한 정보를 제공하게 됩니다.
examples.why: ‘앞으로 몇 주 동안’ frames it as a temporary few-week period during which the information is available; the English announces a staged rollout that ends in a permanent capability. ‘몇 주에 걸쳐 … 하게 됩니다’ restores the rollout sense.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner: the single substantive paragraph (v0.3.0) keeps every claim intact, including the hedge in "might be faster" → "더 빠르고 더 나은 결과를 낼 수 있는", and 트랜스파일/트랜스파일러 패스 are the correct conventional renderings. Three editorial slips remain. (1) "the service invites users to experiment with" → "이 서비스는 사용자가 ... 실험해 볼 수 있도록 초대합니다" is a direct calque of "invite"; Korean technical prose does not have a service "초대하다" a user — "실험해 볼 수 있습니다" or "실험해 보도록 권장합니다" is what a native writer would put. (2) "client" is rendered two ways inside one short file: "Qiskit Transpiler Service client 변경 로그" and the "Qiskit Transpiler Service client 릴리스 노트" link keep the English word, while the H1 says "Qiskit Transpiler Service 클라이언트 v0.15.2". (3) "Perhaps most importantly" is flattened to "무엇보다도", dropping the author's hedge — a mild strengthening, not enough to mislead. Also cosmetic: the "## January 2026" heading was left untranslated while "## 이전 업데이트" was translated.

examples.source: the service invites users to experiment with new and improved AI-powered transpiler passes
examples.translation: 이 서비스는 사용자가 새롭고 개선된 AI 기반 트랜스파일러 패스를 실험해 볼 수 있도록 초대합니다
examples.suggested: 이 서비스를 통해 새롭고 개선된 AI 기반 트랜스파일러 패스를 직접 실험해 볼 수 있습니다
examples.why: '초대합니다' is a word-for-word calque of 'invites'. In Korean an inanimate service does not 초대하다 a user; the idiomatic move is to turn it into a capability sentence.

examples.source: Qiskit Transpiler Service client
examples.translation: '…client 변경 로그' (frontmatter/title) vs '…서비스 클라이언트 v0.15.2' (H1) vs '…Service client 릴리스 노트' (link text)
examples.suggested: Pick one form — keep the product string 'Qiskit Transpiler Service client' verbatim everywhere, or use '클라이언트' everywhere
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency on the same product name across three lines of a very short page; recognizable, so MINOR, but a native editor would unify it.

examples.source: Perhaps most importantly, the service invites users to…
examples.translation: 무엇보다도 이 서비스는 …
examples.suggested: 어쩌면 가장 중요한 점은, 이 서비스가 …
examples.why: 'Perhaps' is dropped, turning a hedged claim into a flat assertion of what matters most. Small strengthening, not misleading on its own.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat: the v2.3 bullets carry every qualifier correctly (「전체 컴파일러 파이프라인을 다시 빌드하지 않고도」 for "without rebuilding the entire compiler pipeline", 「초기 결함 허용 타겟, 특히 Clifford+T 타겟」 for "especially Clifford+T targets", and the beta/version caveat 「현재 베타 버전이며 `qiskit-ibm-runtime` 버전 0.47.0 이상이 필요합니다」). Domain terms are correct and consistent (사영 측정 = projective measurement, 결함 허용 = fault-tolerant, 오류 완화/억제 = error mitigation/suppression, 사후 선택 = postselection, 충실도 = fidelity, 트랜스파일러 패스). Two editorial slips: the entire lead sentence of the April 2026 Executor bullet is left untranslated English ("**Introducing the Executor primitive**: We're excited to announce…"), so a Korean reader hits raw English before the translated paragraph resumes; and the PauliProductMeasurement bullet repeats 「가능하게 하여 … 가능하게 합니다」 in one sentence, which a native technical writer would vary (e.g. 「…측정을 단일 연산으로 수행할 수 있게 하여 … 컴파일이 가능해집니다」). Register is the standard 합니다체 declarative + 「읽어보세요/방문하세요」 imperative mix used in Korean product docs — defensible, not flagged.

examples.source: **Introducing the Executor primitive**: We're excited to announce the release of the new `Executor` primitive and a new version of the noise-learning helper class, `NoiseLearnerV3`, both of which were first previewed at QDC 2025.
examples.translation: **Introducing the Executor primitive**: We're excited to announce the release of the new `Executor` primitive and a new version of the noise-learning helper class, `NoiseLearnerV3`, both of which were first previewed at QDC 2025.
examples.suggested: **Executor 프리미티브 소개**: 새로운 `Executor` 프리미티브와 노이즈 학습 헬퍼 클래스의 새 버전인 `NoiseLearnerV3`의 릴리스를 알려드립니다. 두 가지 모두 QDC 2025에서 처음 공개되었습니다.
examples.why: The whole lead-in sentence of the April 2026 entry is untranslated; the following paragraph is Korean, so the reader hits an English block mid-section. Not misleading (the content is repeated in the Korean that follows only partially), but it is an incomplete translation a native editor would fix.

examples.source: The new `PauliProductMeasurement` instruction enables joint projective measurement across multiple qubits in a single operation, unlocking compilation to Pauli-based computation - a common representation in fault-tolerant quantum computing.
examples.translation: 새로운 `PauliProductMeasurement` 명령은 여러 큐비트에 걸친 결합 사영 측정을 단일 연산으로 가능하게 하여, 결함 허용 양자 컴퓨팅에서 흔히 사용되는 표현 방식인 Pauli 기반 계산으로의 컴파일을 가능하게 합니다.
examples.suggested: 새로운 `PauliProductMeasurement` 명령을 사용하면 여러 큐비트에 대한 결합 사영 측정을 단일 연산으로 수행할 수 있고, 이를 통해 결함 허용 양자 컴퓨팅에서 흔히 쓰이는 표현 방식인 Pauli 기반 계산으로 컴파일할 수 있습니다.
examples.why: Meaning is correct, but 「가능하게 하여 … 가능하게 합니다」 repeats the same verb twice in one sentence — stiff, calqued 'enables … unlocking' phrasing a Korean technical writer would rewrite.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout the changelog — dates, quantities and conditions all survive (1 µs vs 250 µs rep delay, 20-500→20-2000 µs, 57 of 176 two-qubit gates below 1e-3, and the tricky "removed no sooner than 30 September 2024" correctly inverted to "2024년 9월 30일 이전에는 제거되지 않습니다"), so nothing teaches a false fact. What a native editor would change: "fleet-leading coherence" for `ibm_berlin` is inflated to "업계 최고 수준의 코히어런스" (industry-leading), a stronger claim than the English makes; "fleet" is rendered three ways in one file (플릿 / 전 세계 시스템 / 공유 시스템); and "steady, measured progress" becomes "꾸준하고 측정 가능한 발전" (measurable), a false-friend read of "measured". Three chunks are also left in English — the sentence "The new dynamic circuits is now available to all users on all backends, except some QPUs under the On-Prem Plan.", the heading "### `ibm_torino` to retire", and the 2024 AccordionItem titles "Third/Second/First quarter" (the 2025 block translates them as 3분기/2분기/1분기) — so a Korean-only reader loses the On-Prem caveat. Smaller: the H1 localizes the brand as "IBM Quantum 컴퓨팅 서비스" while the rest of the page, including the July 2026 rename section, keeps "IBM Quantum Compute Service", and "일반적인 오류를 문제 해결하고 해결하기 위한 권장 사항" is a redundant calque.

examples.source: while maintaining similar fleet-leading coherence (T$_1$ of ~350 µs)
examples.translation: 유사한 업계 최고 수준의 코히어런스(T$_1$ ~350 µs)를 유지하면서
examples.suggested: 자사 시스템(플릿) 중 최고 수준의 유사한 코히어런스(T$_1$ 약 350 µs)를 유지하면서
examples.why: "fleet-leading" is scoped to IBM's own fleet; "업계 최고 수준" claims industry leadership, a strengthened claim the English does not make (and the 31 July 2025 entry legitimately uses 업계 최고 수준 for the actual 'industry-leading' wording, so the two are now conflated).

examples.source: The new dynamic circuits is now available to all users on all backends, except some QPUs under the On-Prem Plan.
examples.translation: The new dynamic circuits is now available to all users on all backends, except some QPUs under the On-Prem Plan.
examples.suggested: 새로운 동적 회로는 이제 On-Prem Plan의 일부 QPU를 제외한 모든 백엔드에서 모든 사용자에게 제공됩니다.
examples.why: Untranslated body sentence: the Korean reader never gets the availability statement or its On-Prem exception, which is the caveat governing the whole bullet list that follows.

examples.source: the shared fleet across the two regions / our global fleet
examples.translation: 공유 플릿 … 공유 시스템 … 전 세계 시스템
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering (e.g. 플릿 or 시스템 군) and use it for every occurrence of "fleet".
examples.why: The same concept (IBM's QPU fleet) is rendered three different ways within one page; a reader cannot tell that 플릿, 공유 시스템 and 전 세계 시스템 all denote the same thing.

examples.source: This steady, measured progress is at the center of our strategy
examples.translation: 이러한 꾸준하고 측정 가능한 발전은 … 저희 전략의 중심에 있습니다
examples.suggested: 이러한 꾸준하고 신중한 발전은 …
examples.why: "measured" here means deliberate/considered, not "measurable"; 측정 가능한 reads as a machine-translation false friend.

examples.source: # IBM Quantum Compute Service
examples.translation: # IBM Quantum 컴퓨팅 서비스
examples.suggested: # IBM Quantum Compute Service
examples.why: The product name is kept in English everywhere else on the page, including the July 2026 section whose entire subject is the rename to "IBM Quantum Compute Service"; localizing only the H1 breaks the brand reference.

examples.source: recommendations for troubleshooting and resolving common errors
examples.translation: 일반적인 오류를 문제 해결하고 해결하기 위한 권장 사항
examples.suggested: 일반적인 오류를 진단하고 해결하는 데 도움이 되는 권장 사항
examples.why: "문제 해결하고 해결하기" repeats 해결 twice in a single phrase — a literal calque no Korean technical writer would leave in.

editor_note: Nothing in this file misleads: every translated paragraph tracks the English exactly (베타 상태 + `qiskit-ibm-runtime` 0.47.0 이상 요구, EstimatorV2/resilience_level 안내, v0.46.0 릴리스 노트 문장 모두 충실). The one real defect is coverage, not meaning: the entire lead bullet of the April 2026 entry — "**Introducing the Executor primitive**: We're excited to announce the release of the new `Executor` primitive and a new version of the noise-learning helper class, `NoiseLearnerV3`, both of which were first previewed at QDC 2025." — is left verbatim in English, so the headline announcement of the whole changelog entry is untranslated while the very next paragraph continues in Korean and refers back to it with "이들은". Secondary, non-counted observation: the file uses -합니다/-하세요 (합쇼체) throughout rather than 해요체, which is the normal register for Korean product docs and reads fine, but it is not the project's stated informal convention. Terminology is otherwise sound and consistent (오류 완화, 억제, 확률적 오류 상쇄(PEC), 측정 기반 사후 선택, 릴리스 노트), and keeping `directed execution model` / `shaded lightcones` in English is defensible for these unestablished technique names.

examples.source: **Introducing the Executor primitive**: We're excited to announce the release of the new `Executor` primitive and a new version of the noise-learning helper class, `NoiseLearnerV3`, both of which were first previewed at QDC 2025.
examples.translation: **Introducing the Executor primitive**: We're excited to announce the release of the new `Executor` primitive and a new version of the noise-learning helper class, `NoiseLearnerV3`, both of which were first previewed at QDC 2025.
examples.suggested: **Executor 프리미티브 소개**: 새로운 `Executor` 프리미티브와 노이즈 학습 헬퍼 클래스의 새 버전인 `NoiseLearnerV3`의 릴리스를 알려드립니다. 두 가지 모두 QDC 2025에서 처음 공개되었습니다.
examples.why: The headline bullet of the April 2026 entry is left entirely untranslated, so a Korean reader gets no Korean statement of what was released (Executor primitive, NoiseLearnerV3) or that both were first previewed at QDC 2025. The following Korean paragraph then opens with the anaphor "이들은" pointing back at an English-only antecedent.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, dropped caveats or hallucinations; the arithmetic section (A=2, B=3, 결과를 B를 보유하던 레지스터에 씁니다, 모든 1024번의 샷에서 5를 출력) and the amplitude/basis/angle encoding bullets all match the English exactly, and core terms are consistent (변분 양자 알고리즘, 파라미터화, 얽힘 Gate, 기저 상태, 유니터리 결합 클러스터 시험 상태). Three things a native technical editor would still change. In the quantum-volume paragraph, "the software stack transpiling and post-processing results" is rendered "결과를 Transpile하고 후처리하는 소프트웨어 스택", which attaches 결과 to Transpile as well — the stack transpiles circuits and post-processes results, so 회로를 Transpile하고 결과를 후처리하는 is the correct split. In the opening line "a library of popular circuits" becomes "인기 있는 Circuit 라이브러리", where 인기 있는 reads as modifying 라이브러리 rather than the circuits. Finally "assign these parameters to real values" is rendered "실제 값에 할당" (assign the parameters *to* values); Korean convention here is 실제 값으로 할당/지정.

examples.source: ...and the software stack transpiling and post-processing results.
examples.translation: 결과를 Transpile하고 후처리하는 소프트웨어 스택 등 컴퓨터의 모든 측면을 고려합니다.
examples.suggested: 회로를 Transpile하고 결과를 후처리하는 소프트웨어 스택 등 컴퓨터의 모든 측면을 고려합니다.
examples.why: The Korean makes 결과 the object of both verbs, implying the stack 'transpiles results'. Transpilation applies to circuits, not to measurement results, so the sentence slightly misstates what the software stack does.

examples.source: The Qiskit SDK includes a library of popular circuits to use as building blocks in your own programs.
examples.translation: Qiskit SDK에는 자신의 프로그램에서 빌딩 블록으로 사용할 수 있는 인기 있는 Circuit 라이브러리가 포함되어 있습니다.
examples.suggested: Qiskit SDK에는 자신의 프로그램에서 빌딩 블록으로 사용할 수 있는, 널리 쓰이는 Circuit들을 모아 놓은 라이브러리가 포함되어 있습니다.
examples.why: 인기 있는 most naturally attaches to 라이브러리, turning 'a library of popular circuits' into 'a popular circuit library'. The next sentence correctly says 인기 있는 Circuit, so the opening reads as a calqued modifier-order slip.

examples.source: You can also use this to assign these parameters to real values using a dictionary of the form { Parameter: number }.
examples.translation: `{ Parameter: number }` 형식의 딕셔너리를 사용하여 이 파라미터들을 실제 값에 할당할 수도 있습니다.
examples.suggested: `{ Parameter: number }` 형식의 딕셔너리를 사용하여 이 파라미터들에 실제 값을 할당할 수도 있습니다.
examples.why: 실제 값에 할당 reverses the assignment direction in Korean (assigning the parameters onto the values); the idiomatic form is 파라미터에 값을 할당하다.

editor_note: Judged only the delta entry (the "Package versions" note): "이 페이지의 코드는 다음 요구 사항을 사용하여 개발되었습니다. 이러한 버전 이상을 사용하는 것을 권장합니다." is faithful — "이러한 버전 이상" correctly carries "these versions or newer" (not "these exact versions"), 요구 사항 is the standard rendering of requirements, and the dropped "we" plus the 합니다체 ending match the file's consistent register elsewhere (e.g. "…전체 과정을 통해 …안내합니다").

The `Store` section inverts the source's core point. English says the $B[0]\oplus B[1]\oplus\ldots$ form (where $B=
eg A$) is preferable and that "the former computes the negation in a single parallel step before the XOR chain", the latter evaluating each negation sequentially. The Korean reverses the order of the two expressions in the comparison sentence ("$(
eg A[0])\oplus\ldots$보다 $B[0]\oplus B[1]\oplus\ldots$로 표현하는 것이 ... 더 효율적입니다") but then keeps 전자/후자 in the English order, so in Korean 전자 now points at the $(
eg A[i])$ form — the text ends up saying the sequential-negation form is the parallelized one, flatly contradicting its own preceding sentence and teaching the learner the wrong rule about `store`. Secondary, non-misleading: "classical" is rendered as both 클래식 (클래식 피드포워드/클래식 비트, most of the file) and 고전적 (고전적 피드포워드, line 40), and the same paragraph block mixes Circuit/회로 and Qubit/qubit; and "lifting ... to a `Value` node" is calqued as "들어올리는 것" rather than a natural 승격/변환.

examples.source: The former computes the negation in a single parallel step before the XOR chain, instead of evaluating each negation sequentially inside the expression.
examples.translation: 전자는 XOR 체인 전에 단일 병렬 단계에서 부정을 계산하는 반면, 후자는 표현식 내에서 각 부정을 순차적으로 평가합니다.
examples.suggested: $B$를 쓰는 쪽은 XOR 체인 전에 한 번의 병렬 단계로 부정을 계산하는 반면, $(\neg A[i])$를 쓰는 쪽은 표현식 안에서 각 부정을 순차적으로 평가합니다.
examples.why: The Korean comparison sentence lists $(\neg A[0])\oplus\ldots$ FIRST and $B[0]\oplus\ldots$ second, so positional 전자 = the (¬A) form. The sentence therefore claims the sequential form is the parallel one and the recommended $B$ form is the sequential one — the exact opposite of the English, and self-contradictory with the immediately preceding '더 효율적입니다' clause. A learner takes away the wrong reason to use `store`.

examples.source: Qiskit supports four control flow constructs for classical feedforward
examples.translation: Qiskit은 고전적 피드포워드를 위한 네 가지 제어 흐름 구문을 지원하며
examples.suggested: Qiskit은 클래식 피드포워드를 위한 네 가지 제어 흐름 구문을 지원하며
examples.why: 'classical' is 클래식 everywhere else in the file (클래식 피드포워드, 클래식 비트, 클래식 레지스터, 클래식 표현식) but 고전적 here; the same block also drops to 회로/qubit while the rest of the file uses Circuit/Qubit. Recognizable, so MINOR, but a native editor would unify it.

examples.source: the first element of the constructed expression involves lifting the Python object `mr[0]` to a `Value` node
examples.translation: 구성된 표현식의 첫 번째 요소는 Python 객체 `mr[0]`을 `Value` 노드로 들어올리는 것입니다
examples.suggested: 구성된 표현식의 첫 번째 요소에서는 Python 객체 `mr[0]`을 `Value` 노드로 승격(lift)합니다
examples.why: 들어올리다 is the physical sense of 'lift'; a Korean quantum/compiler writer would say 승격하다 (or keep lift) for the type-lifting sense. Also '필요한 변환은 이 경우에 자동으로 수행됩니다' reads as a calque of 'in these cases'.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout: the 32자리 기능 코드 / 계정 ID 제출 caveat, the "이 마지막 단계 없이는 Classroom 계정이 활성화되지 않습니다" warning, the credit-card exception clause ("...업그레이드하고... 요금 청구를 받아들일 의사가 있는 경우가 아니라면"), the `physics-101-john-doe` / `open-student-john-doe` prefix example, and the 28일 롤링 윈도우당 10분 QPU quota all match the English exactly, and 해요체 holds consistently. Nothing misleads. Two small naturalness slips a native technical editor would still touch: "세 점 메뉴" (line 78) is a word-for-word calque of "three-dot menu" — Korean UI docs write "점 3개(⋮) 메뉴" or "추가 옵션 메뉴" — and "Account notice를 작성하고" (line 42) uses 작성(write/fill in) for a notice the user only reviews and acknowledges, where 확인/동의 후 would read correctly.

examples.source: On the Users tab, click the three-dot menu at the end of that user's row.
examples.translation: Users 탭에서 해당 사용자 행 끝에 있는 세 점 메뉴를 클릭하세요.
examples.suggested: Users 탭에서 해당 사용자 행 끝에 있는 점 3개(⋮) 메뉴를 클릭하세요.
examples.why: "세 점 메뉴" is a literal calque of the English UI phrase; Korean product docs render this control as "점 3개(⋮) 메뉴" or "추가 옵션 메뉴". Understandable, so not misleading, but it reads as MT.

examples.source: Complete the Account notice and click **Continue**.
examples.translation: Account notice를 작성하고 **Continue**를 클릭하세요.
examples.suggested: Account notice를 확인하고 **Continue**를 클릭하세요.
examples.why: 작성 means "write/fill out", but the Account notice is a disclosure the user reads and acknowledges — 확인(하고) or 검토 후 동의 matches the actual step. Same wording repeats for the Account privacy notice on the next line.

editor_note: Judged entry 39 (the Benchmarks table) only: headers render naturally and correctly as 예제 / 큐비트 수 / 초기화 / 오차 / 총 시간(분) / 런타임 사용량(분), and every datum is preserved exactly (50/70/18 qubits, `PHYSICALLY_INFORMED` vs `RANDOM`, $10^{-2}$, 66→25, 48→34, 123→100), so nothing could mislead a learner; leaving the three row labels (Inviscid Burgers' equation etc.) in English is a defensible kept-term choice for a benchmark table.

No passage teaches a false quantum concept — the physics-bearing prose (phase disk, reduced purity, q-sphere latitudes/Hamming distance, CNOT/Toffoli/Z/H definitions, "up to relative phases" for RCCX) is faithful and reads like a Korean engineer wrote it. What an editor would change: (1) a boundary slip in the sign-in note — EN "more than four qubits" became "4개 이상의 Qubit" (= four or more), which strictly contradicts the preceding "최대 4개" in the same admonition; (2) "operation" is split within the file between 작업 (첫 절반: 작업 카탈로그, 사용자 정의 작업) and 연산 (후반: 사용자 정의 연산, 연산 목록), so cross-reference link text no longer matches its own section titles (link "OpenQASM에서 사용자 정의 작업 만들기" → heading "…사용자 정의 연산 만들기"), and 작업 doubles as "job" in the run section (작업 이름/작업 보기); (3) the hedge in "possibly even the environment" is dropped, so the reduced-purity sentence asserts environment entanglement outright, and "any other party" is calqued as "다른 어떤 파티와도"; (4) UI strings are handled two ways — the two identical EN admonitions render as 편집 메뉴/"시각화 시드" once and Edit 메뉴/"Visualizations seed" the other time, and "회로 실행 및 결과 확인" uses 회로 where every other heading keeps Circuit. Also 기저 상태 carries both "basis state" and "ground state" (line ~411, ~463).

examples.source: If you don’t sign in, the visualizations automatically show simulated results for up to four qubits. … if you want to visualize a circuit that has more than four qubits, you must sign in.
examples.translation: 로그인하지 않으면 시각화는 최대 4개의 Qubit에 대한 시뮬레이션 결과를 자동으로 표시합니다. … 4개 이상의 Qubit을 가진 Circuit을 시각화하려면 반드시 로그인해야 합니다.
examples.suggested: … 4개를 초과하는(5개 이상의) Qubit을 가진 Circuit을 시각화하려면 반드시 로그인해야 합니다.
examples.why: Off-by-one on the boundary: 이상 is inclusive (≥4), so the sentence says a 4-qubit circuit needs sign-in while the sentence just before it says up to 4 works without signing in. Same admonition, self-contradictory.

examples.source: a reduced purity of 0.5 shows that the qubit is left in the completely mixed state, and has some level of entanglement over the remaining N−1 qubits, and possibly even the environment.
examples.translation: 축소 순도가 0.5이면 Qubit이 완전 혼합 상태에 있으며, 나머지 N-1개의 qubit, 그리고 환경과도 어느 정도 얽혀 있음을 나타냅니다.
examples.suggested: … 나머지 N-1개의 qubit, 경우에 따라서는 환경과도 어느 정도 얽혀 있음을 나타냅니다.
examples.why: The hedge "possibly" is dropped, turning a qualified statement into a flat assertion that the qubit is entangled with the environment.

examples.source: operations catalog / custom operation / operations list
examples.translation: 작업 카탈로그, 사용자 정의 작업 (first half) → 사용자 정의 연산, 연산 목록, 컴포저 작업 용어집 (second half)
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering for "operation" (연산 reads better against Gate/Circuit) and reserve 작업 for "job"; then make link text match the section titles.
examples.why: Same concept split 작업/연산 within one file, so in-page links no longer read as the sections they point to (link "…사용자 정의 작업 만들기" vs heading "…사용자 정의 연산 만들기"), and 작업 simultaneously carries "job" in the Run section (작업 이름, 작업 보기, 작업 결과 페이지).

examples.source: the probability that the qubits are not in the ground state |0…0⟩ / the quantum phases with respect to the ground state
examples.translation: 기저 상태 |0...0⟩에 있지 않을 확률 / 기저 상태에 대한 양자 위상
examples.suggested: 바닥 상태 |0...0⟩ … / 바닥 상태에 대한 양자 위상
examples.why: 기저 상태 is already carrying "basis state" throughout the same page (계산 기저 상태, 기저 상태의 위도). Reusing it for "ground state" two paragraphs later makes the reader parse 기저 상태 two ways in one section.

examples.source: You can see the seed number by selecting "Visualizations seed" from the Edit menu. (identical text in both admonitions)
examples.translation: 편집 메뉴에서 "시각화 시드"를 선택하면 … (line 320) / Edit 메뉴에서 "Visualizations seed"를 선택하면 … (line 358)
examples.suggested: Keep the on-screen labels in English in both places (Edit 메뉴 → "Visualizations seed"), as the file already does for Sign in / Save file / Run circuit elsewhere.
examples.why: The same UI string is translated in one admonition and left English in the other; a reader following the translated label will not find 시각화 시드 in the English UI. Same slip at 보기 → 패널 → 코드 편집기 (line 184), **+추가** (282) and 회로 실행 및 결과 확인 (323, 회로 where all other headings keep Circuit).

examples.source: a value of one indicates that the qubit is not entangled with any other party. / Visualizations characterize your circuit as you build it.
examples.translation: 값이 1이면 해당 Qubit이 다른 어떤 파티와도 얽혀 있지 않음을 나타냅니다. / 시각화는 Circuit을 구성하면서 특성을 나타냅니다.
examples.suggested: 값이 1이면 해당 Qubit이 다른 어떤 계(system)와도 얽혀 있지 않음을 나타냅니다. / 시각화는 Circuit을 구성하는 동안 그 특성을 보여줍니다.
examples.why: "파티" is a raw calque of "party" and reads as a social event in Korean; "구성하면서 특성을 나타냅니다" has no clear subject and reads as MT. Neither misleads, but a native technical writer would rewrite both.

editor_note: Faithful paragraph-for-paragraph; the load-bearing role matrix is exact (rules→Administrator on IBM Quantum Compute Service, network zones→"편집자(Editor) 또는 관리자(Administrator)", Viewer limited to "규칙에 네트워크 영역을 추가하는 것만 가능합니다"), the negation "IAM 정책과 달리 컨텍스트 기반 제한은 액세스를 부여하지 않습니다" and the audit-log caveat ("IBM Quantum Compute Service가 아닌 컨텍스트 기반 제한 서비스에서 발생합니다") both survive intact, and terminology (액세스, 자격 증명, 네트워크 영역, 컨텍스트 기반 제한) is conventional IBM-Korean and consistent throughout, in the corpus-standard 합니다체 + -세요 register.

The single delta entry — the page title "Integrate external quantum resources with Qiskit" → "Qiskit으로 외부 양자 리소스 통합하기" — is faithful and idiomatic: the "-하기" nominalized-gerund form is the standard Korean doc-title convention, "외부 양자 리소스" matches the body's usage in 외부 양자 리소스 프로바이더 (line 10), and it matches the identical H1 at line 8 and the frontmatter description, so nothing in the delta misleads.

Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination: the counterfactuals ("예시 플러그인이 설치되어 있다면 …"), the quantities ("최대 3개의 Qubit", "최적화 수준 3"), the `None` caveat ("레이아웃이 아직 결정되지 않았으며 … 물리적 Qubit이 아직 결정되지 않았음"), and the backward-compatibility promise ("기존 플러그인에 변경이 필요하지 않도록 하위 호환성을 유지하는 방식") all match the English, including the last 40%. What an editor would change is consistency: the same concept "transpiler stage" is rendered two ways within the file — "Transpiler 스테이지" (headings, §39, §170) vs "트랜스파일러 단계" (§75, §154) — and the section headings alternate "예시:" (§73) with "예제:" (§191, §344), with the same split in "예시 플러그인" (§168) vs "예제 플러그인" (§339). Register also wobbles: the file is 합니다체 but drops into 해요체 at "살펴봐요" (§71) and into honorific at "생각되신다면" (§282). Finally "the wider Qiskit community" becomes "더 많은 Qiskit 커뮤니티" (§36), which reads as "more Qiskit communities" rather than "the broader community". None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: In this example, we create a transpiler stage plugin for the `layout` stage … See the table of transpiler plugin stages
examples.translation: 이 예제에서는 `layout` 단계를 위한 트랜스파일러 단계 플러그인을 생성합니다 … [트랜스파일러 단계 표]
examples.suggested: Transpiler 스테이지 플러그인 / Transpiler 스테이지 (match the headings at §73 and the body at §39, §170)
examples.why: The same concept appears as both 'Transpiler 스테이지' and '트랜스파일러 단계' within one file; the concept stays identifiable, so this is a consistency slip, not a misleading term.

examples.source: a great way to share your transpilation code with the wider Qiskit community
examples.translation: 여러분의 트랜스파일 코드를 더 많은 Qiskit 커뮤니티와 공유하는 좋은 방법
examples.suggested: 더 넓은 Qiskit 커뮤니티와 공유하는 좋은 방법
examples.why: '더 많은 Qiskit 커뮤니티' parses as 'more Qiskit communities' (plural count) rather than 'the wider community'; a native technical writer would use 더 넓은.

examples.source: If you find that the inputs available to the `run` method are insufficient … / In the next sections, we show examples of these steps
examples.translation: 입력이 목적에 충분하지 않다고 생각되신다면 … / 다음 섹션에서는 … 살펴봐요.
examples.suggested: 충분하지 않다면 … / 살펴봅니다 (or hold 해요체 consistently)
examples.why: The file is otherwise uniform 합니다체; '생각되신다면' is an honorific slip and '살펴봐요' an isolated 해요체 slip, so neither convention is held cleanly.

examples.source: ## Example: Create a transpiler stage plugin / ## Example: Create a unitary synthesis plugin
examples.translation: ## 예시: Transpiler 스테이지 플러그인 만들기 / ## 예제: 유니터리 합성 플러그인 만들기
examples.suggested: Use one of 예시 or 예제 across all three section headings and the follow-up sentences (예시 플러그인 §168 vs 예제 플러그인 §339)
examples.why: Parallel headings for the three plugin types should read identically; the alternation is visible to any reader scanning the page.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, no hallucinated sentences; the arrow/CZ vs. inter-chip CX explanation (회색 화살표는 CZ Gate이고 검은색 화살표는 칩 간 CX Gate입니다 … Qubit $6 \rightarrow 21$ 및 $25 \rightarrow 40$) and the SWAP-insertion rationale both survive intact, and register is consistently 합니다체 with no 하십시오/드리 honorific slips. Three editor-level slips remain. (1) The core verb is rendered two ways in the same file: 트랜스파일 in the frontmatter/title and the first two paragraphs, then English "Transpile하기 / Transpile하는 것은 간단합니다 / Transpile된 Circuit" from the H2 onward — the concept stays identifiable, so MINOR, but a native editor would unify it. (2) In the "Create unique backends" paragraph "a large library of different graphs" is mis-parsed as 다양한 그래프 라이브러리 ("various graph libraries"), which reverses head and modifier and drops "large" — rustworkx is one library containing many graphs, not a bundle of graph libraries. (3) The disjoint-lattice sentence 이 Backend의 기저 Gate는 내부 벌크와 엣지가 서로 다릅니다 double-marks subjects (…는 …가) and reads stiffly; something like 벌크 내부와 엣지에서 기저 Gate가 서로 다릅니다 is what a Korean engineer would write.

examples.source: transpile / transpiled circuit
examples.translation: 트랜스파일하는 방법 … 트랜스파일할 수 있습니다 (l.46, 48) vs. 커스텀 Backend에 대해 Transpile하기 … Transpile된 Circuit에는 (l.289, 291, 334)
examples.suggested: Pick one and use it everywhere: 트랜스파일 (matching the title/sidebar_label) — 커스텀 Backend에 맞춰 트랜스파일하기 … 트랜스파일된 Circuit에는
examples.why: The same operation appears both transliterated and in English within one page, including in the H2 that the title already renders as 트랜스파일; harmless to comprehension but inconsistent.

examples.source: The rustworkx package contains a large library of different graphs and enables the creation of custom graphs.
examples.translation: [rustworkx](https://www.rustworkx.org/) 패키지에는 다양한 그래프 라이브러리가 포함되어 있으며, 커스텀 그래프를 생성할 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: rustworkx 패키지는 다양한 그래프를 담은 방대한 라이브러리를 제공하며, 커스텀 그래프도 직접 만들 수 있습니다.
examples.why: "a large library of different graphs" became "various graph libraries" — head and modifier are swapped and "large" is dropped, so the reader is told rustworkx bundles several graph libraries rather than that it ships a big catalogue of graph generators.

examples.source: The example below covers a backend with a disjoint qubit lattice, whose basis gates are different along the edges from within the bulk.
examples.translation: 아래 예제는 분리된 qubit 격자를 가진 Backend를 다루며, 이 Backend의 기저 Gate는 내부 벌크와 엣지가 서로 다릅니다.
examples.suggested: 아래 예제는 분리된 Qubit 격자를 가진 Backend를 다룹니다. 이 Backend에서는 벌크 내부와 엣지에서 기저 Gate가 서로 다릅니다.
examples.why: Double subject marking (기저 Gate는 … 엣지가 서로 다릅니다) leaves the comparison grammatically dangling; a Korean technical writer would make 기저 Gate the thing that differs and 벌크/엣지 the locations.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the twirling logic ("두 qubit Gate *이전*(왼쪽)에 적용되는 것들이 ... *이후*(오른쪽)에 적용되는 것들에 의해 상쇄되도록 선택됩니다"), the Analysis-vs-Transformation pass asymmetry (DAG 수정 불가 / property_set 수정 가능 vs. 읽기만 가능), and the mini-DAG apply_operation_back/front contrast all survive intact, and no hallucinated claim appears. Three things a native editor would change. (1) The DAG-background setup sentence of the English ("This example illustrates the DAG by creating a simple circuit that prepares a Bell state and applies an $R_Z$ rotation, depending on the measurement outcome.") is gone; in its place the DAG_circ image is emitted twice — once with a Korean caption, once with the untranslated English caption — so the reader gets a duplicated figure instead of the framing sentence (the information does survive in the Korean caption, hence not misleading). (2) "coherent errors" is rendered "일관된 오류" rather than the conventional 결맞음/코히런트 오류 — recognizable as "systematic error" but not the field's term. (3) The central term is spelled four ways in one file: 트랜스파일러 패스, Transpiler 패스, 트랜스파일레이션, Transpilation; "custom" likewise splits 사용자 정의 패스 / 커스텀 패스 and "noise" splits 노이즈 / 잡음. Register is the standard 합니다체 with 하세요 imperatives, but the opening paragraph slips into the humble 드리다 form ("보여드리며").

examples.source: This example illustrates the DAG by creating a simple circuit that prepares a Bell state and applies an $R_Z$ rotation, depending on the measurement outcome.
examples.translation: (sentence absent; the DAG_circ image appears twice instead — once captioned "Bell 상태를 준비하고 측정 결과에 따라 $R_Z$ 회전을 적용하는 Circuit.", once with the original English caption)
examples.suggested: 이 예제에서는 Bell 상태를 준비하고 측정 결과에 따라 $R_Z$ 회전을 적용하는 간단한 Circuit을 만들어 DAG를 설명합니다.
examples.why: The paragraph that introduces the worked example is missing, and the figure is duplicated in its place. The content is recoverable from the caption, so this is a structural/completeness slip rather than a misleading one, but a reader loses the explicit 'this is what the example does' framing before the code cell.

examples.source: One benefit of Pauli twirling is that it turns coherent errors into stochastic errors, which can be improved by averaging more.
examples.translation: Pauli 트월링의 한 가지 이점은 일관된 오류를 확률적 오류로 변환한다는 것이며, 이는 더 많은 평균화를 통해 개선될 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: ... 결맞음 오류(coherent error)를 확률적 오류로 변환한다는 것이며 ...
examples.why: '일관된 오류' reads as 'consistent error'. The intuition (systematic vs. random) is close enough not to teach a false concept, but 결맞음/코히런트 오류 is the established Korean rendering and the one a reader will meet elsewhere in error-suppression material.

examples.source: transpilation pass / transpiler pass / custom pass
examples.translation: 트랜스파일 패스 · 트랜스파일러 패스 (l.33), 트랜스파일레이션 단계 (l.45), Transpiler 패스 (l.80/82), 커스텀 패스 (l.201), Transpilation 기본 설정 (l.229)
examples.suggested: Pick one surface form (e.g. Transpiler 패스 / 트랜스파일 / 사용자 정의 패스) and hold it for the whole page.
examples.why: The page's central term appears in four spellings and 'custom' in two (사용자 정의 / 커스텀); 'noise' likewise splits 노이즈가 있는 양자 게이트 (l.33) vs 잡음 채널 (l.86). Each is identifiable on its own, so this is polish, not a comprehension risk.

examples.source: Here we will demonstrate how to write a transpiler pass, focusing on building a pass that performs Pauli twirling...
examples.translation: 여기서는 트랜스파일러 패스를 작성하는 방법을 보여드리며, ...
examples.suggested: 여기서는 트랜스파일러 패스를 작성하는 방법을 살펴보고, ...
examples.why: '보여드리며' is the humble 드리다 form, which the locale convention excludes; the rest of the file stays in plain 합니다체 with 하세요 imperatives, so this one clause reads out of key.

examples.source: Passes in general work with the DAG and the property_set, a dictionary-like object for storing properties determined by analysis passes.
examples.translation: 패스는 일반적으로 [DAG]와 분석 패스에 의해 결정된 속성을 저장하는 딕셔너리 유사 객체인 `property_set`으로 작동합니다.
examples.suggested: 패스는 일반적으로 DAG와 `property_set`을 다룹니다. `property_set`은 분석 패스가 결정한 속성을 저장하는 딕셔너리 형태의 객체입니다.
examples.why: '~으로 작동합니다' is a direct calque of 'work with' (Korean 작동하다 takes the pass as subject, not its inputs as instrument), and the long pre-nominal relative clause stacked before `property_set` forces a re-read. Splitting the apposition into a second sentence is what a Korean technical writer would do.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat: the approximation-degree poles (1.0 = 근사 없음, 0.0 = 최대 근사), the `None` → 보고된 오류율 fallback, the alap/asap definitions and "이것이 기본값입니다", and the granularity/min_length/pulse_alignment 배수 constraints all match the English exactly. What a native editor would change is phrasing, not content. (1) In the "Transpiler 동작 방식에 영향을 미치는 매개변수" intro, "해당 값이 변경할 수 있는 모든 패스를 재정의합니다" leaves the relative clause without an object, so it can be misparsed as "passes that the value could change" instead of EN's "the passes that could change it" — "해당 값을 변경할 수 있는 모든 패스보다 우선합니다" is the natural rendering. (2) "매개변수는 두 가지 클래스로 나뉩니다" is a calque of "two classes of arguments"; Korean technical writing would use 두 부류/두 종류 — "클래스" also collides with the Python class sense used a few lines later (`HLSConfig` 구성 클래스). (3) The transpiler term is split within the file between "Transpiler" (Transpiler의 역할, Transpiler 단계), "트랜스파일러" (backend/target/seed_transpiler bullets) and the verb 트랜스파일; the concept stays identifiable, so this is cosmetic, and the capitalized-English half is the deterministic sweep's business. Register (합니다체 declaratives + ~하세요 imperatives) is consistent and appropriate for the corpus.

examples.source: If you specify an argument, such as `initial_layout` for the qubits you want to use, that value overrides all the passes that could change it.
examples.translation: 사용하려는 Qubit에 대한 `initial_layout`과 같이 인수를 지정하면 해당 값이 변경할 수 있는 모든 패스를 재정의합니다.
examples.suggested: 사용하려는 Qubit을 지정하는 `initial_layout`처럼 인수를 직접 지정하면, 그 값은 이를 변경할 수 있는 모든 패스보다 우선합니다.
examples.why: The relative clause has no object marker, so "해당 값이 변경할 수 있는 모든 패스" reads as "passes the value can change" — the inverse of the English relation. The next sentence rescues it, so it is stiff/ambiguous rather than misleading.

examples.source: There are two classes of arguments: those that describe the target of compilation, and those that influence how the transpiler works.
examples.translation: 매개변수는 두 가지 클래스로 나뉩니다: 컴파일 대상을 설명하는 것과 Transpiler의 동작 방식에 영향을 미치는 것입니다.
examples.suggested: 인수는 두 부류로 나뉩니다. 컴파일 대상을 설명하는 인수와 Transpiler의 동작 방식에 영향을 미치는 인수입니다.
examples.why: "클래스" is a direct calque of "classes" and clashes with the programming sense of 클래스 used later (구성 클래스 `HLSConfig`); 부류/종류 is the term a Korean technical writer would use here.

examples.source: transpiler
examples.translation: Transpiler의 역할은 … / 트랜스파일러는 입력 Circuit을 … / 트랜스파일러의 확률적 부분에 대한 랜덤 시드
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering (either Transpiler or 트랜스파일러) and use it for every occurrence.
examples.why: The same term appears in two forms inside one file; the concept stays identifiable so this is cosmetic, and the capitalized-English variant belongs to the deterministic leak sweep.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — every claim I checked survives intact (ZNE "not guaranteed to produce an unbiased result" → "편향되지 않은 결과를 보장하지는 않습니다"; PEC "Unlike ZNE, it returns an unbiased estimate … generally incurs a greater overhead"; the γ ≥ 1 sampling-overhead paragraph, the 3x default-noise-factor overhead, the "might not improve … could even worsen performance" caveat on densely packed circuits, and the three PEA stages). Two domain terms are imperfect but consistent: "coherent errors/noise" is rendered "일관성 오류 / 일관성 노이즈" (reads as "consistency", where the field uses 결맞음/코히런트), and "observable" is rendered "관측값" ("observed value") rather than 관측가능량/옵저버블, so "관측값의 기댓값" reads as "expectation value of the measured value". In the ZNE paragraph, "equivalent sequences of the gate and its inverse" becomes "Gate와 그 역행렬의 동일한 시퀀스" — "동일한" (identical) instead of 등가, and 역행렬 (inverse matrix) where 역연산/역Gate is meant; the $UU^\dagger U$ example keeps this from misleading. Remaining nits are stiffness: the opening sentence uses 실행 twice ("…실행되는 마이크로파 펄스 시퀀스로 실행됩니다"), and "…에만 독점적으로 적용됩니다" doubles the exclusivity. Register (‑습니다 declaratives with 해요체 imperatives like 참조하세요) is consistent, with no 하십시오체/드리 slips.

examples.source: unwanted interactions between qubits can lead to coherent errors on idling qubits … it can mitigate coherent noise because coherent noise tends to accumulate quadratically
examples.translation: 유휴 Qubit에 일관성 오류가 발생할 수 있습니다 … 일관성 노이즈를 완화할 수 있습니다
examples.suggested: 결맞음(코히런트) 오류 / 코히런트 노이즈
examples.why: ‘일관성’ reads as ‘consistency’ in Korean; the established quantum term for coherent is 결맞음/코히런트. Used consistently, so recognizable — MINOR, not misleading.

examples.source: mitigates the effect of measurement errors for the estimation of Pauli observable expectation values … estimating expectation values of observables
examples.translation: 파울리 관측값 기댓값 추정에서 … 관측값의 기댓값을 추정할 때
examples.suggested: 파울리 관측가능량(옵저버블)의 기댓값 … 관측가능량의 기댓값
examples.why: ‘관측값’ names the measured value, not the observable operator, so ‘관측값의 기댓값’ collapses two distinct notions into one word.

examples.source: two-qubit gates are replaced with equivalent sequences of the gate and its inverse
examples.translation: 2-Qubit Gate가 Gate와 그 역행렬의 동일한 시퀀스로 대체됨을 의미합니다
examples.suggested: 2-Qubit Gate가 해당 Gate와 그 역연산으로 이루어진 등가 시퀀스로 대체됨을 의미합니다
examples.why: ‘동일한’ says ‘identical’ where the source says ‘equivalent’, and ‘역행렬’ (inverse matrix) is used for a gate’s inverse operation; the $UU^\dagger U$ example still makes the mechanism clear.

examples.source: Quantum circuits are executed on IBM hardware as sequences of microwave pulses that need to be scheduled and run at precise time intervals.
examples.translation: 양자 Circuit은 IBM 하드웨어에서 정밀한 시간 간격으로 스케줄링되어 실행되는 마이크로파 펄스 시퀀스로 실행됩니다.
examples.suggested: 양자 Circuit은 IBM 하드웨어에서 마이크로파 펄스 시퀀스로 실행되며, 이 펄스들은 정밀한 시간 간격에 맞춰 스케줄링되어야 합니다.
examples.why: ‘실행되는 … 시퀀스로 실행됩니다’ repeats 실행 in one clause — a native technical writer would split the relative clause.

examples.source: this technique is often applied exclusively to (native) two-qubit gates … The overhead of this method scales with the number of noise factors … It scales quadratically with γ
examples.translation: 2-Qubit Gate에만 독점적으로 적용됩니다 … 노이즈 계수의 수에 따라 확장됩니다 … 이차적으로 확장되며
examples.suggested: (기본) 2-Qubit Gate에만 적용됩니다 … 노이즈 계수의 수에 비례하여 증가합니다 … γ에 대해 이차적으로 증가하며
examples.why: ‘…에만 독점적으로’ doubles the exclusivity marker, and ‘확장되다’ is a calque of ‘scale’; Korean technical prose uses 증가하다 for a growing overhead.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — every quantity and condition survives intact (2s per-sub-job overhead, 250마이크로초 default rep_delay, "측정은 x Gate보다 56배 더 오래 걸릴 수 있습니다", the zero-usage-on-system-error vs. usage-up-to-that-point split, and the session wall-clock rule); no drift, dropped caveat, or hallucinated claim, and the informal 해요체 imperatives (참조하세요/알아보세요) hold. Three things a native technical editor would still change: "observable" is rendered 관측값 ("observed value") in "qubit 단위로 교환 가능한 관측값을 그룹화" (line 75), where the domain term is 관측 가능량 / 옵저버블 — the operator, not the measured value; "the last 28 full days" is calqued as "최근 28 전체 일" (line 57), which no Korean writer would produce (지난 28일 전체); and "learn how to transpile locally" becomes the noun-form "로컬 Transpiler 방법을 알아보세요" (line 119) instead of the verbal 로컬에서 트랜스파일하는 방법. None of these mislead — 교환 가능한 only applies to operators, so the learner recovers the concept from context.

examples.source: Estimator groups qubit-wise commuting observables, which reduces the number of executions.
examples.translation: Estimator는 qubit 단위로 교환 가능한 관측값을 그룹화하여 실행 횟수를 줄입니다.
examples.suggested: Estimator는 큐비트 단위로 교환 가능한 관측 가능량(옵저버블)을 그룹화하여 실행 횟수를 줄입니다.
examples.why: 'observable' is the Hermitian operator, conventionally 관측 가능량 or 옵저버블 in Korean quantum docs; 관측값 names the measurement outcome instead. Recoverable from '교환 가능한' (only operators commute), so MINOR rather than FAIL.

examples.source: The Analytics page usage is re-calculated hourly and includes the last 28 full days
examples.translation: 분석 페이지의 사용량은 매 시간 다시 계산되며 최근 28 전체 일을 포함합니다.
examples.suggested: 분석 페이지의 사용량은 매시간 다시 계산되며 지난 28일 전체를 포함합니다.
examples.why: '28 전체 일' is a word-order calque of 'full days'; Korean puts the totality quantifier after the counted unit (28일 전체). Meaning is intact but the phrase reads as machine output.

examples.source: Learn how to transpile locally in the Transpile section.
examples.translation: [Transpile](/guides/transpile/) 섹션에서 로컬 Transpiler 방법을 알아보세요.
examples.suggested: [Transpile](/guides/transpile/) 섹션에서 로컬에서 트랜스파일하는 방법을 알아보세요.
examples.why: The English verb 'transpile' is turned into the tool noun 'Transpiler', so the sentence reads as 'the local transpiler method' rather than 'how to transpile locally'; the adjacent bullet correctly uses Transpiler for the tool's settings, making the noun reuse here read inconsistently.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination anywhere: every claim matches the English, including the tricky ones ("Estimator는 관리형 서비스이므로, 먼저 계정을 초기화해야 합니다", the PUB definition "하나의 Circuit과 해당 Circuit에 브로드캐스트되는 데이터(여러 observable 및 파라미터 포함)를 담은 튜플", the two-part quantum-preprocessing/classical-postprocessing overhead sentence, and the caveat "Open Plan 사용자는 Session 작업을 제출할 수 없습니다"). Core terms are right — expectation value→기댓값, transpile→트랜스파일, error mitigation→오류 완화 — and 해요체 holds throughout with no 하십시오체/드리 slips. What an editor would still change: "parameter" is split within the file between 파라미터 (PUB admonition) and 매개변수 (headings "2. 매개변수 정의", "매개변수화된 Circuit"); the "topic" link label is calqued as "이 [주제](/guides/cloud-setup-rest-api)를 참조하세요" and "이 주제의 단계에서는 … 시연합니다", where a Korean technical writer would write 이 문서/페이지 and 보여줍니다; and the two option headings are inconsistently handled — "동적 디커플링" is translated but the sibling "Twirling" is left in English even though the body text right above renders it as "트월링(twirling)". None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: …the data broadcasted to that circuit, which can be multiple observables and parameters. / ### 2. Define parameters / ## Parameterized circuits
examples.translation: …여러 observable 및 파라미터 포함) / ### 2. 매개변수 정의 / ## 매개변수화된 Circuit
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering for "parameter" and use it everywhere — either 파라미터 throughout, or 매개변수 throughout (matching the headings).
examples.why: The same concept appears as 파라미터 in the PUB admonition and 매개변수 in the section headings that explain exactly that parameter, so a reader cannot tell the two are the same thing. Concept still identifiable, so MINOR.

examples.source: The steps in this topic describe how to run and configure workloads with the REST API, and demonstrate how to invoke them… / Find details … in this [topic].
examples.translation: 이 주제의 단계에서는 REST API를 사용하여 워크로드를 실행하고 구성하는 방법을 설명하며, 원하는 프로그램에서 이를 호출하는 방법을 시연합니다. / …자세한 내용은 이 [주제]를 참조하세요.
examples.suggested: 이 문서에서는 REST API로 워크로드를 실행하고 구성하는 방법을 설명하고, 원하는 프로그램에서 이를 호출하는 방법을 보여줍니다. / …자세한 내용은 이 [페이지]를 참조하세요.
examples.why: "주제" is a literal calque of the IBM authoring word "topic"; Korean docs call a documentation page 문서/페이지. "시연합니다" (a demo/performance verb) is stiff for prose that just shows code. Grammatical but reads as translated English.

examples.source: ### Dynamical Decoupling / ### Twirling
examples.translation: ### 동적 디커플링 / ### Twirling
examples.suggested: Render both headings the same way, e.g. "동적 디커플링" and "트월링" (or leave both in English), matching the body line 다음 예시는 동적 디커플링(dynamical decoupling), 트월링(twirling)…
examples.why: The intro paragraph already establishes 트월링 as the Korean rendering, but the section heading immediately below reverts to bare English while its sibling heading is translated — an internal inconsistency a native editor would smooth out.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — every load-bearing number and condition survives intact (32비트 이하 operand rule, 60비트→약 300 vs 1비트→2400 브로드캐스트, the "c0의 내용이 변경되지 않아" one-broadcast explanation, and the **포함하지 않습니다** / `job.result()[0].data.temp`는 `0` caveat in the Store note), and no hallucinated sentence appears. The defects are terminological, not semantic. "dynamic decoupling" is rendered "동적 분리" (literally "dynamic separation"); the field says 동적 디커플링 / 동적 결합 해제, and 분리 does not name the error-suppression technique the linked stretch guide is about. "terminal measurements" becomes "터미널 측정", a transliteration that in Korean reads as bus/computer terminal — the parenthetical gloss "Circuit 끝에서 수행되는 측정" rescues it, so it misleads no one, but a native editor would write 종단 측정. Step 1 of the Estimator recipe renders "the terms of all observables" as "모든 Observable의 항목" (항목 = item/entry) where the Pauli-decomposition sense needs 항. Finally the file splits the same concept two ways: Circuit is kept in English almost everywhere yet appears as 회로 inside "중간 회로 측정" and "회로 깊이" — defensible for the fixed compound, but inconsistent as written.

examples.suggested: [stretch](/guides/stretch)를 사용하여 정확한 동적 디커플링을 구현하는 방법을 알아보세요.
examples.why: '동적 분리' reads as 'dynamic separation' and is not the established Korean name for dynamical decoupling (동적 디커플링 / 동적 결합 해제). The reader can still follow the link, so it is imperfect-but-recoverable rather than a false concept, but it is the weakest term in the file. 'stretch' is also a Qiskit API keyword and is better left unromanized.

editor_note: Meaning is substantially faithful and the core scheduler concepts (공정 분배 스케줄러, 인스턴스, 할당량 대비 사용량, 선입선출(FIFO)) are correct and consistent, but two quantifiers are loosened relative to the English. The intro's categorical "it is generally impossible to guarantee when a workload will be executed" is downgraded to "일반적으로 보장하기 어렵습니다" ("generally difficult to guarantee"), which leaves room for the reader to think a guarantee is sometimes obtainable; and "If the selected instance has submitted more than one workload" becomes "하나 이상의 워크로드를 제출한 경우", which in Korean reads as "one or more" (≥1) rather than "more than one" (≥2). Neither teaches a false concept about how the scheduler works, so this stays MINOR. Separately, "window" is rendered by the calque 창 throughout (시간 창 / 28일 롤링 창 / 스케줄링 창) where Korean technical docs normally use 윈도우 or 기간, and "twice the number of minutes" surfaces as the bare "두 배의 분(minute)" instead of 할당 시간(분).

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the angle constraint ($0 \lt \theta \leq \pi/2$, FoldRzzAngle, parameterized-RZZ job failure), the "error value is just a copy of the non-fractional counterpart" caveat, and the unsupported-technique list (Pauli twirling unsupported / TREX measurement twirling *supported*) all survive intact, and the final "Which backends…" section keeps the fake-backend default-disabled nuance. The real defects are terminological: the Qiskit domain term "primitive options" is rendered "기본 옵션" ("basic/default options"), which loses the Sampler/Estimator primitive referent — the conventional Korean is "프리미티브 옵션"; and "ansatz" is split within the file between "변분 ansatz" (line 47) and "변분 안자츠" (line 201). Additionally the standalone word "Example:" (line 224) was left untranslated where "예시:" belongs, and "the non-fractional gate's counterpart" is calqued as "비분수 Gate의 상대 항목", which no Korean technical writer would say (natural: "대응하는 비분수 Gate의 값"). Register is consistently 합니다체/해요체 with no 하십시오체 or 드리 slips.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the technically load-bearing passages (the 26.8M control-system-instructions-per-qubit limit "PUB당이 아니라 작업당으로 적용되는", the 1000-randomization → 11 PUB × 1000 = ~11,000 circuit-instance arithmetic, "제공된 딕셔너리는 병합되지 않고 기본값을 완전히 대체합니다", and the segment/ansatz_steps compression plan) all survive intact, and no claim is inverted, softened, or invented. The defects are editorial. The worst is in the Overview: the English relative clause "see [the tutorial], which calls this function to compute the dynamical structure factor of KCuF3" was split into a standalone sentence whose subject is "이 노트북은", immediately followed by "이 노트북은 대신 배포와 입력 계약을 다룹니다" — two consecutive sentences with the same deictic subject making contradictory claims, so the referent has to be guessed. Terminology also splits within the file: "observable" is kept in English everywhere (개요, `t_steps`/`observables` table rows) except line ~347 where it becomes "관측값" (an observed value, not an observable); "randomization" alternates 랜덤화 (~341) / 무작위화 (~347); "circuit" alternates Circuit / 회로 (~347); "dynamical decoupling" is 동적 디커플링 at ~335/343 but left untranslated at ~352.

As written the same phrase makes two contradictory claims one after the other, so a reader can come away thinking this notebook is the one that computes KCuF3's dynamical structure factor. editor_note: Meaning is faithful end-to-end — no inverted conditions, swapped quantities, softened claims or hallucinations; the AQC section (L185) reproduces the target-state → fewer-Trotter-step ansatz → iterative approach → recombination chain exactly, and core terms are correct and consistent (기댓값, 해밀토니안, 종료 충실도(stopping fidelity), 행렬 곱 상태(matrix product state), 트랜스파일, ansatz/observable kept in English). Three editorial slips: (1) "addon" is Koreanized as 애드온 in the opening sentence (L15) but left as English "addon" in every later mention (L21, L27, L35, L765) — a within-file inconsistency; (2) L37 renders "view it locally in a notebook editor" as "로컬로 실행하면" (run it locally), shifting view→execute where the point is merely seeing the %%writefile cells; (3) "iterative component of AQC-Tensor" is calqued as "반복 구성 요소" (L137, L539), stiff phrasing a native writer would render 반복 최적화 과정. None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.translation: …[AQC-Tensor] Qiskit 애드온을 사용하여… (L15) vs …AQC addon 옵션 사양… (L21), AQC addon에서 생성된 Circuit… (L27)

editor_note: The prose is fluent, idiomatic Korean and faithful throughout the second half (job statuses, runtime_jobs/runtime_sessions caveat, filtered_logs include/exclude, catalog.jobs filters are all exact). Three things a native technical editor would change. (1) Two whole paragraphs are left in English — the `save_account()` "If you are working in a trusted Python environment…" block and the "Avoid executing code on an untrusted machine…" security paragraph — so the file's two most safety-relevant instructions are untranslated while everything around them is Korean. (2) In the `run()` tip, English distinguishes "out of capacity" (raises an error) from "capacity is low" (emits a warning), but both are rendered "용량이 부족" ("인스턴스의 용량이 부족하거나 … 즉시 오류를 발생시킵니다. 용량이 부족할 때는 … 경고를 발생시킵니다"), so the same stated condition appears to produce both an error and a warning; the second should be 용량이 얼마 남지 않았을 때 / 잔여 용량이 적을 때. (3) "observable backpropagation" is "관측값 역전파" — 관측값 is the measured value, whereas the Qiskit term is the operator (관측가능량/옵저버블); recognizable in context but not the conventional rendering.

examples.source: If your instance is out of capacity, or the backend you named is not accessible, run() raises an error right away… When capacity is low, run() emits a warning.
examples.translation: 인스턴스의 용량이 부족하거나 지정한 백엔드에 접근할 수 없는 경우, run()은 … 즉시 오류를 발생시킵니다. 용량이 부족할 때는 run()이 경고를 발생시킵니다.

examples.why: "out of capacity" (error) and "capacity is low" (warning) are collapsed into the identical phrase 용량이 부족, so the two branches read as the same condition producing contradictory behavior.
