editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every table cell tracks the English, including the tricky "respectively" pairing in the HI-VQE row (수렴 속도↔슈퍼컴퓨터 고전 솔루션, 정확도↔표준 SQD) and the Q-CTRL "any order / up to maximum device scale" qualifiers. What a native editor would change is wording, not meaning. "Zero Noise Extrapolation" is rendered 영점 잡음 외삽, which reads as "zero-POINT noise" (영점 = zero-point, as in 영점 에너지) rather than "extrapolation to zero noise"; the parenthetical (ZNE) keeps the learner oriented, so it is imperfect-but-recognizable, not false. Two calques flatten the English: "comparable to or exceeding" becomes 비교하거나 이를 초과하는 정확도, where 비교하다 ("to compare") is the wrong verb for "comparable" (필적하거나 능가하는 is the natural rendering), and the application-function audience cell ends on a dangling head noun — 비양자 분야의 연구자로, … 양자를 통합하는 분야 — so the sentence closes on 분야 ("field") where the referent should still be 연구자. The Q-CTRL Optimization Solver row also drops the "abstracts away complexity" clause outright, and 라이센스 should be 라이선스 by standard orthography.

examples.source: standard error mitigation baselines such as Zero Noise Extrapolation (ZNE) and Probabilistic Error Cancellation (PEC)
examples.translation: 영점 잡음 외삽(ZNE) 및 확률적 오류 상쇄(PEC)와 같은 표준 오류 완화 기준선
examples.suggested: 영잡음 외삽(ZNE) 및 확률적 오류 상쇄(PEC)와 같은 표준 오류 완화 기준선
examples.why: 영점 is the established Korean for "zero-point" (영점 에너지 = zero-point energy), so 영점 잡음 reads as a kind of noise rather than as extrapolating the noise TO zero. 영잡음 외삽 (or 제로 노이즈 외삽) is the conventional rendering. Recognizable thanks to the (ZNE) gloss, hence minor.

examples.source: Delivers accuracy comparable to or exceeding classical models such as Random Forest or XGBoost
examples.translation: Random Forest나 XGBoost와 같은 고전적 모델과 비교하거나 이를 초과하는 정확도를 제공하면서
examples.why: 비교하다 means "to compare (something with something)", not "to be comparable to"; the clause literally says the accuracy "compares or exceeds" the models. A Korean technical writer would write 필적하거나 능가하는.
examples.suggested: Random Forest나 XGBoost와 같은 고전적 모델에 필적하거나 이를 능가하는 정확도를 제공하면서

examples.source: Researchers in non-quantum domains, integrating quantum into existing large-scale classical workflows, without needing to map classical data to quantum circuits.
examples.translation: 비양자 분야의 연구자로, 고전적 데이터를 양자 Circuit에 매핑할 필요 없이 기존 대규모 고전적 워크플로우에 양자를 통합하는 분야.
examples.why: The cell answers "Who is it for?", so the head noun must stay 연구자; ending on 통합하는 분야 makes the final referent a "field", leaving 연구자로 dangling. Calqued appositive syntax a native writer would not produce.
examples.suggested: 고전적 데이터를 양자 Circuit에 매핑할 필요 없이, 기존 대규모 고전적 워크플로우에 양자를 통합하려는 비양자 분야의 연구자.

examples.source: It abstracts away complexity by handling error suppression, efficient mapping, and hybrid quantum-classical optimization to solve optimization tasks at full device scale without deep quantum expertise.
examples.translation: 오류 억제, 효율적 매핑, 하이브리드 양자-고전적 최적화를 처리하여 심층적인 양자 전문 지식 없이 전체 디바이스 규모에서 최적화 작업을 해결합니다.
examples.why: The main clause "abstracts away complexity" is dropped — abstraction is the whole selling point of Qiskit Functions and is stated in the intro (추상화하여), so losing it here weakens the emphasis rather than changing the facts. Dropped qualifier, not misleading.
examples.suggested: 오류 억제, 효율적 매핑, 하이브리드 양자-고전적 최적화를 대신 처리하여 복잡성을 추상화하고, 심층적인 양자 전문 지식 없이 전체 디바이스 규모에서 최적화 작업을 해결합니다.

examples.source: License
examples.translation: 라이센스
examples.suggested: 라이선스
examples.why: Standard Korean orthography for "license" is 라이선스; 라이센스 is a common but non-standard spelling, repeated in every table row.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat: the mode→execution-mode mapping ("각각 배치, 세션, Job 실행 모드에 대해 `batch`, `session`, 또는 `backend` 객체") keeps the "respectively" alignment intact, the Open Plan restriction and the "실험적 기능으로 향후 변경될 수 있습니다" caveat both survive, and ISA is correctly unpacked as "명령 집합 아키텍처(ISA)". Two things a native technical editor would still change: (1) "dynamical decoupling" is rendered "동적 분리" (literally "dynamic separation"), whereas the settled Korean-field term is "동적 디커플링"/"동역학적 디커플링" — recognizable in context beside Pauli 트월링/ZNE/PEA/PEC, but a learner searching the term would not find it; (2) the intro sentence "이 주제의 단계는 … 설명합니다" is a word-order calque of "The steps in this topic describe …" — Korean docs open with "이 문서에서는 …하는 방법을 설명합니다". Register convention holds cleanly (해요체 imperatives 따르세요/참조하세요/알아보세요, no 하십시오체 or 드리-), and 기댓값 / Observable / Circuit / 트랜스파일러 are used consistently.

examples.source: including dynamical decoupling, Pauli-twirling, gate-folding ZNE, PEA, and PEC
examples.translation: 동적 분리, Pauli 트월링, 게이트 폴딩 ZNE, PEA, PEC를 포함한
examples.suggested: 동적 디커플링(dynamical decoupling), Pauli 트월링, 게이트 폴딩 ZNE, PEA, PEC를 포함한
examples.why: "동적 분리" reads as "dynamic separation" and is not the term the Korean quantum-error-mitigation literature uses; the established rendering is 동적 디커플링 / 동역학적 디커플링. Recognizable from the surrounding list, so not misleading, but it breaks searchability and sits oddly next to the transliterated 트월링 in the same enumeration.

examples.source: The steps in this topic describe how to set up Estimator, explore the options you can use to configure it, and invoke it in a program.
examples.translation: 이 주제의 단계는 Estimator를 설정하고, 구성에 사용할 수 있는 옵션을 탐색하고, 프로그램에서 호출하는 방법을 설명합니다.
examples.suggested: 이 문서에서는 Estimator를 설정하고, 구성에 사용할 수 있는 옵션을 살펴보고, 프로그램에서 호출하는 방법을 설명합니다.
examples.why: "이 주제의 단계는 … 설명합니다" transplants the English subject ("The steps in this topic") into Korean, where an inanimate "단계" as the subject of 설명하다 is stiff; native Korean docs front the document with 이 문서에서는/여기서는. Grammatical and clear, but audibly translated.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I found no drift, dropped caveat, or hallucination; the dense opening paragraph (오류 억제/완화 없음, 설계 의도 캡처, Circuit 변형 생성의 서버 측 이동, 암묵적 결정 없음) and every step 1-6 track the English clause for clause, and "지향적 실행 모델" matches the rendering used corpus-wide in the ko guides. What a native editor would still change: (1) "워크로드와 함께 `QuantumProgram`을 초기화하세요" is a with-calque — Korean takes the instrumental 로 ("워크로드로 초기화하세요"); (2) the qubit-count compound is written as "2Qubit Gate" with no separator, which no Korean technical writer would set that way (2큐비트 Gate / 2-qubit Gate), and the same file writes the singular case as "단일 qubit Gate", so the two forms disagree; (3) "structurally equivalent" is rendered "구조적으로 동일합니다" (identical), a slight strengthening of equivalence — 구조적으로 동등합니다 is the exact term. None of these would mislead a learner. Register is the standard -습니다 declarative + -하세요 imperative of Korean tech docs, consistent end to end.

examples.source: Initialize a `QuantumProgram` with your workload.
examples.translation: 워크로드와 함께 `QuantumProgram`을 초기화하세요.
examples.suggested: 워크로드로 `QuantumProgram`을 초기화하세요.
examples.why: "with your workload" calqued as 와 함께 (accompaniment). Korean marks the content you initialize something *with* using 로/으로; 와 함께 reads as if the workload were a separate companion object.

examples.source: two-qubit gates ... its single-qubit gates are replaced
examples.translation: 2Qubit Gate와 측정을 박스로 그룹화하고 ... 단일 qubit Gate가 매개변수화된 Gate로 대체됩니다
examples.suggested: 2큐비트 Gate ... 단일 큐비트 Gate (consistent form for both)
examples.why: The numeric compound is glued together as "2Qubit" with no separator, which is not how a Korean technical writer sets a count+unit compound, and the singular case a few paragraphs later uses a different form (단일 qubit). Recognizable either way, but inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: The template circuit is structurally equivalent to the original circuit.
examples.translation: 템플릿 Circuit은 원래 Circuit과 구조적으로 동일합니다.
examples.suggested: 템플릿 Circuit은 원래 Circuit과 구조적으로 동등합니다.
examples.why: 동일 = identical; the very next sentence says the single-qubit gates are in fact replaced, so "identical" mildly overstates the English "equivalent". Context repairs it immediately, so this is a wording sharpening, not a misleading claim.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat; the tricky sentences all survive intact ("Note that Open Plan users cannot submit session jobs" → "오픈 플랜 사용자는 Session Job을 제출할 수 없습니다", and the `batch`/`session`/`backend` "respectively" mapping is preserved with 각각). Three editor-level slips remain. (1) "dynamical decoupling" is rendered as "동적 분리" (line 15); the settled Korean domain term is "동적 디커플링" — "분리" reads as generic "separation" and makes the error-suppression technique harder to recognize, though the neighbouring "트월링" and the /guides link keep it identifiable. (2) "primitive" is split within the file: the frontmatter description says "프리미티브" while the body consistently keeps "Primitive" ("Sampler Primitive 사용 단계", "Primitives를 연습하세요", "Primitive 옵션"). (3) "topic" is calqued as "주제" twice ("이 주제의 단계는…", "…계정 설정 주제의 단계를 따르세요"); a Korean technical writer would write "이 문서"/"이 페이지" — 주제 there reads as MT. Register (해요체 imperatives: 따르세요/참조하세요/알아보세요) is consistent and correct.

examples.source: Sampler also supports built-in dynamical decoupling and twirling for error suppression.
examples.translation: Sampler는 또한 [오류 억제]를 위한 내장 동적 분리 및 트월링을 지원합니다.
examples.suggested: Sampler는 또한 [오류 억제]를 위한 내장 동적 디커플링(dynamical decoupling)과 트월링을 지원합니다.
examples.why: "동적 분리" is a literal gloss ("dynamic separation"); Korean Qiskit/quantum-hardware writing uses "동적 디커플링". Imperfect but still recognizable from context and the linked guide, so MINOR.

examples.source: IBM Quantum Sampler primitive / Steps to use the Sampler primitive / Practice with primitives
examples.translation: frontmatter: 'Sampler 프리미티브'; body: 'Sampler Primitive 사용 단계', 'Sampler Primitive에 대한 입력으로', 'Primitives를 연습하세요', 'Primitive 옵션 사용 방법'
examples.suggested: Pick one convention — either keep 'Primitive' everywhere (including the description) or use '프리미티브' everywhere.
examples.why: Same core term rendered two ways inside one file; the description a reader sees in search results disagrees with every body occurrence.

examples.source: The steps in this topic describe how to set up Sampler… / Follow the steps in the Set up your IBM Cloud account topic
examples.translation: 이 주제의 단계는 Sampler를 설정하고… / …[IBM Cloud 계정 설정](/guides/cloud-setup) 주제의 단계를 따르세요.
examples.suggested: 이 문서에서는 Sampler를 설정하고… 방법을 설명합니다. / [IBM Cloud 계정 설정](/guides/cloud-setup) 문서의 단계를 따르세요.
examples.why: "주제" is a word-for-word calque of documentation-sense "topic"; in Korean it means "subject/theme" and a native technical writer would use 문서/페이지. Reads as MT, meaning still clear.

editor_note: All three delta entries are faithful and natural: the H1 renders "A Qiskit Function by Global Data Quantum" as the idiomatic possessive "Global Data Quantum의 Qiskit Function" with the anchor intact, and both tables translate only the header cells (Set/Date/Assets → 세트/날짜/자산; **Example** → **예시**) while leaving every ticker, date and numeric value (8801.T, XS2239553048, 01/11/2022, population_size 90/92/120/40, num_generations 20) byte-identical to the English, so no quantity or set label can mislead a learner.

Short page, faithful overall: HA/DR framing, the three-zone/load-balancer architecture, the "customers are not responsible for DR planning" disclaimer and the two regions all survive intact, and terminology is consistent (region→지역, zone→영역, single point of failure→단일 장애 지점, load balancer→로드 밸런서). Two things a native technical editor would change. (1) In the SLO sentence the modifier is mis-attached: EN "a regional service that fulfills the defined SLOs with any paid plan" becomes "유료 플랜에서 정의된 SLO를 충족하는 지역 서비스" — which reads as "the SLOs defined in the paid plan" rather than "meets the defined SLOs on any paid plan", and the quantifier "any" (모든) is dropped. (2) "No noticeable degradation of service occurs during a zonal failure" is rendered with a topic marker, "서비스 성능 저하는 눈에 띄지 않습니다", which presupposes that degradation happens and merely isn't visible, and narrows "service" to "성능"; the flat assertion "눈에 띄는 서비스 저하는 발생하지 않습니다" matches the English. Neither would leave a reader with a false picture of the architecture, so this stays MINOR. Register (해요체 "참조하세요" / plain -습니다 declaratives) is consistent throughout.

examples.source: Quantum Compute is a regional service that fulfills the defined Service Level Objectives (SLO) with any paid plan.
examples.translation: Quantum Compute는 유료 플랜에서 정의된 [서비스 수준 목표(SLO)]를 충족하는 지역 서비스입니다.
examples.suggested: Quantum Compute는 모든 유료 플랜에서 정의된 [서비스 수준 목표(SLO)]를 충족하는 지역 서비스입니다.
examples.why: The English says the service meets the defined SLOs on ANY paid plan; the Korean attaches 유료 플랜 to the definition ("the SLOs defined in the paid plan") and drops the quantifier "any". Dropped qualifier, not a false claim.

examples.source: No noticeable degradation of service occurs during a zonal failure.
examples.translation: 영역 장애 발생 시 서비스 성능 저하는 눈에 띄지 않습니다.
examples.suggested: 영역 장애 발생 시 눈에 띄는 서비스 저하는 발생하지 않습니다.
examples.why: The topic marker 저하는 presupposes that degradation occurs and is merely unnoticeable, where the English asserts none noticeable occurs at all; 성능 also narrows "service" to "performance".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked every claim-bearing sentence, including the two that are easiest to invert: the entanglement note (⟨Z_1 Z_0⟩는 1이어야 하고 ⟨I_1⊗Z_0⟩⟨Z_1⊗I_0⟩의 측정값은 0이어야 합니다) and the last-section decay claim (이상적인 시뮬레이션에서는 모든 ⟨Z_0 Z_i⟩가 1이어야 하지만, i가 커질수록 … 감소), plus the resilience-level trade-off and the "소규모 Circuit에서만 가능" caveat in the simulator note — all correct, no dropped qualifiers, no hallucinations. What a native technical editor would change is surface: one ungrammatical construction "거리가 멀어질수록의 동작" (the -ㄹ수록 ending cannot take 의; should be 멀어짐에 따른 동작), "basis gates" rendered as 기본 Gate instead of the conventional 기저 게이트, and three consistency splits within the file — observable as 관측 가능량 (Steps 1–3) vs 관측량 (Step 4 and the scale-up section), credentials as 자격 증명 (Step 2 of part 1) vs 인증 정보 (Step 2 of part 2), and unstable Korean particles after the kept English nouns (Circuit를/Circuit을, 대규모 Qubit로 vs 대규모 Qubit으로 in the intro link and the matching heading). Also "essentially an extended Bell state" is calqued as 기본적으로 확장된 벨 상태, which reads as "a basically-extended Bell state" rather than 사실상/본질적으로. None of these would teach a learner anything false.

examples.source: This example uses the `ZZ` operators between qubits to examine the behavior as they get farther apart.
examples.translation: 이 예제에서는 Qubit 간 `ZZ` 연산자를 사용하여 거리가 멀어질수록의 동작을 살펴봅니다.
examples.suggested: 이 예제에서는 Qubit 사이의 `ZZ` 연산자를 사용하여 두 Qubit이 멀어짐에 따라 동작이 어떻게 달라지는지 살펴봅니다.
examples.why: '멀어질수록의'는 한국어에서 성립하지 않는 형태입니다(-ㄹ수록 뒤에 관형격 '의'를 붙일 수 없음). 의미는 전달되지만 원어민 기술 필자가 쓰지 않을 문장입니다.

examples.source: must consider the device's basis gates and qubit connectivity
examples.translation: 디바이스의 기본 Gate와 Qubit 연결성을 고려해야 합니다
examples.suggested: 디바이스의 기저 Gate(basis gate)와 Qubit 연결성을 고려해야 합니다
examples.why: basis gate의 관용 역어는 '기저 게이트'입니다. '기본 Gate'는 'default/basic gate'로 읽혀 ISA가 정하는 기저 집합이라는 개념이 흐려집니다(오개념을 심을 정도는 아니므로 MINOR).

examples.source: operators represent the observables to be measured … the observables you specified to Estimator
examples.translation: *연산자*는 측정할 관측 가능량을 나타냅니다 … Estimator에 지정한 관측량에 대한 기댓값
examples.suggested: 파일 전체에서 '관측 가능량'(또는 '옵저버블')으로 통일
examples.why: 동일 개념 observable이 1~3단계에서는 '관측 가능량', 4단계와 확장 섹션(349, 390행)에서는 '관측량'으로 갈립니다. 둘 다 인식 가능하나 파일 내 일관성이 깨집니다.

examples.source: It requires that you have already saved your credentials
examples.translation: [자격 증명을 저장]해 두셨어야 합니다 … [인증 정보를 저장]해야 합니다
examples.suggested: 두 곳 모두 '자격 증명'으로 통일
examples.why: 같은 EN 문장, 같은 링크(/guides/cloud-setup)인데 credentials가 '자격 증명'과 '인증 정보'로 다르게 번역되어 독자가 서로 다른 절차로 오인할 여지가 있습니다.

examples.source: a QuantumCircuit that prepares an n-qubit GHZ state (essentially an extended Bell state)
examples.translation: $n$-Qubit GHZ 상태(기본적으로 확장된 벨 상태)를 준비하는 `QuantumCircuit`
examples.suggested: $n$-Qubit GHZ 상태(사실상 벨 상태를 확장한 것)를 준비하는 `QuantumCircuit`
examples.why: 'essentially'를 '기본적으로'로 직역해 '기본적으로 확장된'이라는 수식 관계가 생기고, '본질적으로/사실상 벨 상태의 확장'이라는 원문의 의도가 흐려집니다.

editor_note: Both rewritten Card descriptions (entries 12 and 13) are semantically faithful — nothing is inverted, dropped, or invented, and the 해요체 register ("살펴보세요") matches the surrounding cards. Two editorial slips remain: entry 13 renders "curated sequences of ... content" as the calqued "콘텐츠의 엄선된 시퀀스", an English noun-stack a Korean technical writer would unwind (e.g. "체계적으로 구성된 학습·문서·튜토리얼 콘텐츠"); and entry 12's "full courses" as "전체 과정" is ambiguous, since 전체 과정 most readily reads "the entire process/whole course of" rather than "full-length courses" (전체 강좌 / 정규 강좌 is clearer). Note also that within these two delta entries the linkText values ("Visit IBM Quantum Learning", "Explore learning paths") are left in English while every other card in the file translates linkText ("튜토리얼 둘러보기", "소개 보기") — inconsistent, but not misleading.

examples.source: Explore curated sequences of learning, documentation, and tutorial content designed to facilitate knowledge and skill-building in specific interest areas.
examples.translation: 특정 관심 분야에서 지식과 역량을 쌓을 수 있도록 구성된 학습, 문서, 튜토리얼 콘텐츠의 엄선된 시퀀스를 살펴보세요.
examples.suggested: 특정 관심 분야의 지식과 역량을 쌓을 수 있도록 학습·문서·튜토리얼 콘텐츠를 체계적으로 엮은 학습 경로를 살펴보세요.
examples.why: "콘텐츠의 엄선된 시퀀스" is a direct calque of the English noun stack "curated sequences of ... content"; 시퀀스 is not how Korean tech writing refers to an ordered learning track (학습 경로/순서). Meaning is preserved, so this is a fluency slip only.

examples.source: Explore our free learning offerings, such as full courses and classroom modules.
examples.translation: 전체 과정 및 클래스룸 모듈과 같은 무료 학습 콘텐츠를 살펴보세요.
examples.suggested: 전체 강좌와 클래스룸 모듈 등 무료 학습 콘텐츠를 살펴보세요.
examples.why: "전체 과정" is read most naturally as "the entire process/whole course of (something)" rather than "full-length courses"; 강좌 disambiguates. Recognizable in context because it is coordinated with 클래스룸 모듈, so minor rather than misleading.

editor_note: Meaning is fully faithful — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat; the service description, the two ordered prerequisites, the install command, the update recommendation and all four Next-steps bullets match the English exactly, and domain terms are conventional (클라이언트 패키지, 릴리스 노트, 지원 중단 정책, 양자 계산). Two editorial slips: line 14 writes "`qiskit-ibm-runtime`을(를) 설치하기 전에" with the dual-particle template artifact, even though the token is fixed (런타임 → 을) and the same file gets it right at line 28 ("`pip install -U qiskit-ibm-runtime`을 실행하여") — so it is inconsistent within the file as well as machine-looking. Line 28 also traces "check … to see new releases" literally as "주기적으로 확인하여 새 릴리스를 확인하세요", repeating 확인 twice in one clause where a native writer would say "새 릴리스가 있는지 주기적으로 확인하세요". Neither would mislead a learner; "Grover의 알고리즘" (vs. the more usual 그로버 알고리즘) and the 합니다/-세요 register mix are defensible and not counted.

examples.source: Before installing the `qiskit-ibm-runtime`, follow the instructions in these guides:
examples.translation: `qiskit-ibm-runtime`을(를) 설치하기 전에 다음 가이드의 지침을 따르세요:
examples.suggested: `qiskit-ibm-runtime`을 설치하기 전에 다음 가이드의 지침을 따르세요:
examples.why: Dual-particle "을(를)" is a template placeholder used when the preceding word is dynamic. Here the token is fixed and reads 런타임 (consonant-final), so the particle is determinate: 을. The same file already uses the single correct particle at line 28 ("...runtime`을 실행하여"), making this both an MT artifact and a within-file inconsistency.

examples.source: Periodically check the [`qiskit-ibm-runtime` release notes](...) to see new releases.
examples.translation: [`qiskit-ibm-runtime` 릴리스 노트](...)를 주기적으로 확인하여 새 릴리스를 확인하세요.
examples.suggested: 새 릴리스가 있는지 [`qiskit-ibm-runtime` 릴리스 노트](...)를 주기적으로 확인하세요.
examples.why: Word-for-word tracing of "check … to see" puts 확인 twice in a single clause; a Korean technical writer would collapse the two verbs into one sentence. Meaning is unaffected — purely stiff, calqued phrasing.

editor_note: One hard negation-scope drift makes this misleading. In the `CustomInstruction` paragraph the English says the importer raises `QASM2ParseError` when a `gate` statement matches the custom instruction's `name` but "does not match **both** the number of parameters and the number of qubits" — i.e. an error whenever *either* count differs. The Korean renders this as "파라미터 수와 qubit 수가 모두 일치하지 않는 경우", whose dominant Korean reading is "when *neither* matches", so a learner concludes that a mismatch in only the qubit count (or only the parameter count) is accepted silently — the exact opposite of the API's behavior. Secondary, non-misleading points: "the resulting circuit will typically be more efficient to work with" becomes "결과 Circuit은 일반적으로 더 효율적으로 작동합니다" (shifts from ease of working with the circuit to the circuit's own execution efficiency), and the register is mixed — the body is uniformly 합니다체 with one stray 해요체 line ("사용하길 권장해요") and a corporate "당사의 익스포터". Terminology is otherwise correct and consistent (임포터/익스포터, 기저 Gate, 사용자 정의 고전 함수, 사분면을 인식하는).

examples.source: If a `gate` statement is encountered that matches the `name` of a custom instruction, but does not match both the number of parameters and the number of qubits, the importer will raise a `QASM2ParseError`
examples.translation: 사용자 정의 명령어의 `name`과 일치하는 `gate` 문을 만났지만 파라미터 수와 qubit 수가 모두 일치하지 않는 경우, 임포터는 ... `QASM2ParseError`를 발생시킵니다.
examples.suggested: 사용자 정의 명령어의 `name`과 일치하는 `gate` 문을 만났더라도 파라미터 수와 qubit 수 중 하나라도 일치하지 않으면, 임포터는 ... `QASM2ParseError`를 발생시킵니다.
examples.why: Negation scope is inverted: '모두 일치하지 않는 경우' reads as 'when neither matches', so the learner believes a single mismatched count is tolerated, while the importer actually errors when either count differs.

examples.source: If you specify which gate classes to use for `gate` statements outside of "qelib1.inc", the resulting circuit will typically be more efficient to work with.
examples.translation: `"qelib1.inc"` 외부의 `gate` 문에 사용할 Gate 클래스를 지정하면, 결과 Circuit은 일반적으로 더 효율적으로 작동합니다.
examples.suggested: ... 결과 Circuit을 일반적으로 더 효율적으로 다룰 수 있습니다.
examples.why: '더 효율적으로 작동합니다' claims the circuit itself runs more efficiently; the English claims it is easier/cheaper for the user to work with. A quantifiable-sounding claim shifted to a different subject.

examples.source: We recommend using these versions or newer.
examples.translation: 이 버전 이상을 사용하길 권장해요.
examples.suggested: 이 버전 이상을 사용하는 것을 권장합니다. (or convert the whole file to 해요체)
examples.why: The file is otherwise uniformly 합니다체 (개발되었습니다, 제공합니다, 참조하세요); this single 해요체 sentence plus the corporate '당사의 익스포터' (line 116) makes the register inconsistent within one page.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, swapped quantities, dropped caveats or hallucinated claims; the long OpenQASM 3 paper quote is rendered accurately clause for clause (including "고수준 언어는 아니지만" and the hardware-engineer sentence), and the imperative register is consistently 해요체 (참조하세요 / 학습하세요 / 읽으세요). Three things a native technical editor would still change: (1) "another for transpilation" becomes "Transpiler에는 다른 도구를" — the process (트랜스파일/트랜스파일레이션) is swapped for the agent noun, so it reads as "a different tool for the transpiler"; the trailing "and so forth"(등) is also dropped from that list. (2) "because of its versatility … for a variety of audiences" becomes "그 다양성 덕분에 다양한 사용자층에서" — 다양성 is the wrong sense of versatility (범용성/다재다능함) and the doubled 다양 reads clumsy. (3) The circuit term splits within one sentence: "양자 Circuit" beside "양자 회로 모델" in the opening paragraph (and 회로 nowhere else), so the same concept appears under two spellings. None of these would give a learner a false belief.

examples.source: For developers that prefer one tool for circuit construction, another for transpilation, and so forth
examples.translation: Circuit 구성에는 한 도구를, Transpiler에는 다른 도구를 선호하는 개발자들에게
examples.suggested: 회로 구성에는 한 도구를, 트랜스파일에는 또 다른 도구를 사용하는 것을 선호하는 개발자 등에게
examples.why: The activity (transpilation) is replaced by the tool name (Transpiler), and the open-ended 'and so forth' is dropped, narrowing the sentence from 'a chain of specialized tools' to exactly two.

examples.source: OpenQASM is the choice for a variety of audiences because of its versatility.
examples.translation: OpenQASM은 그 다양성 덕분에 다양한 사용자층에서 선택받고 있습니다.
examples.suggested: OpenQASM은 그 범용성 덕분에 여러 사용자층에서 선택받고 있습니다.
examples.why: versatility is 범용성/다재다능함, not 다양성 (diversity); repeating 다양 twice in one short sentence is phrasing a Korean technical writer would not leave in.

examples.source: an imperative programming language for describing quantum circuits. OpenQASM uses the quantum circuit model…
examples.translation: 양자 Circuit을 기술하기 위한 명령형 프로그래밍 언어입니다. OpenQASM은 양자 회로 모델을 사용하여…
examples.suggested: Use one rendering for the concept throughout (e.g. 양자 회로 / 양자 회로 모델).
examples.why: The same concept appears as both 'Circuit' and '회로' inside a single paragraph; the concept stays identifiable, so this is a consistency slip rather than a comprehension risk.

editor_note: Nothing in this file would mislead a learner on the numbers or the rules — every limit is carried over correctly (1,000만 회 실행, Qubit당 2,680만 개 제어 시스템 명령어, RZ 3,000만/SX 2,000만, Circuit당 2-Qubit Gate 500만), the ISA→control-instruction table note and the (4,1)-shape/2,000-shot worked example both match the English exactly. Two editorial slips: "primitive options" is rendered "특정 기본 옵션" ("certain basic/default options"), which loses the Qiskit Primitive referent and is inconsistent with the same file keeping "Primitive Unified Bloc(PUB)" untranslated three lines later; and the opening sentence drops the probabilistic hedge in "to decrease the likelihood that your job fails" (KO: "실패하는 것을 기다리지 않아도 되도록"), reading as if validation removes post-queue failure rather than making it less likely. Also the closing cross-reference "[사용자 정의 Backend에 대한 트랜스파일.]" carries a stray period inside the link text and is stiffer than the English imperative title. Register is standard Korean tech-doc 합니다체 declaratives with 해요체 imperatives (참조하세요), no honorific/humble 드리- forms — defensible, not counted as a defect.

examples.source: Certain primitive options increase the circuit size.
examples.translation: 특정 기본 옵션은 Circuit 크기를 증가시킵니다.
examples.suggested: 특정 프리미티브(Primitive) 옵션은 Circuit 크기를 증가시킵니다.
examples.why: "기본" reads as "basic/default", not the Qiskit Primitive (Sampler/Estimator) whose options are meant; the same file keeps "Primitive Unified Bloc(PUB)" in English, so the term is split within the file. The following bullets (DD, gate-folding ZNE) still identify the referent, so it is imperfect rather than misleading.

examples.source: it is first validated to try to ensure that the job can run on the QPU, to decrease the likelihood that your job fails after you've waited for it to go through the queue
examples.translation: 먼저 작업 유효성 검사 서비스로 전달됩니다. 이 서비스는 작업이 큐를 통과한 후 실패하는 것을 기다리지 않아도 되도록, 해당 작업이 QPU에서 실행 가능한지 확인하려 합니다.
examples.suggested: 큐를 기다린 끝에 작업이 실패할 가능성을 줄이기 위해, 먼저 해당 작업이 QPU에서 실행 가능한지 유효성 검사를 거칩니다.
examples.why: The hedge "decrease the likelihood" is dropped and the waiting is re-attached to the failure instead of to the queue; the purpose clause keeps it from being an outright guarantee, so it is a dropped qualifier rather than a false claim.

examples.source: For full details, see [Transpile against custom backends](/guides/custom-backend#ex-count-ops).
examples.translation: 전체 내용은 [사용자 정의 Backend에 대한 트랜스파일.](/guides/custom-backend#ex-count-ops)을 참조하세요.
examples.suggested: 자세한 내용은 [사용자 정의 Backend를 대상으로 트랜스파일하기](/guides/custom-backend#ex-count-ops)를 참조하세요.
examples.why: Stray sentence period inside the link label, and "~에 대한 트랜스파일" is a noun-calque of the English imperative title that a Korean technical writer would render verbally.

editor_note: Delta entry 24 (the benchmark table) is faithful: every header renders correctly and conventionally (Number of qubits→큐비트 수, Approximation Ratio→근사 비율, Runtime usage (s)→런타임 사용량(초), Total Number of shots→총 샷 수, Number of iterations→반복 횟수) and all eight data rows preserve the source numbers exactly (28/30/32 → 180s/30s/30k/5; 80 → 480/60/90k/9; 156 HUBO → 600/70/100k/10), with alignment markers and the Unweighted MaxCut / HUBO 1 / HUBO 2 labels left intact.

The opening sentence of "시뮬레이터는 언제 사용해야 하나요?" (line 59) reverses the section's core teaching point: EN says simulators "should be used to help develop and test programs before fine-tuning them and sending them to quantum hardware", i.e. the simulator IS the development-and-testing tool, but the Korean "양자 시뮬레이터는 프로그램을 개발하고 테스트한 후 세밀하게 조정하여 양자 하드웨어로 전송하기 전에 사용해야 합니다" parses as "use simulators AFTER you have developed and tested the program", turning development/testing into a prerequisite step done elsewhere and leaving the learner without the answer to the heading's own question. The following sentence "로컬 시뮬레이터는 좋은 성능과 효율성으로 이를 수행할 수 있습니다" then refers back to an 이를 that no longer names anything the simulator does. Secondary, non-misleading slip: in the comparison table "error correction" is rendered 오류 교정 where the field's standard term is 오류 정정 (the file otherwise uses 오류 완화/오류 억제 correctly for mitigation/suppression). Everything else — retirement date, the ~50-qubit and 100-qubit ceilings, the Open Plan sessions caution, the Aer-from-backend noise-model paragraph — is faithful.

examples.source: Quantum simulators should be used to help develop and test programs before fine-tuning them and sending them to quantum hardware. Local simulators can do this with good performance and efficiency.
examples.translation: 양자 시뮬레이터는 프로그램을 개발하고 테스트한 후 세밀하게 조정하여 양자 하드웨어로 전송하기 전에 사용해야 합니다. 로컬 시뮬레이터는 좋은 성능과 효율성으로 이를 수행할 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 양자 시뮬레이터는 프로그램을 세밀하게 조정하여 양자 하드웨어로 보내기 전에, 프로그램을 개발하고 테스트하는 데 사용해야 합니다. 로컬 시뮬레이터는 이 작업을 좋은 성능과 효율성으로 수행할 수 있습니다.
examples.why: The purpose clause "to help develop and test programs" became a temporal precondition ("개발하고 테스트한 후" = after developing and testing), so the translation answers the section heading with the wrong workflow order and drops the point that the simulator is what you develop and test with. It also strands the 이를 in the next sentence, which in EN refers to "develop and test".

examples.source: Large stabilizer circuits, error correction
examples.translation: 대형 스태빌라이저 Circuit, 오류 교정
examples.suggested: 대형 스태빌라이저 Circuit, 오류 정정
examples.why: Quantum error correction is conventionally 양자 오류 정정 in Korean; 교정 (calibration/proofreading sense) is recognizable but is not the domain term, and the file already uses 완화/억제 correctly for mitigation/suppression, so the mismatch is visible within the same page.

editor_note: Faithful and natural throughout: the "might incur a cost" caveat survives intact as "App ID 사용 (비용이 발생할 수 있습니다)", the dynamic-rules tip correctly keeps the negation ("동적 규칙을 설정하면 … 수동으로 추가할 필요가 없습니다"), and IDP/App ID/SAML are kept in English while ID provider is consistently "ID 제공자"; register is consistent 합니다체 with 해요체 imperatives (참조하세요).

Judging only the re-written title entry: the English "Understand the breaking package changes" becomes "패키지 변경 사항 이해하기", which drops the qualifier "breaking" entirely — the title now promises merely "the package changes" rather than the compatibility-breaking ones, which is exactly the point of the page. It does not mislead a learner, because the very next lines carry the qualifier ("앞으로 이와 같은 주요 패키징 변경은 하지 않을 예정입니다", "주요 패키징 변경을 결정한 이유"), so the concept is recoverable within two sentences; but a native technical editor would restore it for consistency with that body wording (and with the H1/title pair, which are identical here). Suggested "호환성이 깨지는 패키지 변경 사항 이해하기" or, matching the body's own choice, "주요 패키지 변경 사항 이해하기".

examples.source: Understand the breaking package changes
examples.translation: 패키지 변경 사항 이해하기
examples.suggested: 호환성이 깨지는 패키지 변경 사항 이해하기 (or 주요 패키지 변경 사항 이해하기, matching line 15/18)
examples.why: "breaking" is unrendered, so the heading announces generic package changes instead of compatibility-breaking ones; the body itself uses 주요 패키징 변경 for the same idea, so the title is also inconsistent with the page's own term.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, inverted conditions or hallucinations; the tricky spots (the "PrimitiveResult of SamplerPubResult" → "SamplerPubResult의 PrimitiveResult" genitive inversion, "instead of picking a single measurement type per job" → "작업당 단일 측정 유형을 선택하는 대신", the Step 8 XOR/bit-flip explanation, and even the EN typo "innovation rather than data. conversion." correctly reconstructed as "데이터 변환보다는 혁신에") all land correctly. What a native editor would change is consistency: four core terms are each rendered two ways inside one file — "annotation" as 주석 (lines 47, 69, 73) and 어노테이션 (179, 182, 285); "samplex" kept as samplex (47, 69, 73, 141) and as 샘플렉스 (183, 193, 223, 231, 285); "box" as 상자 (50, 69) and 박스 (182, 193); "randomization" as 무작위화 (137, 141, 143) and 랜덤화 (145, 231, 255). The Step 7 table also breaks the file's own convention: its column header translates Executor as "실행기" while every other occurrence in the document keeps "Executor", and its prose cells ("Post-process the array manually", "Automatic", "per register") plus the two "Examples:"/"**Example:**" labels are left untranslated where the Conceptual-mapping table's cells were translated. Finally, "inspect and sample the template circuit locally" (EN line 37) loses "inspect and" in KO line 30, and line 15's "제공해주시기 바랍니다" is a deferential slip against the file's otherwise plain 합니다체/하세요 register.

examples.source: you capture your design intent on the client side (by using circuit annotations and a *samplex*) … you declare that intent explicitly by using annotated boxes and a samplex
examples.translation: (회로 주석과 *samplex*를 사용하여) … 어노테이션이 지정된 박스와 샘플렉스(…)를 사용하여
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering per term and hold it: 어노테이션 (or 주석) throughout, 샘플렉스 (or samplex) throughout, 박스 (or 상자) throughout.
examples.why: Four key terms of the directed-execution vocabulary each appear in two forms in the same document (주석/어노테이션, samplex/샘플렉스, 상자/박스, 무작위화/랜덤화). A reader tracking 'samplex' through Steps 3–5 sees the word change shape mid-guide; the concept stays identifiable, so this is a consistency defect, not a misleading one.

examples.source: | Task | Sampler | Executor |
examples.translation: | 작업 | Sampler | 실행기 |
examples.suggested: | 작업 | Sampler | Executor |
examples.why: This is the only place in the file where the primitive name Executor is translated (실행기); the other ~40 occurrences, including the sibling Conceptual-mapping table and every heading, keep 'Executor'. In a migration guide the primitive name is an API identifier and should stay stable.

examples.source: Post-process the array manually / Automatic / per register / Examples: / **Example:**
examples.translation: Post-process the array manually / Automatic / per register / Examples: / **Example:**
examples.suggested: 배열을 직접 후처리 / 자동 / 레지스터별 / 예: / **예:**
examples.why: Prose cells in the Step 7 results table and the two example labels are left in English, while the equivalent cells in the Conceptual-mapping table (내장 옵션, 수동으로 구성해야 함 …) were translated. The page reads as half-finished at exactly the point where a migrating user scans for the Sampler→Executor equivalence.

examples.source: In the meantime, you can still inspect and [sample the template circuit locally](#sample-local) to validate your workflow before submitting it to hardware.
examples.translation: 그때까지는 [로컬에서 템플릿 회로를 샘플링](#sample-local)하여 하드웨어에 제출하기 전에 워크플로를 검증할 수 있습니다.

examples.source: You are invited to test them and provide feedback by opening an issue in the … GitHub repositories.
examples.translation: … GitHub 저장소에서 이슈를 열어 테스트하고 피드백을 제공해주시기 바랍니다.

examples.why: '-해주시기 바랍니다' is a deferential/formal request form out of step with the plain 합니다체 + -하세요 imperatives the rest of the guide uses (샘플링하고 싶을 때 사용하세요, 옮기세요, 참조하세요). A single slip, but it stands out in the first admonition.

editor_note: The page is fluent, idiomatic 해요체 and teaches the same four cost-control levers as the English, but a native technical editor would change four things. (1) "usage" / "QPU consumption" is rendered as 양자 시간 ("quantum time") in both the frontmatter description and the first bullet — that is IBM's *former* metric name, so the current billing unit (usage) is silently swapped for a related-but-different one; recognizable, not concept-breaking, but stale. (2) "scales with the number of shots" is strengthened to 샷 수에 비례하여 증가합니다 ("increases in proportion to"), which asserts strict proportionality the English does not. (3) The "Cost functions" link label was replaced by the course name 변분 알고리즘 설계, so the reader is no longer told which lesson they will land on. (4) "likely parameterized" is softened/shifted to 주로 매개변수화된 ("mostly parameterized") rather than 아마도, and the hedging "Note that" before the stale-noise-model caveat is dropped (the caveat itself survives intact). No inverted conditions, no hallucinated sentences; 노이즈 모델, 오류 억제/오류 완화, 샷, 세션/배치 are correct and consistent throughout.

examples.source: How to minimize the amount of usage spent processing and running a job. / A job's QPU consumption (and therefore, its cost) scales with the number of shots.
examples.translation: 작업을 처리하고 실행하는 데 소요되는 양자 시간을 최소화하는 방법입니다. / 작업에 소요되는 양자 시간(및 그에 따른 비용)은 샷 수에 비례하여 증가합니다.
examples.suggested: …소요되는 사용량(usage)을 최소화하는 방법입니다. / 작업의 QPU 사용량(및 그에 따른 비용)은 샷 수에 따라 증가합니다.
examples.why: 'usage'/'QPU consumption' is replaced by 양자 시간, the superseded 'quantum time' metric. The concept survives but the billing unit named in the source is not the one the reader is given.

examples.source: scales with the number of shots
examples.translation: 샷 수에 비례하여 증가합니다
examples.why: 'Scales with' is turned into strict proportionality (비례). The English deliberately avoids claiming a linear relationship; 샷 수에 따라 증가합니다 keeps the softer claim.
examples.suggested: 샷 수에 따라 증가합니다

examples.source: Explore error mitigation in the [Cost functions](/learning/courses/variational-algorithm-design/cost-functions) course.
examples.translation: [변분 알고리즘 설계](/learning/courses/variational-algorithm-design/cost-functions) 과정에서 오류 완화를 살펴보세요.
examples.suggested: [비용 함수](/learning/courses/variational-algorithm-design/cost-functions) 강의에서 오류 완화를 살펴보세요.
examples.why: The link text was swapped from the lesson name to the course name, so the label no longer matches the page the link opens.

examples.source: multiple jobs that contain the same (likely parameterized) circuits … Note that a noise model becomes stale after a certain time
examples.translation: 동일한(주로 매개변수화된) Circuit이 포함된 여러 작업 … 노이즈 모델은 일정 시간이 지나면 유효하지 않게 되므로
examples.suggested: 동일한(아마도 매개변수화된) … 참고로, 노이즈 모델은 일정 시간이 지나면 오래되어 쓸 수 없게 되므로
examples.why: 'Likely' (a hedge about this particular case) becomes 주로 ('mostly', a frequency claim), and the 'Note that' framing is dropped; 'stale' is also hardened to 유효하지 않게 (invalid). Each is small on its own and the caveat still lands.

editor_note: Delta entry 11 (the monitoring-method table) is faithful row for row: `job.result()` keeps the blocking caveat as "작업 결과를 가져옵니다(완료될 때까지 차단되는 호출)" and `job.wait_for_final_state()` correctly renders "terminal state" as "작업이 최종 상태에 도달할 때까지 차단합니다", with 메서드/설명 headers and consistent 합니다체 matching the surrounding page prose.

Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat; the intentionally duplicated EN sentence about IBM Cloud Logs (lines 14/18) is reproduced identically in both places, and the whole action/endpoint table maps 1:1 (백엔드 구성 가져오기, ID로 작업 가져오기, 백엔드 레인 구성 가져오기). Two editorial slips remain. (1) Register: the file is otherwise consistent 해요체 (보고해요, 있어요), but the very first body sentence ends in 합쇼체 "생성합니다" — an isolated formal slip on the opening line. (2) The table header "Triggered by" is rendered "트리거 조건" ("trigger condition"), while the column actually lists the API operations that trigger each event; "트리거하는 작업" or "트리거 원인" would match the content. Neither would mislead a learner about the product behavior.

examples.source: IBM Cloud® services, such as IBM Quantum® System Service, generate activity tracking events.
examples.translation: IBM Cloud® 서비스(예: IBM Quantum® System Service)는 활동 추적 이벤트를 생성합니다.
examples.suggested: IBM Cloud® 서비스(예: IBM Quantum® System Service)는 활동 추적 이벤트를 생성해요.
examples.why: Lone 합쇼체 ending on the opening sentence; every other sentence in the file uses 해요체 (보고해요, 준수할 수 있어요, 받을 수 있어요).

examples.source: | Action | Triggered by |
examples.translation: | 작업 | 트리거 조건 |
examples.suggested: | 작업 | 트리거하는 작업 |
examples.why: The column lists the API calls that raise each event, not a condition; '트리거 조건' reads as a precondition and is a slightly imprecise (though not misleading) header.

examples.source: ...to route auditing events in your account to destinations of your choice by configuring targets and routes that define where activity tracking events are sent.
examples.translation: ...대상 및 경로를 구성함으로써 활동 추적 이벤트가 전송될 위치를 정의하고 계정의 감사 이벤트를 원하는 목적지로 라우팅할 수 있어요.
examples.suggested: 활동 추적 이벤트가 전송될 위치를 정의하는 대상과 경로를 구성해, 계정의 감사 이벤트를 원하는 목적지로 라우팅할 수 있어요.
examples.why: The EN relative clause ('targets and routes that define where…') is flattened into a coordinate '정의하고', making the long sentence read as two loosely chained clauses; meaning survives but the syntax is calqued and heavy.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout this short marketing/overview page — no drift, no hallucination, no domain-term error (there are essentially no technical terms here beyond 양자 컴퓨팅/프레임워크/에코시스템, all conventional). Two things a native technical editor would still change. (1) "thanks in part to its vibrant community" loses its hedge: "활발한 커뮤니티 덕분에 가장 인기 있는 양자 프레임워크가 되었습니다" reads as sole causation, and the present-tense "is the most popular" is also shifted to a completed "되었습니다"; "부분적으로는 활발한 커뮤니티 덕분에 … 프레임워크입니다" would be exact. (2) "a dynamic and welcoming group" is calqued as "역동적이고 환영하는 그룹" — "환영하는 그룹" is not idiomatic Korean (a group that welcomes what?); a native writer would use "누구나 환영받는" or "개방적이고 활기찬". The ~습니다 register matches the rest of the ko locale (qpu-information, execution-modes) and is the standard for Korean technical docs, so I do not count it as a slip.

examples.source: Today, Qiskit is the most popular quantum framework, thanks in part to its vibrant community.
examples.translation: 오늘날 Qiskit은 활발한 커뮤니티 덕분에 가장 인기 있는 양자 프레임워크가 되었습니다.
examples.suggested: 오늘날 Qiskit은 부분적으로는 활발한 커뮤니티 덕분에 가장 인기 있는 양자 프레임워크입니다.
examples.why: The qualifier "in part" is dropped, turning a partial attribution into an unqualified one; "되었습니다" also converts the English present-state statement into a completed change of state.

examples.source: The Qiskit community is a dynamic and welcoming group of developers, scientists, and enthusiasts...
examples.translation: Qiskit 커뮤니티는 ... 개발자, 과학자, 열성적인 참여자들로 이루어진 역동적이고 환영하는 그룹입니다.
examples.suggested: ... 개발자, 과학자, 애호가들이 모인, 활기차고 누구나 환영받는 커뮤니티입니다.
examples.why: "환영하는 그룹" is a direct calque of "welcoming group"; in Korean the active participle needs an object, so the phrase reads as machine translation rather than something a Korean technical writer would produce.

editor_note: Judging only the two rewritten headings. Neither misleads — "종량제" is the correct, idiomatic Korean rendering of pay-as-you-go, and "온프레미스" is the standard rendering of on-prem — but both now break the file's own convention twice over. (1) Every other plan heading keeps the English product name ("## Open Plan", "## Flex Plan", "## Premium Plan"), and the running prose still names this very plan in English ("Open Plan 인스턴스와 Pay-As-You-Go Plan 인스턴스를…", "400분을 구매하지 않으려면 Pay-As-You-Go Plan을 고려해 보세요"), so the reader arriving at "## 종량제 요금제" has no visible link between the heading and the product name used everywhere else on the page and on IBM's pricing site. (2) The head noun also switched: the body consistently says 플랜 ("이 플랜은 … 권장됩니다", "여러 플랜에 액세스하려면"), while these two headings say 요금제 — and 요금제 sits especially awkwardly on On-Prem, which the section body describes as a dedicated serviced system rather than a tariff. Recommend restoring "Pay-As-You-Go Plan" / "On-Prem Plan" as the headings (or, if translating, using 플랜 and glossing the English name once) so heading and body agree.

examples.source: Pay-As-You-Go Plan {#pay-as-you-go-plan}
examples.translation: 종량제 요금제 {#pay-as-you-go-plan}
examples.suggested: Pay-As-You-Go Plan (종량제)
examples.why: The prose of this same file keeps the product name in English twice — line 14 ("Open Plan 인스턴스와 Pay-As-You-Go Plan 인스턴스") and line 58 ("Pay-As-You-Go Plan을 고려해 보세요") — as do the sibling headings Open Plan / Flex Plan / Premium Plan. A reader scanning for the section the body points them to sees only 종량제 요금제. Not misleading, but a native editor would align heading and body.

examples.source: On-Prem Plan {#on-prem-plan}
examples.translation: 온프레미스 요금제 {#on-prem-plan}
examples.suggested: On-Prem Plan (온프레미스 플랜)
examples.why: Same convention break as above, plus a head-noun switch: the file otherwise uses 플랜 ("이 플랜은…", "여러 플랜에 액세스하려면"), and 요금제 (tariff/rate plan) reads oddly against this section's own description of a dedicated on-premises system serviced and maintained by IBM.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — deprecation timeline (2025 초, SDK v1.3.0 → v2.0.0), the RXCalibrationBuilder/RZXCalibrationBuilder procedure, the "calibration = ScheduleBlock ↔ QuantumCircuit의 Gate 매핑" definition, and the requirement that both R_X(θ) and R_ZZ(θ) be loaded via use_fractional_gates all survive intact; no drift, no hallucination, nothing that would mislead a learner. The editorial slips are lexical and stylistic: "더 이상 사용 중단(deprecated)되었으며" is a broken collocation (더 이상 is negative-polarity and cannot govern 사용 중단되다 — should be "사용 중단(deprecated)되었으며" or "더 이상 사용되지 않으며"); "applications that might lead to quantum advantage" becomes 응용 프로그램, which in Korean means a software program rather than an application area (응용 분야); and "단일 및 2-Qubit 회전" copies the English hyphen-suspension ("single- and two-qubit"), a construction Korean does not support, so the reader must supply the elided 큐비트. Qubit is also split within the file — 큐비트 in the frontmatter description vs Qubit in every body occurrence. Register is uniformly 합니다체 with no 드리- humble forms or 하십시오 imperatives.

examples.source: pulse-level control on all IBM Quantum® processors has been deprecated and will be removed in early 2025
examples.translation: 모든 IBM Quantum® 프로세서에서의 펄스 수준 제어는 더 이상 사용 중단(deprecated)되었으며 2025년 초에 제거될 예정입니다
examples.suggested: 모든 IBM Quantum® 프로세서의 펄스 수준 제어는 사용 중단(deprecated)되었으며 2025년 초에 제거될 예정입니다
examples.why: '더 이상' is a negative-polarity adverb and cannot govern '사용 중단되다'; the pairing is ungrammatical-sounding to a native reader. Either drop 더 이상 or rewrite as '더 이상 사용되지 않으며'. Meaning is still recoverable, so MINOR.

examples.source: users exploring applications that might lead to quantum advantage
examples.translation: 양자 우위로 이어질 수 있는 응용 프로그램을 탐색하는 사용자
examples.suggested: 양자 우위로 이어질 수 있는 응용 분야를 탐색하는 사용자
examples.why: '응용 프로그램' is the Korean term for a software application/program. The source means application areas or use cases, which is 응용 분야 (or 활용 사례). Recognizable in context but the wrong lexical choice for the domain.

examples.source: single- and two-qubit rotations
examples.translation: 단일 및 2-Qubit 회전
examples.suggested: 단일 큐비트 및 2-큐비트 회전
examples.why: Calqued from the English hyphen-suspension ('single- and two-qubit'), which Korean does not license — 단일 is left dangling with no head noun, so the reader must mentally restore 큐비트. Repeats in the H2 heading and in both body paragraphs.

examples.source: single and two-qubit rotations (frontmatter description) / two-qubit rotations (body)
examples.translation: description: '단일 및 2-큐비트 회전…' vs body '단일 및 2-Qubit 회전'
examples.suggested: pick one rendering of qubit and use it in both the frontmatter and the body
examples.why: The core term qubit is 큐비트 in the frontmatter description but Qubit in every body occurrence — a within-file split of the file's most frequent domain term. Does not obscure the concept, so MINOR.

editor_note: The one delta entry — the title/sidebar_label "Optimization Solver - A Qiskit Function by Q-CTRL Fire Opal" rendered as "Optimization Solver - Q-CTRL Fire Opal의 Qiskit Function" — is faithful and idiomatic: the English "A Qiskit Function by X" is correctly recast as Korean possessive "X의 Qiskit Function", with the product names Optimization Solver / Fire Opal / Qiskit Function kept in English as the rest of the page consistently does (e.g. body text "Fire Opal Optimization Solver를 사용하면…", "Qiskit Functions는 … 실험적 기능입니다"). No drift, no dropped element, nothing a native technical editor would change.

Body prose is faithful and idiomatic — the 30샷 vs 170,000샷 contrast, the "엄격한 제한이 아니라 … 대략적인 임계값" qualifier, and the invariance rationale for metric $A$ all land correctly, and terms like 오류 억제 / 오류 완화(error mitigation) / 기댓값 / 관측량 are correct and consistent. The defects are all in the Sampler plotting step at the end: the step heading "**3. Plot the top bitstrings**" was rendered "**3. 결과 가져오기**" ("Retrieve the results"), which duplicates the preceding "**3. 결과 조회**" heading and no longer names what the step does; and the post-plot caption "The hidden bitstring is highlighted in purple, and it should be the bitstring with the highest number of counts" was replaced by a near-verbatim repeat of the pre-code sentence ("…카운트가 가장 높은 비트스트링을 플롯합니다"), dropping the purple-highlight legend that tells the learner how to read the chart. Separately, "primitive" is split within the file between 프리미티브 (headings, "IBM Quantum 프리미티브") and bare English primitive ("두 가지 primitive를 제공하며", "Estimator primitive를 사용하여"). Nothing teaches a false fact, so this is below the FAIL bar, but both the heading and the caption should be restored.

examples.source: **3. Plot the top bitstrings**
examples.translation: **3. 결과 가져오기**
examples.suggested: **3. 상위 비트스트링 플로팅**
examples.why: The step heading was replaced with "Retrieve the results", duplicating the previous step's heading ("3. 결과 조회") and hiding the fact that this step is about plotting. A reader scanning headings sees two identical retrieval steps and no plotting step.

examples.source: The hidden bitstring is highlighted in purple, and it should be the bitstring with the highest number of counts.
examples.translation: 최빈값이 숨겨진 비트스트링인지 확인하기 위해, 카운트가 가장 높은 비트스트링을 플롯합니다.
examples.suggested: 숨겨진 비트스트링은 보라색으로 강조 표시되며, 카운트가 가장 높은 비트스트링이어야 합니다.
examples.why: The caption after the code cell is not a translation of the English sentence — it is a duplicate of the sentence already given before the code cell (ko 396). The purple-highlight cue, which is the key to reading the bar chart, is dropped, and the sentence instructs the reader to plot something they have just plotted.

examples.source: The function offers two primitives, Sampler and Estimator …
examples.translation: 이 함수는 Sampler와 Estimator 두 가지 primitive를 제공하며 … (but: "IBM Quantum 프리미티브", "## Estimator 프리미티브")
examples.suggested: 이 함수는 Sampler와 Estimator 두 가지 프리미티브를 제공하며 …
examples.why: "primitive" is rendered as 프리미티브 in the headings and in "IBM Quantum 프리미티브", but left untranslated as bare English primitive in three body sentences. The concept stays identifiable, so this is a consistency slip rather than a comprehension problem, but one form should be picked.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I found no drift or hallucination: the accuracy formula gloss, the "scale 1.0 ≠ unmitigated because 1.0 includes readout mitigation" caveat, the complementary-scale rule (0.5→1.5, 1.3→0.7, "보완적인 스케일에 대한 precision은 보장되지 않습니다"), the "one observable per parameter set" zip, and every benchmark quantity (136 qubits of ibm_fez, 6.5시간/45분, up to 2x volume) all land correctly. What a native editor would change is consistency and polish: the QET paragraph (~l.708) abandons the Korean terms established earlier and writes raw lowercase English — "PUB precision", "요청된 각 noise scale", "readout mitigation을 포함합니다", "scale-factor 결과", "mitigation이 적용되지 않은 값" — where §QESEM 휴리스틱 (l.389/396) had used 판독 완화(REM), 스케일, 정밀도, `unmitigated`. The file also splits core terms by half (Observable/Circuit/Job in §개요–§벤치마크 vs 관측량/회로/작업 from l.321 onward). Smaller: "key figure of merit" → "핵심 성과 지표" (reads as KPI rather than a hardness metric), the calqued "…QPU 시간 오버헤드를 가집니다 / 확장되는" (l.120), and the doubled "…위해 … 위해" plus the humble "도와드릴" in §지원 받기 (l.827/840), which breaks the 해요체 convention.

examples.source: Returned scale-factor results are stored in `noise_scaling.results_with_REM` and include readout mitigation. The scale `1.0` point is therefore not identical to the unmitigated value…
examples.translation: 반환된 scale-factor 결과는 `noise_scaling.results_with_REM`에 저장되며 readout mitigation을 포함합니다. 따라서 scale `1.0` 지점은 mitigation이 적용되지 않은 값과 동일하지 않은데…
examples.suggested: 반환된 스케일 계수 결과는 `noise_scaling.results_with_REM`에 저장되며 판독 완화(REM)를 포함합니다. 따라서 스케일 `1.0` 지점은 `unmitigated` 값과 동일하지 않은데…
examples.why: Same concepts are rendered 판독 완화(REM)/스케일/정밀도 at lines 389 and 396; this paragraph switches to bare lowercase English (precision, noise scale, readout mitigation, scale-factor), so the reader cannot tell it is the same quantity.

examples.source: observable / circuit / job
examples.translation: 1st half: 'Observable', 'Circuit', 'Job'; 2nd half: '관측량', '회로', '작업'
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering per term for the whole file (e.g. 관측량 / 회로 / 작업, or the kept English form) and use it consistently.
examples.why: The file splits cleanly in two: §개요–§벤치마크 keeps the English forms, everything from `metadata["results"]` onward uses the Korean ones. Concept stays identifiable, so MINOR, but an editor would unify it.

examples.source: A key figure of merit for quantifying the hardness of both error mitigation and classical simulation … is **active volume**
examples.translation: …어려움을 정량화하는 핵심 성과 지표는 **활성 볼륨**입니다
examples.suggested: …어려움을 정량화하는 핵심 지표(성능 지수)는 **활성 볼륨**입니다
examples.why: '핵심 성과 지표' is the fixed Korean rendering of KPI (a business/management term); 'figure of merit' here is a physical hardness metric, so the register is off even though the sentence is not misleading.

examples.source: This method has a QPU time overhead that roughly scales as:
examples.translation: 이 방법은 대략 다음과 같이 확장되는 QPU 시간 오버헤드를 가집니다.
examples.suggested: 이 방법의 QPU 시간 오버헤드는 대략 다음과 같이 스케일링됩니다.
examples.why: '…를 가집니다' calques English 'has', and '확장되는' reads as physical expansion rather than asymptotic scaling; a Korean technical writer would make the overhead the subject and use 스케일링된다/증가한다.

examples.source: Our knowledgeable and friendly support staff are ready to assist you … We are committed to providing you with prompt and effective support to ensure you have the best possible experience
examples.translation: …지원 직원이 기술적 우려나 문의 사항을 도와드릴 준비가 되어 있습니다. … 최고의 경험을 보장하기 위해 신속하고 효과적인 지원을 제공하기 위해 노력하고 있습니다.
examples.suggested: …지원 직원이 기술적인 문제나 문의 사항을 도와줄 준비가 되어 있어요. … 최고의 경험을 드릴 수 있도록 신속하고 효과적인 지원을 제공하려고 노력하고 있습니다.
examples.why: '도와드릴' uses the humble 드리- form the locale convention avoids, and the doubled '…하기 위해 … 하기 위해' in one sentence is stiff; both are polish-level, not misleading.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I found no inverted condition, swapped quantity, dropped caveat or hallucinated claim; the tricky passages (V1 요구사항 "입력 회로의 수는 관측량 및 매개변수 집합의 수와 일치해야 했습니다", the `2\pi` full-cycle phase note "이산 대응 항목과 달리", the ScalableSymbolicPulse "마이그레이션 작업이 필요하지 않습니다", and the `qiskit.utils` "역시 제거된 `qiskit.algorithms` 및 `qiskit.opflow` 모듈에서만 사용되었습니다") all land correctly. The one real editorial defect is that "observable" is rendered two ways inside the same file: 관측량 (the pub/vectorized-input paragraph and the dense-`BaseOperator` bullet) versus 옵저버블 (the multi-PUB paragraph and the `PauliList` bullet) — the concept stays identifiable, so it is MINOR, but a native editor would unify on 관측량. Beyond that, two sentences are stiff calques: the dense→`SparsePauliOp` bullet stacks "…`BaseOperator`에서 `Estimator` 관측량 인수의 `SparsePauliOp`로의 암시적 변환은…", which mis-attaches `SparsePauliOp` to the argument instead of naming the argument as the site of the conversion; and the `extensions` removal sentence drops the English causal "as" ("제거되었으며, 해당 기능이 중복되었거나 … 연결되어 있었습니다" instead of "…있었기 때문에 제거되었습니다"). Register (해요체 "사용하세요/참조하세요") is consistent and correct throughout.

examples.source: …for arrays of n parameter sets, n observables… / …various parameter/observable combinations… / …in Estimator observable arguments…
examples.translation: `n`개의 관측량 … 다양한 매개변수/옵저버블 조합 … `Estimator` 관측량 인수 … Estimator 옵저버블 인수
examples.suggested: Unify on 관측량 (or on 옵저버블) for every occurrence of "observable" in this file.
examples.why: Same core domain term rendered two different ways within one page; a reader may wonder whether 관측량 and 옵저버블 are two different objects. Concept still identifiable, so MINOR.

examples.source: Implicit conversion from a dense `BaseOperator` to a `SparsePauliOp` in `Estimator` observable arguments is no longer allowed.
examples.translation: 밀집(dense) `BaseOperator`에서 [`Estimator`] 관측량 인수의 [`SparsePauliOp`]로의 암시적 변환은 더 이상 허용되지 않습니다.
examples.suggested: `Estimator`의 관측량 인수에서 밀집(dense) `BaseOperator`가 `SparsePauliOp`로 암시적으로 변환되는 동작은 더 이상 허용되지 않습니다.
examples.why: The calqued 에서…의…로의 chain makes `SparsePauliOp` read as belonging to the argument, whereas the English scopes "in Estimator observable arguments" to where the conversion occurs. Meaning survives, but the sentence is stiff and briefly ambiguous.

examples.source: The following classes have been removed from the codebase, as their functions were either redundant or linked to the `extensions` module:
examples.translation: 다음 클래스는 코드베이스에서 제거되었으며, 해당 기능이 중복되었거나 `extensions` 모듈에 연결되어 있었습니다:
examples.suggested: 다음 클래스는 해당 기능이 중복되었거나 `extensions` 모듈에 연결되어 있었기 때문에 코드베이스에서 제거되었습니다:
examples.why: The English "as" gives the reason for removal; the Korean 며-connective turns it into a second, merely additive fact, flattening the explanation in teaching material.

examples.source: The bitstrings show the measurement outcomes, preserving the shot order in which they were measured.
examples.translation: 비트문자열은 측정된 순서를 보존하며 측정 결과를 보여줍니다.
examples.suggested: 비트문자열은 측정 결과를 보여주며, 측정된 샷 순서를 그대로 보존합니다.
examples.why: "shot order" is reduced to plain 순서, dropping the shot-level qualifier that is the whole point of the V2 Sampler contrast with quasi-probability distributions. Not misleading, but a lost qualifier.

editor_note: Faithful and natural throughout: the breaking-change warning is preserved with correct negation scope ("이전 모든 버전의 Qiskit과의 호환성을 지원하지 않습니다"), "Breaking package changes" uses the accepted Korean IT convention "주요 변경 사항", and the three link bullets are recast into idiomatic "제목: 설명입니다" form without dropping any of the English purpose clauses ("의존성 업그레이드 방법", "코드 업데이트 방법", "새로운/기존 패키지 구조 이해").

Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination: the removal of `c_if`, the `Instruction.duration`/`unit` rationale, all six `generate_preset_pass_manager` migration points, and the v1.x support dates (2024년 9월 버그 수정 / 2025년 3월 보안) all match the English, and "duration→지속 시간" is consistent. What a native editor would change is surface polish and term discipline: "custom" is rendered two ways in the same section ("커스텀 Target" in point 1 vs "사용자 지정 target/Target" in points 2–5), and "transpiler" appears as "Transpiler" (§qiskit.transpiler intro, pulse bullet list) but "트랜스파일러" in point 6. Several phrases are visible calques: "in favor of the target and backend inputs" → "…입력을 선호하여 줄었습니다" (agentless, reads as if the use cases do the preferring), "strictly less featureful" → "기능이 엄격하게 제한되어 있었으며" (엄격하게 reads as "rigidly restricted" rather than "strictly fewer"), and "cannot be resolved" → "해석될 수 없습니다" (interpreted) where 확정/결정 is meant. One sentence also ends in the stiff "…제공하거나 합니다" construction. None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: There are multiple paths for constructing a custom Target … / it is possible to build a custom target … / It was used to provide pulse information to the transpiler
examples.translation: 커스텀 [`Target`](…)을 구성하는 방법은 여러 가지가 있습니다 … `instruction_durations` 및/또는 `timing_constraints`가 있는 사용자 지정 target을 구축하는 것도 가능합니다 … 이는 트랜스파일러에 펄스 정보를 제공하는 데 사용되었으며 (vs. 'Transpiler 사용 사례', 'Transpiler 패스')
examples.suggested: Unify to one rendering per term: '사용자 지정 Target' in every one of the six numbered points, and one of Transpiler / 트랜스파일러 throughout the file.
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency: 'custom' alternates 커스텀/사용자 지정 across consecutive numbered points, and 'transpiler' alternates Transpiler/트랜스파일러. The concept stays identifiable, so this is MINOR, but a reader scanning the migration list sees two labels for the same thing.

examples.source: The number of transpilation use cases where loose constraints are accepted has been reduced in favor of the target and backend inputs …, which allow for a more expressive communication of these constraints.
examples.translation: 느슨한 제약이 허용되는 Transpiler 사용 사례의 수가 `target` 및 `backend` 입력(…)을 선호하여 줄었습니다. 이 입력들은 이러한 제약을 더 표현력 있게 전달할 수 있도록 합니다.
examples.suggested: 느슨한 제약을 허용하는 트랜스파일 사용 사례는 `target` 및 `backend` 입력(…)을 우선하는 방향으로 줄어들었습니다.
examples.why: 'in favor of' calqued as '…을 선호하여' leaves the preferring agentless and grammatically attached to '사용 사례의 수', which no Korean technical writer would produce; '…을 우선하는 방향으로' is the idiomatic rendering. Meaning survives, so MINOR.

examples.source: This was strictly less featureful than the full control-flow form, and was never well-supported on hardware.
examples.translation: 이 방법은 완전한 제어 흐름 형식보다 기능이 엄격하게 제한되어 있었으며, 하드웨어에서 잘 지원되지 않았습니다.
examples.suggested: 이 방법은 완전한 제어 흐름 형식보다 기능이 확실히 더 적었고, 하드웨어에서 제대로 지원된 적도 없었습니다.
examples.why: 'strictly' here means 'strictly fewer features', not 'rigidly'; '엄격하게 제한되어' reads as if something imposed a strict restriction. The emphatic 'never' also flattens to a plain '잘 …않았습니다', dropping the qualifier — a softening small enough to stay MINOR.

examples.source: In these cases there are multiple sources of truth, and information such as gate errors and durations from the backend cannot be resolved based on the information given.
examples.translation: 이러한 경우 여러 진실의 원천이 존재하며, 게이트 오류 및 지속 시간과 같은 정보는 주어진 정보를 기반으로 백엔드로부터 해석될 수 없습니다.
examples.suggested: 이러한 경우 정보의 출처가 여러 개가 되어, 백엔드의 게이트 오류나 지속 시간 같은 정보를 주어진 정보만으로는 확정할 수 없습니다.
examples.why: 'resolved' (determined/settled) becomes '해석될' (interpreted), and 'multiple sources of truth' is calqued as '여러 진실의 원천'. Both are understandable in context, so no false belief forms, but neither is the term a Korean engineer would use.

examples.source: …or an InstructionProperties instance, from which the duration field may provide the duration in seconds (or None, if not supplied).
examples.translation: … 또는 [`InstructionProperties`](…) 인스턴스가 반환됩니다. 후자의 경우 [`duration`](…) 필드가 초 단위의 지속 시간을 제공하거나(제공되지 않은 경우 `None`) 합니다.
examples.suggested: … 후자의 경우 [`duration`](…) 필드에서 초 단위 지속 시간을 얻을 수 있으며, 값이 지정되지 않았다면 `None`입니다.
examples.why: The '…제공하거나 … 합니다' construction is a mechanical rendering of the English 'may provide … (or None)' and reads as unfinished Korean; splitting the alternative into its own clause is how a native writer would phrase it. Content is intact.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every section, prerequisite (Python 3.10 이상, 3.11+ 권장) and the auth exemption (Qiskit MCP 서버와 Qiskit Docs MCP 서버는 인증이 필요하지 않습니다) matches the English, and register is consistent 해요체/합니다. Three editorial slips remain. (1) The verb "transpiling/transpilation" is rendered as the noun-phrase calque "Transpiler 처리" / "AI 기반 Transpiler" (lines 21, 44, 64, 29) where a Korean quantum engineer would write 트랜스파일(하다) / 트랜스파일레이션 — the tool name is substituted for the process. (2) The whole "Next steps" list uses the English purpose-clause calque "~를 위해 … 하세요" ("상세한 문서, API 범위 및 예시를 위해 … 방문하세요", "이해하기 위해 … 알아보세요", "더 알아보기 위해 … 살펴보세요"), which reads as MT; native form is "…에 대한 자세한 내용은 …를 참고하세요". (3) In the Qiskit Docs MCP 서버 paragraph the English "intelligent retrieval and search" is collapsed to "지능형 검색" (retrieval dropped) and "without requiring authentication" is relocated from the second sentence to the first — harmless here, but the qualifier no longer sits on the search capability it modifies.

examples.source: Creating, manipulating, and transpiling quantum circuits / Optimizing circuits using AI-powered transpilation
examples.translation: 양자 Circuit 생성, 조작 및 Transpiler 처리 / AI 기반 Transpiler를 활용한 Circuit 최적화
examples.suggested: 양자 Circuit 생성, 조작 및 트랜스파일 / AI 기반 트랜스파일레이션을 활용한 Circuit 최적화
examples.why: The process (transpiling/transpilation) is replaced by the tool noun plus the generic verbalizer 처리; recognizable, but it is a calque a native technical writer would not use for the verb form.

examples.source: Visit the Qiskit MCP Servers GitHub repository for detailed documentation, API coverage, and examples.
examples.translation: 상세한 문서, API 범위 및 예시를 위해 [Qiskit MCP 서버 GitHub 저장소]를 방문하세요.
examples.suggested: 자세한 문서와 API 지원 범위, 예시는 [Qiskit MCP 서버 GitHub 저장소]에서 확인하세요.
examples.why: English "for X, do Y" mapped literally onto "X를 위해 Y하세요" throughout the recommendations block; Korean docs front the topic with ~은/는 rather than a purpose clause.

examples.source: ...This server enables intelligent retrieval and search across the Qiskit documentation without requiring authentication.
examples.translation: 인증 없이 Qiskit 문서 전체 생태계(...)에 대한 접근을 AI 어시스턴트에게 제공합니다. 이 서버를 통해 Qiskit 문서 전반에 걸쳐 지능형 검색을 수행할 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: ...이 서버를 통해 인증 없이도 Qiskit 문서 전반에 걸쳐 지능형 검색과 조회를 수행할 수 있습니다.
examples.why: "retrieval and search" is compressed to 검색 alone and the "without requiring authentication" caveat is moved onto the access sentence; the net claim is still true here, so it is a dropped qualifier rather than a misleading statement.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful end to end: the billing caveat keeps its negation ("...청구에 사용되는 시간(QPU 시간)이 아닙니다"), the Branch/T0/Duration/Pulse field definitions, the `Receive channel` gloss, and the closing hover example ("1161 dt에서 qubit 10에 적용된 X 게이트에 대한 제어 펄스") all preserve the source's conditions, quantities and setup — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat. What a native editor would change is terminology surface: "readout" is rendered with the everyday verb 읽기 ("읽기 채널", "임의 파형 생성기 읽기", "읽기 기기 ID") where Korean hardware docs write 판독 or 리드아웃; "The gate and the qubit to operate on" became "게이트와 작동할 qubit", which reads as "the qubit that will operate" rather than the target qubit; and qubit appears three ways inside one bullet list (큐비트 _x_ / qubit 번호 / Qubit을 측정할 때). None of these would teach a false concept, so they stay MINOR. Register is consistent 합니다체 with -세요 imperatives, no 하십시오체 or 드리- slips.

examples.source: `AWGRx_y` (arbitrary waveform generator readout) - Used by readout channels to communicate when measuring qubits. The _x_ and _y_ arguments correspond to the readout instrument ID and the qubit number, respectively.
examples.translation: `AWGRx_y` (임의 파형 생성기 읽기) - Qubit을 측정할 때 통신하기 위해 읽기 채널에서 사용됩니다. _x_ 및 _y_ 인수는 각각 읽기 기기 ID와 qubit 번호에 해당합니다.
examples.suggested: `AWGRx_y` (임의 파형 생성기 판독) - 큐비트를 측정할 때 통신하기 위해 판독 채널에서 사용됩니다. _x_ 및 _y_ 인수는 각각 판독 장비 ID와 큐비트 번호에 해당합니다.
examples.why: 'readout' in superconducting-qubit hardware is 판독 (or 리드아웃); 읽기 is the generic verb 'reading' and reads as machine output. Consistent within the file, so recognizable — MINOR, not misleading.

examples.source: `Instruction` - The gate and the qubit to operate on.
examples.translation: `Instruction` - 게이트와 작동할 qubit.
examples.suggested: `Instruction` - 게이트와 연산이 적용될 대상 큐비트.
examples.why: '작동할 qubit' parses most naturally as 'the qubit that will operate', inverting the agent; the English means the qubit the gate acts on. A native writer would use 대상 큐비트 / 연산이 적용될 큐비트.

examples.source: qubit (throughout the raw-timing-data bullet list)
examples.translation: 작동할 qubit … 큐비트 _x_에 대한 드라이브 채널 … Qubit을 측정할 때 … qubit 번호
examples.suggested: pick one rendering (큐비트) and use it in all prose positions
examples.why: Three renderings of the same core term inside a single bullet list. The concept stays identifiable, so MINOR; note the capitalized 'Qubit' instances may be the deterministic leak sweep's territory, but the 큐비트/qubit split is an editorial inconsistency on its own.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination found: the versioning rules ("수정 번호가 변경되면 Circuit은 계속 실행됩니다 / 주요 또는 부 번호가 변경되면 … 실행되지 않을 수 있으나, 실행될 수도 있습니다"), the P(0|1)/P(1|0) prepare-vs-measure directions, the EPLG 4/5 factor and the `error = 1` caveat all match the English exactly. What a native editor would change is consistency and a few physics terms: "calibration" is 교정 throughout but becomes 보정 in the Initialization-error card (l.644); "coherence" is rendered as the generic 일관성 ("위상 일관성", "Qubit의 일관성 특성") rather than the standard 결맞음, and "dephasing" appears as 위상 소실 in the T2 card title but 순수 위상 이탈 two lines later; "population in the |1⟩ state" becomes 모집단 (the statistics word for a sample population) instead of 점유(수). The 2Q-layered and Initialization cards also drop into 큐비트/Details 섹션/회로 while the rest of the file uses qubit/세부 정보 섹션/Circuit, and a few sentences are calqued (l.260 "백엔드는 교정될 때마다 … 변경되는 속성도 있습니다" needs 백엔드에는). None of these would mislead a learner; they are polish, not accuracy.

examples.source: View on IBM Quantum Platform — Calibration data section: Qubit dropdown menu
examples.translation: IBM Quantum Platform에서 확인 — 보정 데이터 섹션: 큐비트 드롭다운 메뉴
examples.suggested: IBM Quantum Platform에서 보기 — 교정 데이터 섹션: qubit 드롭다운 메뉴
examples.why: "Calibration" is 교정 everywhere else in the file (교정 데이터 섹션, 교정 시퀀스, 교정 작업); only this last Accordion card switches to 보정, and it also switches the row label from "…에서 보기" to "…에서 확인". Same UI section, two names.

examples.source: `T2` (Dephasing time) … the timescale over which a qubit maintains phase coherence … It accounts for both energy relaxation and pure dephasing processes, providing insight into the qubit's coherence properties.
examples.translation: `T2` (위상 소실 시간) … 위상 일관성을 유지하는 시간 척도 … 에너지 이완과 순수 위상 이탈 프로세스를 모두 고려하여 Qubit의 일관성 특성에 대한 통찰을 제공합니다.
examples.suggested: `T2` (위상 결어긋남 시간) … 위상 결맞음을 유지하는 시간 척도 … 에너지 이완과 순수 위상 결어긋남 과정을 모두 고려하여 Qubit의 결맞음 특성에 대한 통찰을 제공합니다.
examples.why: "Coherence" is the standard 결맞음 in Korean quantum literature; 일관성 is the everyday word for "consistency" and reads as a literal gloss. "Dephasing" is additionally split across the same card: 위상 소실 in the title, 위상 이탈 in the body.

examples.source: quantifies the percentage of the population in the $|1\rangle$ state after the default rep-delay
examples.translation: 기본 rep-delay와 큐비트 초기화 절차를 거친 뒤 $|1\rangle$ 상태에 있는 모집단의 비율을 정량화합니다
examples.suggested: … $|1\rangle$ 상태에 남아 있는 점유(population) 비율을 정량화합니다
examples.why: 모집단 is the statistics term for a sampled population; the physics sense here (level occupancy) is 점유/점유수. Recognizable in context but the wrong register of "population".

examples.source: the lowest two-qubit gate error (layered) measured as a function of the number of qubits in the chain … the value presented in the Details section / a circuit with a Hadamard gate
examples.translation: 체인 내 큐비트 수의 함수로 측정된 … Details 섹션에 표시되는 값 … Hadamard gate와 단일 측정을 포함하는 회로
examples.suggested: 체인 내 qubit 수 … 세부 정보 섹션에 표시되는 값 … Hadamard Gate와 단일 측정을 포함하는 Circuit
examples.why: Three separate conventions break only in these two cards: qubit→큐비트 (elsewhere qubit/Qubit), "Details section"→Details 섹션 (elsewhere 세부 정보 섹션), circuit→회로 (elsewhere Circuit). Within-file inconsistency, not a meaning change.

examples.source: Backends also have properties that change whenever the backend is calibrated, such as qubit lifetime and operation error rates.
examples.translation: 백엔드는 교정될 때마다 qubit 수명 및 연산 오류율과 같이 변경되는 속성도 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 백엔드에는 qubit 수명이나 연산 오류율처럼 백엔드가 교정될 때마다 바뀌는 속성도 있습니다.
examples.why: The English "Backends also have properties that…" is carried over word-order-first, leaving 백엔드는 … 속성도 있습니다 (subject-marker where 백엔드에는 is required) and attaching 교정될 때마다 to the wrong clause. Grammatically parseable but not something a Korean technical writer would write.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — every load-bearing number and comparison survives intact (44% vs 95.3% logical Bell fidelity, the three BV configurations at 26/60/70 큐비트 with the "(iii)에서는 모든 구성 요소가 활성화되었을 때만 0이 아닌 성공 확률" caveat, "낮을수록 좋습니다" on logical error probability, and the "1보다 큰 값은 … 에너지 오차를 줄인다" reading of the VQE ratio), and no hallucinated sentence appears. Three editor-level slips: (1) "high-order, robust DD sequences" is rendered 고차원의 견고한 DD 시퀀스 — 고차원 means "high-dimensional", not "high-order", and the very next sentence renders "higher-order sequences" correctly as 고차 시퀀스, so the same concept is split two ways within one paragraph; (2) "without requiring the additional jobs typically needed for separate calibration and mitigation workflows" flattens to 추가 작업 없이, which reads as "without extra work" and loses that these are separate job submissions; (3) in workflow step 1, [Qiskit Functions Catalog]를 통해 is fronted so it scopes over both 정의하고 and 선택합니다, implying the circuit itself is defined through the Catalog, where the English attaches "through the Catalog" only to selecting Orbit. Register is consistent 합니다체 declaratives with 하세요 imperatives (사용하세요 / 읽어보세요) — no honorific-humble slips.

examples.source: In automated mode, users can seamlessly apply high-order, robust DD sequences without needing to select or configure them manually. Advanced users can instead experiment with available higher-order sequences...
examples.translation: 자동 모드에서는 사용자가 수동으로 선택하거나 구성할 필요 없이 고차원의 견고한 DD 시퀀스를 원활하게 적용할 수 있습니다. 고급 사용자는 대신 사용 가능한 고차 시퀀스로 실험하여...
examples.suggested: 고차(高次)의 견고한 DD 시퀀스
examples.why: 고차원 = 'high-dimensional', not 'high-order'; DD sequences (CPMG, XY8 …) are characterized by order. The next sentence already uses the correct 고차, so the same term is rendered two ways one line apart — recognizable, but an editor would unify on 고차.

examples.source: Orbit also provides instantaneous MEM without requiring the additional jobs typically needed for separate calibration and mitigation workflows.
examples.translation: Orbit은 또한 별도의 교정 및 완화 워크플로우에 일반적으로 필요한 추가 작업 없이 즉각적인 MEM을 제공합니다.
examples.suggested: … 일반적으로 필요한 추가 작업(job) 제출 없이 …
examples.why: 'jobs' here are extra quantum job submissions (the calibration runs MEM normally needs); 추가 작업 reads as generic 'extra work', dropping the concrete point that no separate job is queued. A dropped qualifier, not a false claim.

examples.source: 1. Define a quantum circuit and select Orbit through the Qiskit Functions Catalog.
examples.translation: 1. [Qiskit Functions Catalog](…)를 통해 양자 회로를 정의하고 Orbit을 선택합니다.
examples.suggested: 양자 회로를 정의한 뒤 [Qiskit Functions Catalog]를 통해 Orbit을 선택합니다.
examples.why: Fronting 'Catalog를 통해' makes it govern both verbs, suggesting the circuit is defined inside the Catalog; in the English the Catalog qualifies only the selection of Orbit.

editor_note: Delta entry 64 is the benchmark table: all six data rows are byte-identical to the English (verified by diff — qubit counts 16/20/30/32/36/40, exact matrix sizes up to 6,009,350,400, E(diff) 0.08–1.20 mHa, iteration counts and times all preserved), and the header row is rendered in correct, idiomatic Korean ("화학 시스템", "큐비트 수", "정확한 행렬 크기", "정확값과의 E(diff) (mHa)", "반복 횟수", "QPU 런타임 사용량"). No quantity swap, no invented column, nothing a native technical editor would change in this entry. (Out of scope for this delta and for the deterministic leak sweep: the surrounding prose keeps "Qubit" in English, e.g. "16개 Qubit", while this header uses "큐비트".)

Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked every prose paragraph including the last 40% (coupling map directionality, the SWAP/CX-triple remark, the `ecr` vs `cx` default-basis-gate discussion, and the closing `VF2PostLayout` sentence "동일한 물리적 Qubit을 사용하여 처음에 찾은 것과 동일한 Circuit이 생성됩니다"), and found no inverted condition, swapped quantity, dropped caveat or hallucinated claim. The defects are editorial. First, "기본" is overloaded to carry four distinct English words: "기본 구성" (default configuration), "기본 트랜스파일 알고리즘" for *underlying* algorithms (line 46 — reads as "default algorithms"), "기본 기저 Gate" (default basis gates) and, in the very same admonition, "기본 Gate 및 연산 목록" for *native* gates and operations (line 180) — the conventional rendering is 네이티브 게이트, and using 기본 blurs native against default one sentence after the default-basis-gate discussion. Second, the register convention is broken in the opposite direction from usual: the file is almost entirely 합니다체, with exactly two 해요체 slips ("여러 예제를 살펴봐요", lines 49 and 60), so it is neither consistently 해요체 nor consistently formal. Third, a couple of calques ("Circuit의 연결성을 존중하기 때문에" for "respects the circuit's connectivity"; "Note that…" flattened to the imperative "…확인하세요") read as translated rather than written.

examples.source: See the list of possible native gates and operations for more details.
examples.translation: 자세한 내용은 가능한 [기본 Gate 및 연산 목록](/guides/qpu-information#native-gates)을 참조하세요.
examples.suggested: 자세한 내용은 [네이티브 Gate 및 연산 목록](...)을 참조하세요.
examples.why: "native" is rendered 기본, the same word the surrounding sentences use for "default" (기본 기저 Gate). Within one admonition the reader sees 기본 Gate meaning both "default gate" and "native gate", losing the distinction the page is drawing between calibrated defaults and the hardware's native set.

examples.source: Because many of the underlying transpilation algorithms are stochastic, there is no guarantee that a better circuit will be found.
examples.translation: 기본 트랜스파일 알고리즘 중 다수가 확률론적이기 때문에, 더 나은 Circuit이 발견된다는 보장은 없습니다.
examples.suggested: 트랜스파일에 사용되는 내부 알고리즘 중 다수가 확률론적이기 때문에, ...
examples.why: "underlying" becomes 기본, which a Korean reader parses as "default" — implying the caveat applies only to the default algorithms rather than to the transpilation machinery in general. Not misleading enough to change what the learner does, but the qualifier is wrong.

examples.source: This page shows several examples of passing QPU information to the transpiler. / This topic shows several examples of passing information to the transpiler.
examples.translation: 이 페이지에서는 QPU 정보를 Transpiler에 전달하는 여러 예제를 살펴봐요. / 이 항목에서는 Transpiler에 정보를 전달하는 여러 예제를 살펴봐요.
examples.suggested: ... 여러 예제를 살펴봅니다. (or convert the whole file to 해요체)
examples.why: These are the only two 해요체 sentences in a file that is otherwise uniformly 합니다체, so the voice audibly jumps twice. Either ending is defensible on its own; the inconsistency is the defect.

examples.source: Because this layout respects the circuit's connectivity, there are no SWAP gates, providing a much better circuit for execution.
examples.translation: 이 레이아웃은 Circuit의 연결성을 존중하기 때문에 SWAP Gate가 없으며, 실행에 훨씬 더 좋은 Circuit을 제공합니다.
examples.suggested: 이 레이아웃이 Circuit의 연결 구조와 맞아떨어지기 때문에 SWAP Gate가 필요 없고, 실행하기에 훨씬 유리한 Circuit이 됩니다.
