(1) The course name is rendered two ways inside one short file: the frontmatter description says '실용적인 양자 컴퓨팅' while the title and body both say '실전 양자 컴퓨팅'; the rest of this course directory uses 실전 양자 컴퓨팅 (7 occurrences vs 2), so the description should follow it. (2) Register: the body prose is uniformly 합니다체 rather than the project's 해요체 convention, and line 22 escalates to a 하십시오체 imperative ('준비가 되었는지 확인하십시오') where the English is a plain advisory 'Make sure you're ready'; '확인해 보세요' would fit the teaching voice. The legal NOTICE paragraph correctly stays formal, and '축하드립니다' is idiomatic and not worth changing.

examples.source: Quantum computing in practice
examples.translation: 실용적인 양자 컴퓨팅 (description) vs 실전 양자 컴퓨팅 (title, body)
examples.suggested: 실전 양자 컴퓨팅 in both places
examples.why: The course's proper name is split into two renderings within the same file; the rest of this course directory consistently uses 실전 양자 컴퓨팅.

examples.source: Make sure you're ready to take the exam.
examples.translation: 시험을 치를 준비가 되었는지 확인하십시오.
examples.suggested: 시험을 치를 준비가 되었는지 확인해 보세요.
examples.why: 하십시오체 imperative against the file's 해요체 convention, and stiffer than the English's plain advisory tone.

examples.source: …you can take the badging exam… your badge will automatically be sent…
examples.translation: …배지 시험을 치를 수 있습니다. … 배지가 자동으로 전송됩니다.
examples.suggested: …치를 수 있어요. … 자동으로 전송돼요.
examples.why: Body prose is uniformly 합니다체 rather than the 해요체 teaching register used across the course — consistent, but off-convention.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the 100+ qubit scope, the "recommended background" framing, the exam/Credly sequence and the full privacy notice all match the English with no drift, softening or invention, so nothing here misleads a learner. What a native editor would change: (1) the "Awarded Badge" heading is rendered 수상한 배지, which reads as "prize-winning" and is a homograph of 수상하다 "suspicious"; a digital credential is 획득한 배지 or 수여된 배지. (2) "course" is split within the file — 강좌 in the intro and background sections but 과정 twice in the Exam section. (3) Register slips out of the file's own 합니다체/해요체 into 하십시오체 with 시험을 치르십시오 in the Exam paragraph. (4) "we recommend a familiarity with…" is calqued as 친숙함을 권장합니다, a noun-form a Korean technical writer would render as ~에 익숙할 것을 권장합니다.

examples.source: ## Awarded Badge
examples.translation: ## 수상한 배지
examples.suggested: ## 획득한 배지
examples.why: 수상(受賞) is winning a prize, not earning a credential, and 수상한 is also the everyday word for "suspicious" — an unfortunate reading for a badge heading.

examples.source: course (throughout)
examples.translation: 강좌 (intro, 권장 배경 지식) vs 과정 ("실전 양자 컴퓨팅" 과정의 배지…, 이 과정의 강의)
examples.suggested: pick one — 강좌 throughout, or 과정 throughout
examples.why: The same referent is named two ways within one short page; the concept stays identifiable, so this is a consistency slip rather than a meaning problem.

examples.source: take the exam at IBM® Training
examples.translation: IBM® Training에서 시험을 치르십시오.
examples.suggested: IBM® Training에서 시험을 치르세요.
examples.why: 하십시오체 imperative breaks the file's own informal-instructional register (cf. 알아보세요 in the description).

examples.source: we recommend a familiarity with quantum information and quantum circuits
examples.translation: 양자 정보 및 양자 회로에 대한 친숙함을 권장합니다
examples.suggested: 양자 정보와 양자 회로에 익숙할 것을 권장합니다
examples.why: Nominalizing "familiarity" as 친숙함 is an English-shaped construction; Korean technical prose uses a verbal clause here.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — depth-as-game, ZNE ("이미 존재하는 노이즈 위에 노이즈를 추가"), PEC's non-level-3 caveat and its exponential run-time, and the "spending more computational effort doesn't always improve the output circuit" hedge all survive intact, so nothing here teaches a false concept. The defects are consistency: "error mitigation" is 오류 완화 in the overview and error-suppression sections (lines 27, 165) but switches wholesale to 오류 경감 from the Execute section on (174, 180, 182, 194); "utility-scale" is 유틸리티 규모 in the frontmatter/overview/conclusion but 실용 규모 at line 111; "classical" alternates 고전 (고전 레지스터, 고전적 후처리) and 클래식 (클래식 컴퓨터, line 111); "lesson" is 레슨 except 수업 at line 117; and headings are half-translated (맵(Map), 최적화(Optimize), 후처리) and half not (Execute, Conclusion). One small referential drift: "as we'll discuss later in the lesson" (about heavy-hex topology) becomes "이후 레슨에서 자세히 다룰 예정입니다", pointing the reader at a future lesson instead of later in this one. Register is 합니다체 with two 시- honorific slips at line 69.

examples.source: they also abstract error suppression and mitigation away from the user … The Execute step is also when we can select *error mitigation* strategy.
examples.translation: 오류 억제 및 경감을 사용자로부터 추상화합니다 … Execute 단계에서는 *오류 경감(error mitigation)* 전략도 선택할 수 있습니다
examples.suggested: 오류 완화 (matching lines 27 and 165, where 오류 완화(error mitigation) is already glossed)
examples.why: The same term is rendered 오류 완화 in the first half of the file and 오류 경감 in the second; both are glossed with the English so the concept stays identifiable, but a learner reading straight through sees two names for one technique.

examples.source: before going straight for a utility-scale project
examples.translation: 실용 규모 프로젝트에 바로 도전하기 전에
examples.suggested: 유틸리티 규모 프로젝트에 바로 도전하기 전에
examples.why: 'utility-scale' is the course's key framing term and is 유틸리티 규모 everywhere else in this file (description, lesson overview, conclusion); 실용 규모 reads as an unrelated 'practical scale'.

examples.source: This connectivity — the so-called *topology* — of our processors is an important factor to consider when designing a circuit, as we'll discuss later in the lesson.
examples.translation: 이 연결성, 즉 프로세서의 *토폴로지(topology)*는 회로를 설계할 때 중요하게 고려해야 할 요소로, 이후 레슨에서 자세히 다룰 예정입니다.
examples.suggested: … 이 레슨 뒷부분에서 자세히 다룰 예정입니다.
examples.why: 'later in the lesson' becomes 'in later lessons'; topology is in fact taken up again in the Map/Optimize sections of this same lesson, so the pointer sends the reader to the wrong place.

examples.source: So, for those of you just getting started, you came in at the perfect time! For those of you that are already familiar with Qiskit…
examples.translation: 이제 막 시작하시는 분들께는 최적의 시기에 입문하신 것입니다! 이미 Qiskit에 익숙하신 분들은…
examples.suggested: 이제 막 시작한 분들은 딱 좋은 시기에 들어온 거예요! Qiskit에 이미 익숙한 분들은…
examples.why: Honorific 시-/드리는 style (…하시는 분들께는, 입문하신 것입니다) is the deferential register the file otherwise avoids; the rest of the lesson keeps a plain instructional tone.

examples.source: This typically involves unrolling custom instructions and converting the circuit to just single- and two-qubit gates.
examples.translation: 일반적으로 사용자 지정 명령어를 풀어헤치고 Circuit을 단일 및 이중 Qubit Gate로 변환하는 작업을 포함합니다.
examples.suggested: 일반적으로 사용자 지정 명령어를 전개(unroll)하고 …
examples.why: '풀어헤치다' is colloquial ('to undo/unravel clothing') and is not how a Korean quantum engineer writes about transpiler unrolling; 전개 or 언롤링 is the conventional rendering.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I found no inverted condition, swapped quantity or hallucinated sentence, and the technically dense passages (Trotter 1차/2차 공식의 역순 곱, ZNE 3단계, PEA vs PEC 샘플링 오버헤드, TLS 결함으로 인한 재냉각) all land correctly. What a native editor would change: (1) "quantum dynamics" is rendered as 양자 역학 (= quantum mechanics) at lines 24 and 26 instead of 양자 동역학, blurring the lesson's actual subject in its opening paragraph; (2) boson appears as both 보존 (76, 92, 94) and 보손 (98, 99), and 보존 collides with its other sense in this same file — line 309 uses 보존 to mean "preserving" the noise bias, and 제약 at line 335 (pharmaceuticals) collides with 제약 = constraint used at 161/235; (3) decoherence splits into 결어긋남 (204) and 결맞음 상실 (253), two-qubit gate into 이중 Qubit Gate (235, 239) and 2-Qubit Gate (317), observables into 관측값 (105, 180) and 관측량 (280). Also two flattened emphases (the utility paper's "beyond the reach of brute-force classical simulation" softened to 처리하기 어려운; "especially in scenarios where" turned into 이는 …에서도 유효합니다), the heading 오류 완화 간주 for "Error mitigation interlude" (간주 reads as "regard as", not "interlude"), and a lone 해요체 slip 되길 바라요 at line 339 in an otherwise consistent 합니다체 document.

examples.source: how quantum computers are used to solve quantum dynamics problems—specifically, how they help us understand the time-evolution of a quantum system
examples.translation: 양자 컴퓨터가 양자 역학 문제, 특히 양자 시스템의 시간 진화를 이해하는 데 어떻게 활용되는지
examples.suggested: 양자 컴퓨터가 양자 동역학 문제를 푸는 데, 특히 양자 시스템의 시간 진화를 이해하는 데 …
examples.why: 양자 역학 = quantum mechanics (the whole theory); the lesson is specifically about quantum dynamics (time evolution), 양자 동역학. Same substitution recurs at line 26 for 'simulating quantum dynamics'. Recognizable but imprecise in the sentence that defines the lesson's scope.

examples.source: whether the system involves fermions or bosons
examples.translation: 시스템이 페르미온인지 보존인지 판단하는 것이 중요합니다 … (후반) 페르미온이나 보손과 같이 구별할 수 없는 입자
examples.suggested: 보손 throughout
examples.why: Boson is rendered 보존 in the first half and 보손 in the second. 보존 is additionally the file's own word for 'preservation' — line 309 reads 잡음 편향 보존 ('preserving the noise bias') — so the earlier 보존 is momentarily ambiguous. Within-file inconsistency, not concept-destroying.

examples.source: short decoherence times / two-qubit gate / expectation values of observables
examples.translation: 결어긋남 시간 … 결맞음 상실(decoherence) / 이중 Qubit Gate … 2-Qubit Gate / 관측값의 기댓값 … 관측량의 기댓값
examples.suggested: pick one each: 결어긋남(decoherence), 2-Qubit Gate, 관측량(observable)
examples.why: Three core terms each rendered two ways inside one lesson; 관측값 additionally reads as 'measured value' rather than 'observable', which is the operator being measured.

examples.source: can produce accurate expectation values for quantum circuits that lie beyond the reach of brute-force classical simulation methods
examples.translation: 무차별 대입 방식의 고전적 시뮬레이션 방법으로는 처리하기 어려운 양자 Circuit에 대해 정확한 기댓값을 계산할 수 있다
examples.suggested: … 고전적 시뮬레이션 방법의 한계를 넘어서는 양자 Circuit에 대해 …
examples.why: 'beyond the reach of' (out of reach) is softened to 처리하기 어려운 ('hard to handle'). The utility paper's central claim is weakened, though the learner still gets the right direction — dropped force, not a false statement.

examples.source: quantum computers can be used to verify or compare results with approximate classical simulation methods … especially in scenarios where the exact solution is unknown beforehand
examples.translation: …비교하는 데 활용할 수 있음을 보여주었다는 점에서 특히 중요합니다. 이는 정확한 해가 미리 알려져 있지 않은 상황에서도 유효합니다.
examples.suggested: …특히 정확한 해를 미리 알 수 없는 상황에서 그렇습니다.
examples.why: EN says the verification role matters *most* where no exact answer exists; KO demotes it to 'this also holds even there'. The emphasis that makes the point pedagogically interesting is flattened.

examples.source: Error mitigation interlude / Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE)
examples.translation: 오류 완화 간주 / 변분 양자 고유값 분해기(VQE)
examples.suggested: 오류 완화 막간 설명 (or 잠깐: 오류 완화 짚고 가기) / 변분 양자 고유값 솔버(VQE)
examples.why: As a standalone heading 간주 reads as 간주하다 ('to regard as'), not 'interlude'. 고유값 분해기 suggests an eigen-decomposition device rather than an eigensolver; 솔버/계산기 is the convention.

examples.source: we hope that you can now use this video and tutorial as a guide for even more simulation problems
examples.translation: 이 영상과 튜토리얼이 더 많은 시뮬레이션 문제를 다루는 데 좋은 지침이 되길 바라요.
examples.suggested: …좋은 지침이 되기를 바랍니다.
examples.why: The whole document is consistent 합니다체; this final bullet alone drops into 해요체 (바라요), which reads as an abrupt tonal break at the summary's close.

editor_note: Judging only the re-written entry (the page title/sidebar_label "Utility-scale QAOA" → "유틸리티 스케일 QAOA"): the meaning is faithful and nothing about it would mislead a learner — "유틸리티 스케일" is a recognizable transliteration of the IBM "utility-scale" framing. The one defect is internal inconsistency: this same compound is rendered "유틸리티 규모" everywhere else in the file, including the frontmatter `description` two lines above it ("Max-Cut 문제의 유틸리티 규모 예제"), the intro ("유틸리티 규모 QAOA에 관한 비디오"), the video title, and the closing section heading "유틸리티 규모에서". So the page's H1/sidebar label uses 스케일 while the body it heads uses 규모 throughout. Aligning the title to "유틸리티 규모 QAOA" (or switching the body) would fix it; the concept stays perfectly identifiable either way, so this is MINOR, not a FAIL.

examples.source: Utility-scale QAOA
examples.translation: 유틸리티 스케일 QAOA
examples.suggested: 유틸리티 규모 QAOA
examples.why: The rest of the file — including the `description` field directly above ("유틸리티 규모 예제"), the opening sentence ("유틸리티 규모 QAOA에 관한 비디오"), and the final heading "유틸리티 규모에서" — consistently renders utility-scale as 유틸리티 규모. Using 유틸리티 스케일 only in the title/sidebar label splits the term between the page's label and its own body; not misleading, but a native technical editor would unify it.

editor_note: Meaning is fully faithful — nothing here would mislead a learner: the exam facts ("20문제로 구성되어 있으며 합격하려면 최소 16문제를 맞혀야 합니다", "두 번의 시도에서 합격 점수를 받지 못하면 시험이 일시적으로 잠깁니다"), the maintenance notice, and the entire Credly privacy paragraph are complete and correctly conditioned, with no dropped caveat or added claim. Two things an editor would still change. First, "course" is rendered two ways in the same short file: 강좌 in the heading and body ("강좌 후 설문조사", "이 강좌의 학습 및 활동을 완료한 후") but 과정 in the survey paragraph ("이 과정을 완료하신 것을 축하드립니다", "저희가 과정을 개선하는 데") — unify to 강좌. Second, the survey paragraph slips out of the 해요체 convention into humble/합쇼체 forms, "축하드립니다" and "…도움을 주시기 바랍니다", while line 22 correctly uses "확인하세요"; 축하해요/도와주세요 style would restore consistency.

examples.source: Congratulations on completing this course! … help us improve our course … After completing the reading and activities in this course
examples.translation: 이 과정을 완료하신 것을 축하드립니다! … 저희가 과정을 개선하는 데 … 이 강좌의 학습 및 활동을 완료한 후
examples.suggested: 이 강좌를 완료하신 것을 축하해요! … 저희가 강좌를 개선하는 데 …
examples.why: The same source term "course" is rendered 과정 in one paragraph and 강좌 two lines later (and in the section heading 강좌 후 설문조사). Not confusing, but a native technical editor would pick one and keep it — 강좌 already carries the headings.

examples.source: Congratulations on completing this course! Please take a moment to help us improve our course by filling out the following quick survey.
examples.translation: 이 과정을 완료하신 것을 축하드립니다! 다음 간단한 설문조사를 작성하여 저희가 과정을 개선하는 데 도움을 주시기 바랍니다.
examples.suggested: 이 강좌를 완료하신 것을 축하해요! 다음 간단한 설문조사를 작성해서 저희가 강좌를 개선하도록 도와주세요.
examples.why: 드리 (축하드립니다) and 주시기 바랍니다 are humble/합쇼체, off the file's 해요체 convention, which line 22 ("…준비가 되었는지 확인하세요") does follow. A formal-register slip only — meaning is unaffected.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat; the Credly/IBM privacy notice and the exam/badge flow ("시험에 합격하면 Credly로부터 배지를 획득했다는 알림을 받게 됩니다") track the English clause for clause, and 대각화 / 스케일링 / 배지 are used consistently. Two things a native technical editor would change: "양자 알고리즘을 동기 부여한 방법" (line 12) is a calque of "methods that motivated the quantum algorithms" — 동기 부여하다 in Korean is about motivating people, and the rendering also drops the fact that these are still 고전적 방법; and "학습자는 … 완료할 것을 권장합니다" (line 18) mis-marks the subject, since the recommender is "we", not 학습자. Register is standard doc-style 합니다체 with -세요 imperatives (설정하세요 / 시도해 보세요), consistent and appropriate; no 드리- humble forms.

examples.source: Some background is provided on the classical methods that are used, or that motivated the quantum algorithms.
examples.translation: 사용되는 고전적 방법과 양자 알고리즘을 동기 부여한 방법에 대한 약간의 배경이 제공됩니다.
examples.suggested: 사용되는 고전적 방법, 그리고 양자 알고리즘의 계기가 된 고전적 방법에 대한 배경 지식을 어느 정도 제공합니다.
examples.why: 동기 부여하다 is used for motivating people, not for one method inspiring an algorithm — reads as machine-translated 'motivated'. The second noun phrase also loses '고전적', so the reader may take it as a separate, non-classical category.

examples.source: We recommend that learners complete the following prerequisites prior to this course:
examples.translation: 학습자는 이 과정을 시작하기 전에 다음 사전 준비를 완료할 것을 권장합니다.
examples.suggested: 이 과정을 시작하기 전에 학습자가 다음 사전 준비를 완료할 것을 권장합니다.
examples.why: With 학습자는 as topic, 권장합니다 reads as though the learners are doing the recommending; the recommender in the source is 'we'. Marking 학습자가 inside the embedded clause fixes it.

editor_note: All 7 delta entries are faithful, natural and locally term-consistent: the a/the distinction in entry 49 is solved idiomatically ("__그__ 크릴로프 부분공간" vs "__어떤__ 크릴로프 부분공간"), the space/subspace clarification keeps EN's hedge ("크릴로프 __공간__이라는 표현도 타당하다"), entry 116 preserves the caveat and the figure ("계산을 다시 실행하면 답이 달라질 수 있지만 … 대략 차원 80~85"), and entry 265 renders "and the corresponding minimal value is" correctly as "그리고 이에 대응하는 최솟값은". Entries 114/116 use "Krylov 방법" while 49/56/59 use "크릴로프 방법", but each matches its surrounding section's existing convention, so it is not a new inconsistency. OUT-OF-DELTA note for the maintainer (not counted in the verdict): in Appendix II the entry immediately BEFORE entry 265 — EN is the bare connector "is" — is rendered as "이고, 이에 대응하는 최솟값은", so the Korean labels the minimizing polynomial $p^*(x)$ as "the corresponding minimal value" and then repeats the same phrase for $\beta(a,b,d)$; it should be a plain "…의 해는 … 이고," (KO line ~1799). That entry was not rewritten in this round and did not drive this verdict.

All five delta entries are semantically faithful — no drift, no hallucination: entry 43 keeps the "click the triangles to reveal the solutions" instruction intact (삼각형을 클릭하여 정답을 확인하세요), entry 48 preserves the hedge "there may be other valid answers" (다른 타당한 답변이 있을 수 있지만), and entry 50 correctly carries both the quantity claim and its cause ("QPU 시간이 훨씬 적게 필요합니다 … Hadamard 테스트를 통한 행렬 요소의 값비싼 계산을 피하기 때문에"). The only editorial slip is register inconsistency between the two sibling AccordionItem question titles: entry 44 ends in the softer 해요체-adjacent "…무엇을 할 수 있을까요?" while entry 47 ends in the 하십시오체 "…무엇입니까?" — a native editor would harmonize the two quiz prompts (e.g. "…주요 장점은 무엇일까요?"). Nothing here would mislead a learner.

examples.source: What are the principal advantages to SKQD over (a) SQD, and (b) KQD?
examples.translation: SKQD가 (a) SQD와 (b) KQD에 비해 갖는 주요 장점은 무엇입니까?
examples.suggested: SKQD가 (a) SQD와 (b) KQD에 비해 갖는 주요 장점은 무엇일까요?
examples.why: The sibling quiz title two lines above uses the softer '…무엇을 할 수 있을까요?'; '무엇입니까' is 하십시오체 and clashes with the page's 해요체 quiz convention. Meaning is unaffected.

examples.source: (b) SKQD requires much less QPU time, because it avoids the costly calculation of matrix elements via the Hadamard test.
examples.translation: (b) SKQD는 Hadamard 테스트를 통한 행렬 요소의 값비싼 계산을 피하기 때문에 QPU 시간이 훨씬 적게 필요합니다.
examples.suggested: (no change)
examples.why: Checked as a drift candidate and it is clean: comparative degree ('much less' → 훨씬 적게), the causal link, and 'matrix elements' → 행렬 요소 are all preserved; the sentence is not softened or inverted.

editor_note: The opening paragraph of §4 ("Sampling the LUCJ ansatz in the computational basis generates a pool of noisy configurations…") is left entirely in English — it is the only place the post-processing chain is explained (noisy pool χ̃ → configuration recovery → subsampling into batches → each batch defines a subspace S^(k) → H projected onto it), so a Korean-only reader gets none of it and then meets "각 투영된 해밀토니안 …" referring to a projection the Korean text never set up. Core terminology also splits: "ground state" is 바닥 상태 in §1–4 but 기저 상태 from §4.1 on (14 occurrences), and 기저 상태 is simultaneously used for "basis state" ("계산 기저 상태와 그 진폭", §4.1), so "추정된 기저 상태" is readable as "estimated basis state" in the very passage where the two ideas sit side by side. "orbital" likewise splits 궤도 (59×) / 오비탈 (8×, all inside §4.1), including 스핀 궤도 vs 스핀 오비탈 for the same object. Smaller slips: "Givens rotation" → 기번스 회전 (should be 기븐스), Fock space → 폭 공간 (conventional 포크 공간; 폭 reads as "width"), and §4.3 drops the hedge in "can be attributed to" → "…에 기인합니다".

examples.source: Sampling the LUCJ ansatz in the computational basis generates a pool of noisy configurations $\tilde{\mathcal{\chi}}$ … Each batch of samples defines a subspace ($\mathcal{S^{(k)}}$). Next, the molecular Hamiltonian, $H$, is projected onto subspaces:
examples.translation: (untranslated — the full English paragraph is shipped verbatim in the Korean page)
examples.suggested: 계산 기저에서 LUCJ 앤자츠를 샘플링하면 후처리 루틴에 사용되는 잡음 섞인 구성들의 풀 $\tilde{\mathcal{\chi}}$가 생성됩니다. 여기에는 전자 수가 틀린 구성을 확률적으로 보정하는 _구성 복구_(자세한 내용은 뒤에서 설명)라는 방법이 포함됩니다. 그런 다음 전자 수가 올바른 구성 $\tilde{\mathcal{\chi}}_{R}$만 서브샘플링되어, 고유한 각 구성의 출현 빈도에 따라 여러 배치로 나뉩니다. 각 샘플 배치는 하나의 부분 공간($\mathcal{S^{(k)}}$)을 정의합니다. 다음으로 분자 해밀토니안 $H$를 각 부분 공간에 투영합니다:
examples.why: This is the only prose in the lesson that defines the whole SQD post-processing chain and introduces the projection; leaving it in English removes the setup that the next Korean sentence ('각 투영된 해밀토니안 …') depends on.

examples.source: the estimated ground states from them are … Using the computational basis states and their amplitudes …
examples.translation: 추정된 기저 상태가 다음과 같다고 가정합니다 … 계산 기저 상태와 그 진폭을 이용하여 …
examples.suggested: 추정된 바닥 상태 … / 계산 기저 상태 … (bring §4.1–4.3 back to 바닥 상태 for ground state, as in §1–§4 and the section title '바닥 상태 에너지')
examples.why: Ground state switches from 바닥 상태 to 기저 상태 at §4.1 while 기저 상태 also renders 'basis state' two lines later, so the same phrase carries two different concepts in adjacent sentences.

examples.source: Each bit in a bitstring (Slater determinant) represents a spin orbital … average orbital occupancy
examples.translation: 각 비트는 스핀 오비탈을 나타냅니다 … 평균 오비탈 점유 (vs. elsewhere: 스핀 궤도, 평균 궤도 점유율)
examples.suggested: 스핀 궤도 / 평균 궤도 점유율 (use the 궤도 convention that dominates the file, 59× vs 8×)
examples.why: 'orbital' is rendered 궤도 everywhere except §4.1, where it silently becomes 오비탈, so the reader must map two labels onto one object mid-explanation.

examples.source: 2-qubit Given's rotation gates ($XX + YY$ gates) … the Fock space of fermions in M spatial orbitals
examples.translation: 2-Qubit 기번스 회전 Gate($XX + YY$ Gates) … M개의 공간 궤도에서 페르미온의 폭 공간
examples.suggested: 기븐스 회전 게이트 … 포크 공간
examples.why: 기번스 is a misspelling of the standard 기븐스 (Givens), and 폭 공간 reads first as 'width space' to a Korean engineer; 포크 공간 is the conventional rendering of Fock space.

examples.source: This gap can be attributed to the small subspace dimension we used above for projection and diagonalization.
examples.translation: 이 차이는 투영 및 대각화에 사용한 작은 부분 공간 차원에 기인합니다.
examples.suggested: 이 차이는 투영 및 대각화에 사용한 작은 부분 공간 차원 때문으로 볼 수 있습니다.
examples.why: 'can be attributed to' is a hedge; '기인합니다' asserts the cause outright, slightly strengthening the claim.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — every numeric claim (2951 Pauli 항 → 1187 그룹, 10^5–10^7 샷, 49%/1%/0.01%, -0.5357 vs -0.2111 vs -1.4267), the crucial negation in "정확한 바닥 상태에서 준비하고 샘플링하지 **않는** 것이 오히려 유리한 경우가 많습니다", and the upper-bound claim ("추정된 에너지는 실제 바닥 상태 에너지보다 결코 낮아지지 않습니다") all survive intact, with no hallucinated sentence. What a native technical editor would change is consistency and phrasing: the key concept "support" is rendered three ways in one file — "_지지_" (§2 note), bare English "support" (all of §3), and "지지"/"지지 영역" again in §4–§6; "noise" alternates between "잡음 허용성" (§2.3) and "노이즈 내성" elsewhere; "Lesson" alternates between "강의 4/강의 5" (§3) and "레슨 5" (§5 table); "pre-fault-tolerant" is "결함 허용 이전" in §3 but the looser "오류 내성이 없는" in the §5 table. Additionally "minimum/lowest eigenvalue" is consistently the stiff calque "최솟값 고유값" where a Korean quantum writer would write "최소 고유값", and §2 has a lone 해요체 outlier ("살펴봐요") in an otherwise uniform -습니다 file. None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: the subspace must be in _support_ of our target (for example, ground) eigenstate … which must be in _support of the target state_ … to prepare and sample from ground state support
examples.translation: 부분 공간은 목표(예: 바닥) 고유 상태의 _지지_ 안에 있어야 합니다 … 이 벡터들은 반드시 _목표 상태의 support_ 안에 있어야 합니다 … 바닥 상태 지지 영역에서 준비하고 샘플링하기 위해
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering for the file's central concept — e.g. keep English "support" everywhere (with a one-time gloss), or use "지지(support)" consistently — rather than 지지 / support / 지지 영역.
examples.why: "Support" is the load-bearing concept of the whole lesson; splitting it three ways forces the learner to re-identify it in each section, though the concept stays recoverable.

examples.source: find the lowest eigenvalue … The ground state energy (minimum eigenvalue) … The minimum eigenvalue of the projected matrix
examples.translation: 최솟값 고유값
examples.suggested: 최소 고유값 (or 최저 고유값)
examples.why: "최솟값 고유값" stacks a noun ("minimum value") onto another noun and reads as literal MT; Korean linear-algebra writing uses "최소 고유값". It recurs about seven times, so the stiffness is pervasive.

examples.source: Samples from pre-fault tolerant quantum computers can be noisy. … VQE energy estimation is susceptible to noise from pre-fault-tolerant quantum computers.
examples.translation: 결함 허용 이전 양자 컴퓨터의 샘플은 노이즈가 있을 수 있습니다. … VQE 에너지 추정은 오류 내성이 없는 양자 컴퓨터의 노이즈에 취약합니다.
examples.suggested: Use 결함 허용 이전(pre-fault-tolerant) in both places.
examples.why: The same term is rendered two ways, and "오류 내성이 없는" ("having no error tolerance") is a weaker, slightly different claim than "pre-fault-tolerant" — recognizable, but not the established rendering.

examples.source: We will diagonalize the full matrix along with different projected versions ($H_\mathcal{S}$) for different subspaces to demonstrate the scalability and importance of the choice of subspace.
examples.translation: …부분 공간 선택의 확장성과 중요성을 살펴봐요.
examples.suggested: …살펴보겠습니다.
examples.why: A single 해요체 ending in a file that is otherwise uniformly -습니다/-겠습니다; the tonal jump is noticeable mid-lesson.

examples.source: Fortunately, we do not always need all the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a Hamiltonian $H$, and therefore, diagonalization of the full matrix is not required in many practical cases.
examples.translation: 다행히, 해밀토니안 $H$의 모든 고유값과 고유벡터가 항상 필요한 것은 아니므로, 실제 적용 사례에서 전체 행렬의 대각화는 필수적이지 않습니다.
examples.suggested: …많은 실제 적용 사례에서 전체 행렬의 대각화는 필요하지 않습니다.
examples.why: "in many practical cases" loses its quantifier and reads as a claim about practical cases in general — a dropped qualifier rather than a reversal, so the lesson's point still lands.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the variational principle (§1.5), the qubit-wise-commuting Estimator caveat (§2.2, including "ZZZZ와 ZZXX도 동시에 측정할 수 없음"), the O(1/ε) vs O(1/ε²) QPE/VQE comparison, and the four-group answer key all land correctly, so nothing inverts a condition or swaps a quantity. The defects are editorial: "the unitary operation of the ansatz" becomes "ansatz의 단일 연산" (§1.2), where 단일 = "single", not 유니타리 — the unitarity attribute is silently dropped; and core terms split within the file (해밀토니안 vs Latin "Hamiltonian" from §2.3 on, 파울리 vs "Pauli", 매개변수 vs 파라미터, 노이즈 vs 잡음, barren plateau as 황무지 고원 in §2.2 but 불모 고원 in §4.1). Two small content slips: the geometry answer adds "이를 변분 파라미터로 활용해야 합니다", a claim the English does not make and one that blurs the outer-loop geometry scan with the ansatz's θ; and §1.4's parenthetical is misattached — "목적 함수(일반적으로 최솟값)의 극값" reads as if the target function is a minimum, where the English marks the *extremum* as typically a minimum. Residual translationese is light ("그것이 들리는 것만큼 쉽지는 않습니다", "서로 교환 가능한 여러 그런 문자열"); register is uniform 합니다체 with no 드리-/honorific slips.

examples.source: We will call the unitary operation of the ansatz on the circuit $U_{\text{var}}(\vec{\theta_0})$.
examples.translation: ansatz의 단일 연산을 $U_{\text{var}}(\vec{\theta_0})$라고 부르겠습니다.
examples.suggested: ansatz가 Circuit에 가하는 유니타리 연산을 $U_{\text{var}}(\vec{\theta_0})$라고 부르겠습니다.
examples.why: 'unitary' is rendered as 단일 ('single'), a false friend; the unitarity of the ansatz operator — the property that makes it implementable as a circuit — disappears from the definition.

examples.source: We would need to introduce variables for inter-atomic spacing, and the angles between bonds. We would need to vary these.
examples.translation: 원자 간 거리와 결합 각도에 대한 변수를 도입하고 이를 변분 파라미터로 활용해야 합니다.
examples.suggested: 원자 간 거리와 결합 각도에 대한 변수를 도입하고, 이 값들을 변화시켜야 합니다.
examples.why: Adds a claim the English does not make: calling the geometry variables 변분 파라미터 conflates them with the ansatz parameters θ, whereas the very next sentence (correctly) says each geometry gives a *new* Hamiltonian and a *separate* optimization.

examples.source: A classical optimizer is any classical algorithm designed to find extrema of a target function (typically a minimum).
examples.translation: 고전 최적화기는 목적 함수(일반적으로 최솟값)의 극값을 찾기 위한 고전 알고리즘입니다.
examples.suggested: 고전 최적화기는 목적 함수의 극값(대개 최솟값)을 찾도록 설계된 고전 알고리즘입니다.
examples.why: The parenthetical is attached to 목적 함수 instead of 극값, so it reads as 'the target function (typically a minimum)' — the qualifier now modifies the wrong noun.

examples.source: Hamiltonian / Pauli / parameters / noise / barren plateaus
examples.translation: 해밀토니안 ↔ Hamiltonian; 파울리 ↔ Pauli; 매개변수 ↔ 파라미터; 노이즈 ↔ 잡음; 황무지 고원 ↔ 불모 고원
examples.suggested: Pick one per term across the file (해밀토니안, 파울리, 매개변수, 노이즈, 불모 고원).
examples.why: Five core terms each split two ways within one lesson; all remain recognizable, but §2.3 onward switches to Latin-script 'Hamiltonian' right after §1–2 established 해밀토니안, and 'barren plateau' changes name between §2.2 and §4.1 where §4.1 is explaining the same concept.

examples.source: this lesson / this course
examples.translation: 이 단원 / 이 강좌 / 이 코스 / 이 과정 / 이 강의
examples.suggested: Fix 단원 = lesson and 강좌 = course, and use them consistently.
examples.why: Four renderings for 'course' alone; worst in §2.3 where '이 과정에서 나중에 다룰 다른 알고리즘들' sits one sentence after 과정 was used for 'process' (이 과정이 유용할 수 있습니다), so the reader briefly parses 'course' as 'process'.

examples.source: That may sound easier than it is.
examples.translation: 그것이 들리는 것만큼 쉽지는 않습니다.
examples.suggested: 말처럼 쉬운 일은 아닙니다.
examples.why: Calqued on the English 'sound'; 들리다 for an abstract proposition is not how a Korean technical writer would phrase it. Same class: '서로 교환 가능한 여러 그런 문자열' (§2.2) for 'several such strings that commute'.

editor_note: No misleading drift: every quantitative and conditional claim survives intact (n ≥ log2(N) qubits, α = √105 / √270, "위상 인코딩은 Hadamard 레이어를 포함하여 Circuit 깊이가 2", the (0,2π] rescaling caveat, "ZZFM은 ZFM과 달리 고전 컴퓨터에서 계산하기 어려울 것으로 추정됩니다", and the neither-consistent-nor-inconsistent little-endian remark). The main defect is within-file inconsistency for the file's central term: "feature"/"feature map" is rendered four ways — 특징 매핑 (lines 19–29), 특성/특성 맵 (line 172 onward, and all headings from line 624), 피처 맵 (line 336, 521, and the heading "### $Z$ 피처 맵" at 719), and left untranslated as English "feature map"/"feature mapping" inside the very section that heading introduces (lines 721, 734, 736, 766, 780). Secondary slips: line 1028 renders "Transpilation is the process…" as "Transpiler는 … 변환하는 과정으로", naming the tool where the process is meant; line 864 inverts the agent in "단일 qubit 게이트에 작용하는 qubit 집합" (source: qubits acted on BY single-qubit gates); line 726 calls |0⟩^⊗N the "$N$-Qubit 기저 상태" where EN says ground state (바닥 상태), colliding with 계산 기저 상태 used for "basis state" elsewhere; line 225 leaves "Note that" as a bare stranded "주목하세요."; line 164 fuses two EN sentences so that α itself reads as the normalization condition.

examples.source: feature / feature map / feature mapping
examples.translation: 특징 매핑 (19-29) / 특성·특성 맵 (172, 624, 782, 850) / 피처 맵 (336, 521, 719) / untranslated "feature map", "feature mapping" (721, 734, 736, 766, 780)
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering for the whole file (특성 맵 / 특성 매핑, matching the headings at 624, 782, 850, 948) and use it everywhere, including inside the $Z$ section.
examples.why: The file's central term is split four ways, and the ZFM section's heading (피처 맵) does not even match the term used in its own body (feature map). Recognizable throughout, so MINOR, but a native technical editor would unify it.

examples.source: Transpilation is the process of converting the quantum circuit from a high-level abstraction to one that is ready to run on a real quantum computer
examples.translation: Transpiler는 양자 Circuit을 고수준 추상화에서 실제 양자 컴퓨터에서 실행 가능한 형태로 변환하는 과정으로, 하드웨어 제약 조건을 고려합니다.
examples.suggested: 트랜스파일(transpilation)은 양자 Circuit을 고수준 추상화에서 실제 양자 컴퓨터에서 실행 가능한 형태로 변환하는 과정이며, 이때 하드웨어 제약 조건을 고려합니다.
examples.why: The subject is swapped from the process to the tool, so the sentence literally defines the transpiler as being a process. The rest of the paragraph uses 트랜스파일 for the action, so the file is inconsistent with itself as well.

examples.source: the set of all qubit connectivities as determined by the feature map, including the set of qubits acted on by single-qubit gates
examples.translation: $\mathcal{I}$는 단일 qubit 게이트에 작용하는 qubit 집합을 포함하여, 특성 맵에 의해 결정되는 모든 qubit 연결성의 집합입니다
examples.suggested: $\mathcal{I}$는 단일 qubit 게이트가 작용하는 qubit 집합까지 포함하여, 특성 맵에 의해 결정되는 모든 qubit 연결성의 집합입니다
examples.why: The particle 에 reverses agent and patient: as written it says the qubits act on the single-qubit gates. The following example ({{0},{2,3}}) rescues the meaning, so it is a wording slip rather than a false claim.

examples.source: Here, α is a normalization constant to be determined from the data being encoded. This is the normalization condition imposed by quantum mechanics:
examples.translation: $\alpha$는 인코딩할 데이터로부터 결정되는 정규화 상수이며, 이는 양자역학에서 부과되는 정규화 조건입니다:
examples.suggested: $\alpha$는 인코딩할 데이터로부터 결정되는 정규화 상수입니다. 다음은 양자역학이 부과하는 정규화 조건입니다:
examples.why: Merging the two English sentences with -이며 makes α read as being the normalization condition, blurring the constant/condition distinction the lesson is drawing right before the displayed equation.

examples.source: Note that
examples.translation: 주목하세요.
examples.suggested: 다음에 주목하세요:
examples.why: "Note that" introducing the ⟨ψ|ψ⟩ equation becomes a stranded one-word sentence ending in a period; a Korean technical writer would end it with a colon so it clearly points at the equation that follows.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the exam facts (20문제 / 최소 16문제 / 두 번의 시도에서 합격 점수를 받지 못하면 일시적으로 잠깁니다), the maintenance notice (향후 며칠 동안 일시적으로 이용할 수 없을 수 있습니다) and the whole Credly privacy paragraph all match the English with no drift, dropped caveat or invented claim. Two editorial slips only: "course" is rendered two ways inside one short file — 강좌 in the heading and body (강좌 후 설문조사, 이 강좌의 학습 및 활동) but 코스 twice in the survey paragraph (이 코스를 완료하신, 저희 코스를 개선하는) — and that same survey paragraph drops out of the file's 해요체 register (…확인하세요, …받으세요) into 하십시오체-flavored 도움을 주시기 바랍니다. Neither would mislead a learner; both are what a native technical editor would change.

examples.source: Congratulations on completing this course! Please take a moment to help us improve our course …
examples.translation: 이 코스를 완료하신 것을 축하합니다! … 저희 코스를 개선하는 데 도움을 주시기 바랍니다.
examples.suggested: 이 강좌를 완료하신 것을 축하합니다! … 저희 강좌를 개선하는 데 도움을 주세요.
examples.why: "course" is 강좌 everywhere else in the file (heading 강좌 후 설문조사, body 이 강좌의 학습 및 활동) but becomes 코스 twice here; one file should keep one rendering.

examples.source: Please take a moment to help us improve our course by filling out the following quick survey.
examples.translation: 다음 간단한 설문조사를 작성하여 저희 코스를 개선하는 데 도움을 주시기 바랍니다.
examples.suggested: 다음 간단한 설문조사를 작성해서 저희 강좌를 개선하는 데 도움을 주세요.
examples.why: 주시기 바랍니다 is 하십시오체; the rest of the page holds 해요체 (시험을 치를 준비가 되었는지 확인하세요, 배지를 받으세요), so this paragraph reads a register above its neighbours.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination anywhere: the course blurb, the exam/badge instructions and the whole Credly privacy notice track the English clause by clause, and "variational quantum circuits" is correctly 변분 양자 회로. What a native technical editor would still change is (1) the term "machine learning" is spelled two ways inside this one file — 머신러닝 in the frontmatter description but 머신 러닝 three times in the body (the ko course corpus is itself split 41/30, so this file should at least be internally consistent); (2) two calques in the opening paragraph — "assume some familiarity" rendered as "친숙함도 가정합니다" (a native writer would write "어느 정도 익숙하다고 가정합니다") and "fit into existing machine learning workflows" rendered as "어떻게 적합할 수 있는지입니다", where 적합하다 ("be suitable for") misses the integrate-into sense and the trailing -지입니다 nominalization is stiff; (3) register is mixed — the body is 합니다체 throughout while the exam sentence switches to 해요체 ("시험을 치르세요"). None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: machine learning
examples.translation: 머신러닝 (description) / 머신 러닝 (body, 3x)
examples.suggested: pick one spelling and use it in both the frontmatter and the body
examples.why: Same core term spelled two ways within a single short file; internally inconsistent orthography for the course's own title concept.

examples.source: but will also assume some familiarity with these methods
examples.translation: 이러한 방법에 대한 어느 정도의 친숙함도 가정합니다
examples.suggested: 이러한 방법에 어느 정도 익숙하다고 가정합니다
examples.why: '친숙함을 가정하다' is a word-for-word calque of 'assume familiarity'; Korean technical writing nominalizes far less and would use an 익숙하다고 clause.

examples.source: The primary focus will be how quantum computing can fit into existing machine learning workflows.
examples.translation: 주된 초점은 양자 컴퓨팅이 기존 머신 러닝 워크플로에 어떻게 적합할 수 있는지입니다.
examples.suggested: 주로 양자 컴퓨팅을 기존 머신러닝 워크플로에 어떻게 접목할 수 있는지를 다룹니다.
examples.why: 적합하다 means 'be suitable for', not 'fit into / be integrated into'; combined with the '…어떻게 …인지입니다' copula ending the sentence reads as MT rather than as written Korean.

examples.source: take the exam at IBM Training
examples.translation: IBM Training에서 시험을 치르세요
examples.suggested: keep one register across the page (the body is 합니다체)
examples.why: Lone 해요체 imperative inside an otherwise uniformly 합니다체 page; a formal-register slip either way, not misleading.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the P_0 derivation, the 0.90^10 ≈ 35% answer, the "2-Qubit 깊이 100 초과는 시작 자체가 불가능", the (1-p)^N readout-error argument and the "커널 행렬의 차원은 피처 수가 아니라 훈련 데이터의 포인트 수에 의해 결정" claim all track the English exactly, with no inversion, hallucination or swapped quantity. What a native technical editor would still change: (1) "feature map" is rendered two ways in the same file — 특징 맵 in the introduction and the first example (lines 21, 34, 85, 290, 292) but 피처 맵 from the "전체 커널 행렬" section onward (lines 380, 624, 656, 818, 835), with "feature" itself likewise split 특징/피처; "matrix element/entry" is similarly split 원소 (lines 21, 85, 104, 311) vs 요소 (lines 520, 524, 818, 827). (2) One explanatory sentence is dropped: EN "Thus we must optimize our circuit for each data point pair" has no counterpart in line 405, so the "따라서 2단계와 3단계는 함께 수행됩니다" conclusion loses its stated reason. (3) The qualifier "from the same category" is dropped from the depth-experiment advice at line 296. (4) "to respect time on IBM quantum computers" is calqued as "시간을 존중하기 위해" (line 92) — a Korean writer would say 사용 시간을 아끼기 위해. (5) "error correction" is rendered 오류 수정 (line 822) where the field's term is 오류 정정 (오류 완화 for mitigation is correct elsewhere). (6) The step headings in the first worked example are left as "Step 1:/Step 2:/Step 4:" (lines 106, 157, 245) while every other section uses "1단계:/2단계:/4단계:". None of these would teach a learner anything false.

examples.source: feature map ... feature map
examples.translation: 특징 맵(feature mapping) $\Phi(\vec{x})$는 … / 이제 고전 데이터를 양자 Circuit으로 인코딩하고 매핑하기 위한 피처 맵을 생성합니다.
examples.suggested: Pick one and use it throughout — e.g. 특징 맵 everywhere (and 특징 for "feature"), or 피처 맵 everywhere.
examples.why: The same core concept is named 특징 맵 in the first half and 피처 맵 in the second, and "feature" alternates 특징/피처 within the same section; the concept stays identifiable, so this is a consistency slip rather than a misleading one.

examples.source: a single kernel matrix element … a single matrix element
examples.translation: 단일 커널 행렬 원소 … 단일 커널 행렬 요소
examples.suggested: Use 원소 consistently for matrix element/entry (it is the standard linear-algebra term in Korean).
examples.why: 원소 and 요소 are used interchangeably for the same object across sections, which makes the reader pause to check whether a new object was introduced.

examples.source: For each pair of data vectors $\vec{x}_i$ and $\vec{x}_j$, we create a different overlap circuit. Thus we must optimize our circuit for each data point pair. So steps 2 and 3 would be done together in the multiple iterations.
examples.translation: 데이터 벡터 쌍 $\vec{x}_i$와 $\vec{x}_j$ 각각에 대해 서로 다른 오버랩 Circuit을 생성합니다. 따라서 2단계와 3단계는 여러 번의 반복 안에서 함께 수행됩니다.
examples.suggested: … 서로 다른 오버랩 Circuit을 생성합니다. 따라서 데이터 포인트 쌍마다 Circuit을 다시 최적화해야 하며, 그래서 2단계와 3단계는 여러 번의 반복 안에서 함께 수행됩니다.
examples.why: The middle sentence — the actual reason steps 2 and 3 merge — is absent, so the conclusion arrives without its justification. Nothing false is asserted, but the explanation is thinner than the English.

examples.source: It is worth playing around with a few data points from the same category to see how low your depth must be to obtain good results.
examples.translation: 몇 가지 데이터 포인트를 가지고 깊이를 얼마나 낮추어야 좋은 결과를 얻을 수 있는지 실험해 보는 것이 좋습니다.
examples.suggested: 동일한 범주에 속한 데이터 포인트 몇 개를 가지고 깊이를 얼마나 낮추어야 좋은 결과를 얻을 수 있는지 실험해 보는 것이 좋습니다.
examples.why: "from the same category" is the point of the exercise — same-class points should overlap strongly, so they are the ones that reveal how depth degrades the zero-state probability. Dropping it leaves the advice vaguer, though not wrong.

examples.source: in order to respect time on IBM® quantum computers
examples.translation: IBM® 양자 컴퓨터의 시간을 존중하기 위해
examples.suggested: IBM® 양자 컴퓨터의 사용 시간을 아끼기 위해
examples.why: "시간을 존중하다" is a word-for-word calque; in Korean 존중 applies to people or principles, not machine time, and a technical writer would say 아끼다/절약하다.

examples.source: look forward to what will be possible in the era of error correction
examples.translation: 오류 수정 시대에 무엇이 가능해질지도 기대해 보세요
examples.suggested: 오류 정정 시대에 무엇이 가능해질지도 기대해 보세요
examples.why: The established Korean term for quantum error correction is 오류 정정 (양자 오류 정정); 오류 수정 reads as generic bug-fixing. Recognizable, but the wrong register for the field — and the file already uses the correct 오류 완화 for error mitigation.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, swapped quantities or hallucinated claims; the load-bearing passages (CNOT 리스트 확장이 "수평선의 존재 여부만 감지하는 것으로 충분한지", 60%→100% 정확도 서사, "완전히 수렴하지 않은 것으로 보입니다", 72개 자유 파라미터를 2~3배 줄이라는 권고) all track the English. The recurring defect is the calque "motivated → 동기화": "technically motivated" becomes "기술적으로 동기화된 임의의 순서" and "it is well motivated" becomes "잘 동기화되어 있습니다", where 동기화 in Korean means *synchronization*, so both sentences read as nonsense rather than "타당한 근거가 있다". Secondary: the layer sentence doubles itself ("각각 고유한 목적을 가진 몇 개의 레이어로 식별할 수 있는 소수의 레이어를 가진 VQC"), and core terms split within the file — 매개변수(15)/파라미터(8), 최적화기(5)/옵티마이저(1), 컨볼루션 레이어/합성곱 레이어. Register is consistent 합니다체, matching the rest of the ko locale, so not counted against it.

examples.source: One could have multiple variational and/or encoding layers in any order that is technically motivated.
examples.translation: 기술적으로 동기화된 임의의 순서로 여러 개의 변분 및/또는 인코딩 레이어를 가질 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 기술적으로 타당한 근거가 있다면 변분 레이어와 인코딩 레이어를 어떤 순서로든 여러 개 배치할 수 있습니다.
examples.why: 'motivated'를 '동기화(synchronization)'로 옮겨 문장이 '기술적으로 동기화된 순서'라는 무의미한 말이 됩니다. 오개념을 심지는 않지만 해당 문장의 요지(근거만 있으면 순서는 자유)가 독자에게 전달되지 않습니다.

examples.source: There is nothing unique about choosing $Z$, but it is well motivated:
examples.translation: $Z$를 선택하는 것이 특별한 이유는 없지만, 다음과 같은 이유로 잘 동기화되어 있습니다:
examples.suggested: $Z$를 선택해야만 하는 것은 아니지만, 다음과 같은 충분한 근거가 있습니다:
examples.why: 같은 'motivated → 동기화' 오역이 반복됩니다. 바로 뒤 불릿이 근거를 나열하므로 독자가 맥락으로 복구할 수는 있으나, 네이티브 기술 편집자라면 반드시 고칠 표현입니다.

examples.source: This will be accomplished using a VQC with few layers that can be identified by their distinct purposes:
examples.translation: 이는 각각 고유한 목적을 가진 몇 개의 레이어로 식별할 수 있는 소수의 레이어를 가진 VQC를 사용하여 달성됩니다:
examples.suggested: 이는 각각 뚜렷한 목적으로 구분되는 몇 개의 레이어로 이루어진 VQC를 사용해 달성합니다:
examples.why: '레이어'가 한 문장에서 두 번 중복되어 영어 구문을 그대로 겹쳐 옮긴 번역투가 됩니다. 의미는 보존되지만 한국인 기술 필자가 쓰지 않을 문장입니다.

examples.source: parameters / optimizer / convolutional layer
examples.translation: 매개변수(15회) vs 파라미터(8회), 최적화기(5회) vs 옵티마이저(1회), 컨볼루션 레이어(19행) vs 합성곱 레이어(262행)
examples.suggested: 파일 내에서 매개변수·최적화기·합성곱 레이어로 통일
examples.why: 동일 개념이 한 문서 안에서 두 가지 표기로 갈립니다. 개념 식별이 불가능해지는 수준은 아니므로 MINOR이지만, 학습자가 서로 다른 대상을 가리킨다고 오인할 여지가 있습니다.

examples.source: But the scaling of this to more optimization steps and larger testing data sets should be clear from instructions throughout the lesson.
examples.translation: 하지만 더 많은 최적화 단계와 더 큰 테스트 데이터셋으로의 확장은 이 레슨 전반에 걸친 지침에서 명확하게 설명됩니다.
examples.suggested: 하지만 최적화 단계를 늘리고 테스트 데이터셋을 키우는 방법은 이 강의 전반의 설명을 통해 충분히 짐작하실 수 있을 것입니다.
examples.why: 'should be clear from'(독자가 추론할 수 있을 것이다)이 '명확하게 설명됩니다'(문서가 명시적으로 설명한다)로 강화되었습니다. 실제로 확장 절차를 따로 설명한 절은 없으므로 약한 과장이지만, 오개념 수준은 아닙니다.

editor_note: Delta entry 5 (the IBMVideo title) renders "describes how to install Qiskit and write your first quantum program" faithfully as "Qiskit을 설치하고 첫 번째 양자 프로그램을 작성하는 방법을 설명합니다" — correct scope of the "how to" clause over both verbs, speaker name kept, no added or dropped claim, and it matches the body's 합니다체 and the surrounding prose that already introduces Olivia Lanes ("아래 영상에서 Olivia Lanes가 이 레슨의 내용을 안내해요").

Placeholder stub with a single prose line: "Lesson coming soon!" → "레슨이 곧 공개됩니다!" is faithful and idiomatic, and the frontmatter description ("IBM Quantum Platform의 다른 강좌 및 학습 경로 안내") correctly renders "courses and learning pathways" with no drift or added claim.

Meaning is fully faithful throughout: the 20-question/16-correct pass threshold, the "two attempts then temporarily locked" caveat ("두 번의 시도에서 합격 점수를 받지 못하면 시험이 일시적으로 잠깁니다"), the badge-to-registration-email routing, and the entire Credly NOTICE paragraph (third-party processor, US location, name/email/badge shared, IBM subsidiaries worldwide) all match the English with no dropped qualifier, inverted condition or added claim. The only thing a native technical editor would change is the redundant "최소 16문항 이상 정답을 맞혀야" — Korean style guides treat 최소 … 이상 as a doubled quantifier; "16문항 이상" or "최소 16문항" is the edited form. Note also that the body prose is 합니다체 rather than the requested 해요체, but this matches the ko corpus convention (every other use-a-qc-today page is 합니다체-dominant), so I do not count it as a per-file defect; imperatives are already 해요체 ("확인하세요", "받으세요"). Heading "지식 테스트" for "Test your knowledge" is slightly calqued but defensible and consistent with the course.

examples.source: you must answer at least 16 correctly to pass
examples.translation: 합격하려면 최소 16문항 이상 정답을 맞혀야 합니다
examples.suggested: 합격하려면 16문항 이상 정답을 맞혀야 합니다
examples.why: 최소 … 이상 doubles the quantifier; Korean editing style keeps only one. Meaning is still unambiguous, so this is cosmetic, not misleading.

examples.source: The exam consists of 20 questions … the exam becomes temporarily locked.
examples.translation: 시험은 20문항으로 구성되며 … 시험이 일시적으로 잠깁니다.
examples.why: Body prose is 합니다체 rather than the 해요체 convention named in the brief, but the whole ko use-a-qc-today course is 합니다체, so this is consistent house style rather than a slip — reported for visibility only.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the welcome paragraph, the "no physics degree / no years of programming" reassurance, the exam-and-Credly flow, and the entire Credly privacy notice (third-party processor in the US, name/email/badge shared, subsidiaries and third parties globally) all match the English with no drift, softening or invented claims. Two editorial slips: "course" is rendered two ways inside this one short file — 강좌 in the two intro paragraphs (line 12/14) but 코스 twice in the Exam section (line 18, ""양자 컴퓨터 사용하기" 코스의 배지", "이 코스의 레슨") — while the sibling lesson pages consistently use 강좌; and "follow along with a notebook" becomes the bare 노트북, which in Korean first reads as "laptop" rather than a Jupyter notebook, so the sentence "노트북을 따라가며 "실행" 버튼을 클릭할 수 있다면" is momentarily ambiguous for exactly the beginner audience this sentence targets. Register (합니다체 declaratives plus 치르세요) is consistent with the rest of the ko locale and is not a defect.

examples.source: Welcome to *Use a quantum computer today*! In the course, … / To earn your badge for the "Using a quantum computer" course … after reading the lessons in this course.
examples.translation: 이 강좌에서는 … / 이 강좌는 호기심 많고 … / "양자 컴퓨터 사용하기" 코스의 배지를 취득하려면 … 이 코스의 레슨을 읽은 후
examples.suggested: Use 강좌 in the Exam section too: "…" 강좌의 배지를 취득하려면 … 이 강좌의 레슨을 읽은 후
examples.why: The same word "course" is split between 강좌 and 코스 within one short page; the surrounding lesson pages of this course use 강좌, so 코스 here reads as an unedited second pass rather than a deliberate choice. Not misleading — the concept stays identifiable — but a native technical editor would unify it.

examples.source: If you can follow along with a notebook and click "Run," you're ready.
examples.translation: 노트북을 따라가며 "실행" 버튼을 클릭할 수 있다면 준비가 된 것입니다.
examples.suggested: 주피터 노트북을 따라가며 "실행"을 클릭할 수 있다면 준비가 된 것입니다.
examples.why: Bare 노트북 in Korean defaults to "laptop"; the Jupyter sense only resolves retroactively from "실행" 버튼. For an absolute-beginner audience this is worth disambiguating (주피터 노트북 / 노트북(notebook)). Meaning is recoverable, so MINOR only.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the misconception bullets, the scale/quality/speed triad (규모/품질/속도, QuOps→큐비트 연산), the QPU-as-non-general-purpose passage, and the four application categories all carry the English claims and hedges intact, and no hallucinated sentence appears. Three things a native technical editor would still change. (1) Register is mixed: the body is uniformly 합니다체 while the opening ("Olivia Lanes가 이 레슨의 내용을 안내해요") and closing ("어디로 나아갈지 살펴봐요") are 해요체, and line 16 adds a humble 드리 form ("도와드리겠습니다") — the very first paragraph switches style between its two sentences. (2) The hedge in "It is unlikely that error correction will completely replace error mitigation" is dropped: "오류 수정이 오류 완화를 완전히 대체하지는 않을 것입니다" states it flatly; the following 예측합니다 keeps the takeaway correct, so this is a lost qualifier rather than a misleading claim. (3) A few calques: "NP-어려운 문제" for NP-hard (Korean convention is NP-난해 or the untranslated NP-hard), "선형 방정식의 대형 시스템" for "large systems of linear equations" (natural: 대규모 선형 연립방정식), "이국적인 양자 상태" for "exotic quantum states", and "읽기" for readout.

examples.source: In the following video, Olivia Lanes steps you through the content in this lesson. Alternatively, you can open the YouTube video ...
examples.translation: 아래 영상에서 Olivia Lanes가 이 레슨의 내용을 안내해요. 또는 별도 창에서 이 레슨의 YouTube 영상을 열 수도 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 안내합니다 … 열 수도 있습니다 (or convert the whole file to 해요체 consistently)
examples.why: The two sentences of the very first paragraph use different speech levels (해요체 then 합니다체); the rest of the file is 합니다체 except the final sentence ("살펴봐요"), and line 16 additionally uses the humble form "도와드리겠습니다". Pick one level and hold it.

examples.source: It is unlikely that error correction will completely replace error mitigation.
examples.translation: 오류 수정이 오류 완화를 완전히 대체하지는 않을 것입니다.
examples.suggested: 오류 수정이 오류 완화를 완전히 대체할 가능성은 낮습니다.
examples.why: "It is unlikely that" is a probabilistic hedge; the Korean renders it as a flat prediction. The lesson's point (both will be used together) survives, so this is a dropped qualifier, not a false teaching — but the hedge should be restored.

examples.source: Many optimization problems are categorized as NP-hard in complexity theory
examples.translation: 많은 최적화 문제는 복잡도 이론에서 NP-어려운 문제로 분류됩니다.
examples.suggested: 많은 최적화 문제는 복잡도 이론에서 NP-난해(NP-hard) 문제로 분류됩니다.
examples.why: "NP-어려운" is a word-by-word calque; Korean CS texts use NP-난해 or keep NP-hard. Recognizable, so minor, but it reads as machine output in an otherwise competent paragraph.

examples.source: Mapping PDEs to large systems of linear equations / exotic quantum states / efficient state preparation and readout
examples.translation: PDE를 선형 방정식의 대형 시스템에 매핑 / 이국적인 양자 상태 / 효율적인 상태 준비 및 읽기
examples.suggested: PDE를 대규모 선형 연립방정식으로 매핑 / 특이한(이색적인) 양자 상태 / 효율적인 상태 준비 및 판독(읽어내기)
examples.why: English noun-phrase order is carried over literally instead of using the settled Korean forms (연립방정식, 판독); "이국적인" is the travel sense of exotic, not the condensed-matter sense. All grammatical, all slightly off-register for a Korean physics writer.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I found no drift or hallucination: the CNOT condition keeps "only if" ("qubit 0…이 상태 |1⟩에 있을 때만 qubit 1…을 뒤집습니다"), little-endian right=least-significant is correct, the 50/50 probabilities, the "superposition is a mathematical description, not testably real" caveat, and the coin-glued-together analogy all survive intact; core terms are correct and consistent (기저/계산 기저, 중첩, 얽힘, 붕괴, 고유 상태, 유니터리 행렬, 관측량, 진폭/위상). The defects are stylistic. (1) Register: the body is uniformly deferential 합니다체, not the locale's 해요체, and the very first paragraph mixes both in adjacent sentences — "…안내해요." followed by "…열 수도 있습니다." (2) In the phase/wave analogy, "trough" is rendered 골짜기 (a geographic valley); the wave term is 골. (3) A few English-shaped calques remain, e.g. "동등하게 중요한 두 번째 해석을 가지고 있습니다" for "have a second, equally important interpretation". (4) "same underlying mathematics" flattens to "동일한 수학에서 비롯됩니다", dropping the "underlying/기저에 깔린" nuance. None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: In the following video, Olivia Lanes steps you through the content in this lesson. Alternatively, you can open the YouTube video for this lesson in a separate window.
examples.translation: 다음 영상에서 Olivia Lanes가 이 수업의 내용을 안내해요. 또는 별도의 창에서 이 수업의 [YouTube 영상]을 열 수도 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 다음 영상에서 Olivia Lanes가 이 수업의 내용을 안내해요. 또는 별도의 창에서 이 수업의 [YouTube 영상]을 열 수도 있어요.
examples.why: Two different speech levels in adjacent sentences (해요체 then 합니다체). The rest of the file is consistently 합니다체, so this single 해요 is also the only sentence matching the locale's stated 해요체 convention — either way the opening paragraph is internally inconsistent.

examples.source: are their peaks aligned, or is one wave shifted so its peak meets the other's trough?
examples.translation: 파동의 마루가 정렬되어 있나요, 아니면 한 파동이 이동하여 마루가 다른 파동의 골짜기와 만나나요?
examples.suggested: 두 파동의 마루가 서로 맞아떨어지나요, 아니면 한 파동이 밀려서 그 마루가 다른 파동의 골과 만나나요?
examples.why: 마루 is correctly the wave crest, but its partner term is 골, not 골짜기 (a geographic valley/ravine). The mismatched pair breaks the crest/trough analogy a Korean physics writer would render as 마루/골.

examples.source: But Pauli matrices have a second, equally important interpretation.
examples.translation: 하지만 Pauli 행렬은 동등하게 중요한 두 번째 해석을 가지고 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 하지만 Pauli 행렬에는 그에 못지않게 중요한 또 다른 해석이 있습니다.
examples.why: Calqued English syntax: 'have' → '가지고 있습니다' plus the literal '동등하게 중요한 두 번째'. Natural Korean uses '…에는 …이 있습니다' with '그에 못지않게 중요한'.

examples.source: Both roles come from the same underlying mathematics.
examples.translation: 두 역할 모두 동일한 수학에서 비롯됩니다.
examples.suggested: 두 역할 모두 그 바탕에 깔린 동일한 수학에서 비롯됩니다.
examples.why: Dropped qualifier: 'underlying' carries the pedagogical point that one shared mathematical structure sits beneath both the gate role and the observable role. Not misleading, but the emphasis flattens.

editor_note: Delta entry 6 (the IBMVideo title) is faithful and idiomatic: "Qiskit의 Estimator 프리미티브를 사용하여 2-Qubit 이징 해밀토니안의 에너지를 구하는 과정을 안내합니다" preserves every element of the English — the Estimator primitive, the two-qubit Ising Hamiltonian, and "walks you through finding the energy" rendered naturally as "구하는 과정을 안내합니다" — with no added or dropped claim, and 이징/해밀토니안/프리미티브 match the terms used elsewhere in the file (해밀토니안 in the H = J Z₁Z₀ + hₓ(X₁+X₀) passage, 프리미티브 in the Sampler/Estimator introduction).

Meaning is faithful throughout — the CNOT condition ("제어 Qubit이 |1⟩일 때만 표적 Qubit을 반전시킵니다"), the 75% amplitude example, the little-endian caveat, the "no coefficients satisfy both equations → entangled" argument, and the depth-4 / shallowest-depth-5 claims all match the English exactly; no drift or hallucination, and register is consistent. What a native editor would still change is terminology: "Born rule" is rendered 본 규칙, which in Korean reads as "this rule" rather than the physicist Born (standard: 보른 규칙) — the English gloss rescues it, so it does not mislead. "Noise" is split within the file between 노이즈 (Aer-simulator and decoherence paragraphs) and 잡음 (depth paragraph, summary), and the same happens with 블로흐 구 vs "Bloch 구" and 상태 벡터 시뮬레이터 vs "statevector 시뮬레이터" in Exercise 1. Finally "quantum circuits are the native format" became 양자 명령을 표현하는 기본 형식 (= default/basic format), flattening "native".

examples.source: So, $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are called probability amplitudes. (see "Born rule")
examples.translation: 따라서 $\alpha$와 $\beta$를 확률 진폭(probability amplitude)이라고 합니다. ("본 규칙(Born rule)" 참조)
examples.suggested: ("보른 규칙(Born rule)" 참조)
examples.why: "본 규칙" reads as "this/the present rule" in Korean, not as the physicist Born; the conventional rendering is 보른 규칙. The parenthetical English keeps it identifiable, so MINOR rather than a false concept.

examples.source: In modern noisy quantum computers, low-depth circuits have fewer errors and are likely to return good results.
examples.translation: 현대의 잡음이 있는 양자 컴퓨터에서는 깊이가 낮은 Circuit일수록 오류가 적고 좋은 결과를 반환할 가능성이 높습니다.
examples.suggested: 현대의 노이즈가 있는 양자 컴퓨터에서는 …
examples.why: "noise" is 노이즈 in the Aer-simulator paragraph and in "노이즈와 qubit 결맞음 손실", but 잡음 in the depth paragraph and the summary — the same core term rendered two ways in one file.

examples.source: Then run each circuit using the statevector simulator and display the resulting state on the Bloch sphere.
examples.translation: 그런 다음 statevector 시뮬레이터로 각 Circuit을 실행하고 Bloch 구에 결과 상태를 시각화해 보세요.
examples.suggested: 그런 다음 상태 벡터 시뮬레이터로 각 Circuit을 실행하고 블로흐 구에 결과 상태를 시각화해 보세요.
examples.why: Section 3.1 established 블로흐 구 and 상태 벡터 시뮬레이터; Exercise 1 alone reverts to bare English forms, so both terms appear two ways within the file.

examples.source: In a quantum program, quantum circuits are the native format in which to represent quantum instructions.
examples.translation: 양자 프로그램에서 양자 Circuit은 양자 명령을 표현하는 기본 형식입니다.
examples.suggested: 양자 프로그램에서 양자 Circuit은 양자 명령을 표현하는 고유(네이티브) 형식입니다.
examples.why: 기본 형식 means "default/basic format"; the English "native format" asserts circuits are the intrinsic representation, an emphasis the current wording flattens.

editor_note: Three-sentence stub, faithful throughout: attribution ("도쿄대학교 Yoshiaki Kawase 교수가 준비했습니다"), hosting ("해당 모듈은 GitHub에 호스팅되어 있습니다"), and the optional-but-recommended caveat ("선택 사항으로 간주될 수 있지만 수강을 적극 권장합니다") all preserve the English's hedging and emphasis exactly; the -습니다 style matches the ko corpus convention seen in the sibling course index.mdx.

Meaning is fully faithful — nothing here would mislead a learner: the 14 lessons/labs, the IBM Quantum + University of Tokyo collaboration, the "building toward a utility-scale calculation" framing and the "very similar to work published on the cover of Nature in June 2023" hedge are all carried over intact and correctly scoped. Two editorial slips remain. (1) Within-file term inconsistency: the frontmatter description renders lesson/course as "레슨"/"코스" ("14개 레슨 코스"), while the body of the same page renders the identical concepts as "수업"/"과정" ("14개의 수업과 실습", "이 이벤트 재생 과정") — a reader seeing the card blurb and then the page sees two vocabularies for one thing. (2) "event replay course" is calqued as "이벤트 재생 과정"; "재생" reads as media playback and a Korean technical writer would more naturally write "이벤트 다시보기 과정" or "이벤트 재방송 과정". Register is consistent 합니다체 throughout (구성됩니다 / 맞추고 있습니다 / 유사합니다) rather than 해요체 — uniform and defensible for technical docs, so noted rather than counted.

examples.source: a 14-lesson course … 14 lessons and labs
examples.translation: frontmatter: '14개 레슨 코스' — body: '14개의 수업과 실습으로 구성됩니다 … 이 이벤트 재생 과정'
examples.suggested: Pick one pair and use it in both places, e.g. '14개 레슨으로 구성된 코스' in the description and '14개의 레슨과 랩' / '이 코스' in the body (or standardise on 수업/과정 in both).
examples.why: The same two concepts (lesson, course) are rendered with loanwords in the frontmatter and native words in the body of one short page; the card blurb and the page it opens do not share vocabulary.

examples.source: This event replay course consists of 14 lessons and labs developed and run by IBM Quantum in collaboration with the University of Tokyo.
examples.translation: 이 이벤트 재생 과정은 IBM Quantum®이 도쿄대학교와 협력하여 개발하고 진행한 14개의 수업과 실습으로 구성됩니다.
examples.suggested: 이 이벤트 다시보기 과정은 IBM Quantum®이 도쿄대학교와 협력하여 개발하고 운영한 14개의 레슨과 랩으로 구성되어 있습니다.
examples.why: '이벤트 재생' is a word-for-word calque of 'event replay'; 재생 reads as media playback rather than 'a re-run of a past live event', which is what the English means. Meaning survives, but it is the one phrase that betrays translation.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the lesson-by-lesson map (레슨 2-6 / 7-8 / 9 / 10-11 / 12-14), the "부차적" rendering of "tangential", and the "이 강좌에는 퀴즈나 배지가 연관되어 있지 않습니다" caveat all track the English exactly, and no claim is inverted, softened or invented. Three editorial slips remain, none misleading. "a live course held at the University of Tokyo" is rendered "실시간 강좌", which in Korean connotes a real-time *online/streamed* course rather than the in-person lecture course actually meant (대면/현장 강의). "Good-faith estimates" becomes "성실한 추정치", a calque — 성실한 describes a person's diligence, not an estimate; a native technical writer would write "최선을 다한 추정치" or "합리적인 추정치". Within one paragraph "lab" is rendered two ways, "계산 실습 활동" then "랩"/"랩이 간결하여", so the same object gets both a translated and a transliterated name. Register is 합니다체 consistently, matching the rest of the ko corpus, so it is not counted as a defect here.

examples.source: This course is based on a live course held at the University of Tokyo in 2024.
examples.translation: 이 강좌는 2024년 도쿄대학교에서 진행된 실시간 강좌를 기반으로 합니다.
examples.suggested: 이 강좌는 2024년 도쿄대학교에서 진행된 대면 강의를 기반으로 합니다.
examples.why: "live course" here means a course taught in person before a live audience (each lesson has a lecture PDF). Korean "실시간" is the standard word for real-time/streamed online delivery, so the reader pictures a webinar rather than a classroom lecture. Low-stakes but a wrong picture.

examples.source: Good-faith estimates of required QPU time have been provided at the top of each lesson, but your calculations might vary slightly.
examples.translation: 필요한 QPU 시간에 대한 성실한 추정치가 각 레슨 상단에 제공되어 있지만, 실제 계산은 약간 다를 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 각 레슨 상단에 필요한 QPU 시간을 최선을 다해 추정한 값이 제시되어 있지만, 여러분의 실제 계산에서는 약간 다를 수 있습니다.
examples.why: "성실한 추정치" is a word-for-word calque; 성실하다 is an attribute of a person's conduct, not of a number, so the collocation is one no Korean technical writer would produce. The suggestion also restores "your" (여러분의), which the current rendering drops.

examples.source: Each lesson consists of a PDF … and a computational lab activity. In some cases, the labs are sparse and merely show a workflow …
examples.translation: 각 레슨은 … PDF와 계산 실습 활동으로 구성됩니다. 일부 경우에는 랩이 간결하여 단순히 워크플로우만 보여주고 …
examples.suggested: … 계산 실습으로 구성됩니다. 일부 실습은 내용이 소략하여 워크플로우만 보여주고 …
examples.why: The same referent is called 실습 활동 in one sentence and 랩 in the next, within a single paragraph — the reader has to infer they are the same thing. Separately, "sparse" (bare, minimal) is softened to 간결하다 (concise, a compliment), losing the English's mildly apologetic tone.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the QFT product-representation setup, the 5/16-turn encoding example, the T-gate θ=1/8 derivation and the Shor closing sentence all match the English, and core terms are correct and consistent (유니터리 연산자, 고유벡터/고유값, 계수 레지스터, 제어 유니터리, 계산 기저/푸리에 기저, 중첩). Three small editorial slips remain, none misleading: (1) the pedagogical "and so on" is dropped twice — in "…세 번째는 4씩 증가할 때마다 뒤집힙니다." and in "…그 다음 Qubit에서는 이 각도가 다시 두 배가 됩니다.", so the "pattern continues" cue that the English uses to generalize is lost; (2) "problems that are infeasible for classical computers" is strengthened to "고전 컴퓨터로는 불가능한 문제" (impossible rather than infeasible/impractical); (3) "only if its corresponding control bit is |1⟩" becomes "제어 Qubit이 |1⟩인 경우에만" (bit → Qubit). Also cosmetic: the kept term is written Qubit in most places but lowercase qubit in a few ("한 세트의 qubit 레지스터", "4 qubit QFT", "qubit 1/2") — casing only, for the deterministic sweep.

examples.source: the leftmost qubit flips with every increment in the number, the next with every 2 increments, the third with every 4 increments, and so on.
examples.translation: 가장 왼쪽 Qubit은 숫자가 1씩 증가할 때마다 뒤집히고, 그 다음은 2씩 증가할 때마다, 세 번째는 4씩 증가할 때마다 뒤집힙니다.
examples.suggested: …세 번째는 4씩 증가할 때마다 뒤집히는 식으로 이어집니다.
examples.why: "and so on" is dropped, so the sentence reads as an exhaustive three-item list instead of signalling the doubling pattern continues for all remaining qubits — the point the paragraph is teaching. The same omission recurs at ko line 105 ("…이 각도가 다시 두 배가 됩니다." for "this angle is then doubled for the qubit after, and so on").

examples.source: QFT and QPE form the essential backbone of many quantum algorithms solving problems that are infeasible for classical computers.
examples.translation: QFT와 QPE는 함께 고전 컴퓨터로는 불가능한 문제를 해결하는 많은 양자 알고리즘의 핵심 기반을 형성합니다.
examples.suggested: …고전 컴퓨터로는 사실상 풀기 어려운(실행 불가능한) 문제를 해결하는…
examples.why: "infeasible" (computationally impractical) is strengthened to "불가능한" (impossible). A learner could take it as a claim about classical impossibility rather than intractability.

examples.source: the controlled unitary CU that applies the unitary operator U on the target register only if its corresponding control bit is |1⟩
examples.translation: 제어 Qubit이 |1⟩인 경우에만 목표 레지스터에 유니터리 연산자 U를 적용하는 제어 유니터리 CU가 필요합니다.
examples.suggested: 해당 제어 비트가 |1⟩인 경우에만 …
examples.why: The English says "control bit"; the Korean substitutes "제어 Qubit". Harmless in context (the control is a qubit), but it silently changes the source's wording and loses "its corresponding".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I found no semantic drift or hallucination; the load-bearing physics passages (the non-commuting-operator caveat in §1, the "trotterization → deeper circuits → more error accumulation" trade-off, and the dense §4 paragraph on ↓↑ → ↑↓ spin swap at α=0°, no evolution at α=±90°, 67% swap probability at α=±45°) all track the English exactly, including the right-to-left label caveat. What a native technical editor would change is terminological consistency: "magnetization" is rendered 자화 in §1 (자화값 +1과 -1, 자화와 같은 시스템의 특정 속성) but 자기화 from §2.5 onward (자기화 연산자, 자기화의 기댓값); "time evolution" is 시간 발전 in §1 (시간 발전 기법, 시간 발전을 공부합니다) but 시간 진화 from §2.2 on (시간 진화 시뮬레이션); and the external field is 자기장 in §1/§2.1 but bare 필드 in §4 (횡방향 필드, 필드가 종방향). Separately, §3.4 renders "the classical computer" as 클래식 컴퓨터, which reads as "vintage/classic computer" — the field term is 고전 컴퓨터, and the same file already uses 고전적 입력 in §4.1. None of these would make a learner form a false belief, so this stays MINOR.

examples.source: a magnetization of $+1$ and $-1$ … properties of the system like magnetization / a *magnetization operator*
examples.translation: 각각 자화값 $+1$과 $-1$에 해당합니다 … 자화와 같은 시스템의 특정 속성들 / *자기화 연산자*
examples.suggested: Pick one and use it throughout — 자화 is the standard physics rendering: 자화 연산자, 자화의 기댓값.
examples.why: The same observable is named 자화 in the introduction and 자기화 in the sections that actually measure it, so a learner cannot tell that §2.5's 자기화 연산자 is the quantity §1 introduced as 자화. Concept is still recoverable from the math, so MINOR.

examples.source: real time evolution technique … the time evolution of a system / Set the parameters of the time-evolution simulation
examples.translation: 실시간 시간 발전 기법 … 시스템의 시간 발전 / 시간 진화 시뮬레이션 파라미터 설정하기
examples.suggested: Use 시간 발전 consistently (the conventional Korean rendering of quantum time evolution), including in the §2/§3/§4 headings.
examples.why: The file's central concept switches label at the §2 boundary; 진화 additionally carries a biological-evolution connotation that 발전 does not.

examples.source: The data below is the precomputed exact results from the classical computer.
examples.translation: 아래 데이터는 클래식 컴퓨터에서 미리 계산한 정확한 결과입니다.
examples.suggested: 아래 데이터는 고전 컴퓨터에서 미리 계산한 정확한 결과입니다.
examples.why: 클래식 컴퓨터 reads as "classic/vintage computer" rather than the physics sense of classical (as opposed to quantum); the file itself uses the correct 고전적 in §4.1's 고전적 입력을 양자 문제로 매핑하기.

examples.source: under a transversal field ($\alpha=0^\circ$) … If the field is longitudinal ($\alpha=\pm90^\circ$)
examples.translation: 횡방향 필드($\alpha=0^\circ$) 아래에서 … 필드가 종방향($\alpha=\pm90^\circ$)이면
examples.suggested: 횡방향 자기장 … 자기장이 종방향이면
examples.why: §1 and §2.1 consistently render the same object as 자기장 (외부 자기장, 횡방향 자기장 이징 해밀토니안); the bare loanword 필드 in the §4 discussion breaks that thread and is less natural in Korean physics prose.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the two correction tables (텔레포테이션 "01"→X/"10"→Z, 초고밀도 "01"→Z/"10"→X) are not swapped, the little-endian/100% $|0\rangle$ reasoning, the no-cloning and faster-than-light Q&A, and the dynamic-circuit error explanation all match the English, so nothing here would mislead a learner. What a native technical editor would change is terminology consistency: "quantum state tomography" is 양자 상태 단층촬영 in the §3 heading and body but 양자 상태 토모그래피 from Exercise 1 onward (§3 은 단층촬영, 이후 토모그래피), and "superdense coding" is 초고밀도 코딩 in the page title and §1 bullet but 초고밀도 부호화 from §5 through the summary; "unknown quantum state" likewise alternates 미지의 양자 상태 (§1, §6) and 알 수 없는 양자 상태 (§4). Two small emphasis slips: "Almost the same setup can be used for a different purpose" is strengthened to "전혀 다른 목적", and "we can visualize the state ... but only because we know what parameters were used" loses the restrictive "only" (단순히 "…알고 있기 때문에 시각화할 수 있습니다"). Also two mechanical blemishes: §4.1 step 1 uses the passive-shaped 얽힙니다 where the transitive 얽습니다/얽히게 합니다 is meant (§4.2 correctly uses 얽고), and in §4.3 a sentence-final period is swallowed into math as "것입니다$.U^{-1}U$는".

examples.source: quantum state tomography
examples.translation: 양자 상태 단층촬영 (§3 heading and body) / 양자 상태 토모그래피 (Exercise 1, Exercise 2, wrap-up)
examples.suggested: 양자 상태 토모그래피 throughout (or 단층촬영 throughout)
examples.why: The same core concept is named two different ways inside one lesson; 단층촬영 is the medical-imaging calque, while 토모그래피 is the conventional Korean quantum-info rendering the file itself uses later.

examples.source: superdense coding
examples.translation: 초고밀도 코딩 (title, §1 bullet) / 초고밀도 부호화 (§5 onward)
examples.suggested: Pick one — 초고밀도 부호화 — and use it in the title and §1 bullet as well
examples.why: A learner scanning the table of contents sees 초고밀도 코딩 but finds 초고밀도 부호화 in the section that teaches it; still identifiable, but a needless split of a protocol name.

examples.source: Almost the same setup can be used for a different purpose.
examples.translation: 거의 동일한 설정을 전혀 다른 목적에 활용할 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 거의 동일한 설정을 다른 목적에 활용할 수 있습니다.
examples.why: 전혀 다른 ("entirely different") strengthens the English's plain "a different purpose"; the point of the paragraph is that the setup is nearly identical, so amplifying the contrast works against the intended framing.

examples.source: We can visualize the state we've created, but only because we know what parameters were used in the U gate.
examples.translation: $U$ Gate에 사용된 파라미터를 알고 있기 때문에 생성된 상태를 시각화할 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 생성된 상태를 시각화할 수 있는 것은 오직 $U$ Gate에 사용된 파라미터를 알고 있기 때문입니다.
examples.why: The English's "but only because" is the whole teaching point — visualization is a privilege of this toy setup, not something available in general; the Korean states the cause without the restriction, flattening the caveat that the next sentence builds on.

examples.source: Alice entangles |psi> with her part of the e-bit using the CNOT gate. / ... so that we can measure '0'. That is, since U^{-1}U is the identity ...
examples.translation: Alice는 CNOT Gate를 사용하여 $|\psi \rangle$를 자신이 보유한 e-비트와 얽힙니다. / ... '0'을 측정하는 것입니다$.U^{-1}U$는 항등 연산이므로 ...
examples.suggested: ... e-비트와 얽습니다(또는 얽히게 합니다). / ... '0'을 측정하는 것입니다. $U^{-1}U$는 항등 연산이므로 ...
examples.why: 얽힙니다 is the passive-shaped form used with a transitive object marker (를), which a Korean technical writer would not write; and the sentence-final period has been pulled inside the math delimiters, so it typesets as part of the formula.

editor_note: No misleading drift or hallucination: the Hamiltonian setup, the "data dependence" → coupling-map coloring argument, the θ_J=-π/2 simplification, ZNE+PEA, the 27-qubit/6-layer vs 127-qubit/60-layer contrast and all quantities (28 edges → 28*5 entangling gates, 144 Eagle edges, 2min 19s, 3 colors) are all faithful. The defects are terminological/consistency. "observable" is rendered 관측값 ("observed value") in all three places (⟨Z_62⟩을 관측값으로 하는), where the domain term is 관측가능량/옵저버블 — recognizable but teaches the wrong word. "mitigate" splits within the file: §1 uses 완화 ("오류를 완화했습니다", "미완화(unmitigated)") while §5.3 switches to 보정 ("보정된(mitigated)", "보정되지 않은(unmitigated)"); "fake device" likewise splits 가짜 장치 (§2–3) vs 가상 디바이스 (§4), and "edge" splits 에지 (§3) vs 엣지 (§5.2). Two small qualifier drops: "Trotter decomposition of the time-evolution operator" loses 시간 진화 연산자의, and "This is not likely to be a single event" loses the hedge, becoming the flat assertion "단 하나의 사건으로 이루어지는 것이 아니라". Register is consistent 합니다체 technical-doc style with no 드리-type humble forms.

examples.source: a 127-qubit × 60-layer (20 Trotter steps) circuit with the ⟨Z_62⟩ as an observable
examples.translation: $\langle Z_{62} \rangle$을 관측값으로 하는 127-Qubit $\times$ 60-레이어(20 Trotter 단계) Circuit
examples.suggested: $\langle Z_{62} \rangle$을 관측가능량(observable)으로 하는 …
examples.why: 관측값 means "observed/measured value", not "observable". The conventional Korean domain term is 관측가능량 (or the kept form 옵저버블). Used consistently in all three occurrences, so it is recognizable rather than misleading, but it is the wrong technical noun for the Estimator's observable argument.

examples.source: applied … (ZNE) … to mitigate errors / the "mitigated" points / the "unmitigated" in Figure 4b
examples.translation: §1: "오류를 완화했습니다", "미완화(unmitigated)" — §5.3: "보정된(mitigated)", "보정되지 않은(unmitigated)"
examples.suggested: Pick one stem for the whole file — e.g. 완화된(mitigated) / 완화되지 않은(unmitigated), matching 오류 완화 for error mitigation.
examples.why: Error mitigation is the file's central technique; rendering it 완화 in the introduction and 보정 (which reads as "calibration/correction") in the final section makes the reader work to connect §5.3's plot back to §1's ZNE/PEA discussion.

examples.source: fake device
examples.translation: 가짜 장치 (§2.2, §3, §4.3 intro) vs 가상 디바이스 (§4, §4.3 heading)
examples.suggested: Use one rendering throughout (가상 디바이스 is the more idiomatic of the two); same for 에지/엣지 (edge) split between §3 and §5.2.
examples.why: Two labels for the same FakeTorontoV2 object inside one lesson; a learner can briefly wonder whether 가짜 장치 and 가상 디바이스 are different execution targets.

examples.source: They simulate spin dynamics from an initial state by means of first-order Trotter decomposition of the time-evolution operator. … This is not likely to be a single event, but rather an era …
examples.translation: 논문에서는 1차 Trotter 분해를 사용하여 초기 상태에서의 스핀 동역학을 시뮬레이션합니다. … 이것은 단 하나의 사건으로 이루어지는 것이 아니라, …
examples.suggested: …시간 진화 연산자의 1차 Trotter 분해를 사용하여… ; 이것은 단 하나의 사건이 되지는 않을 가능성이 높으며, …
examples.why: Two dropped qualifiers: the object of the Trotter decomposition (the time-evolution operator) is omitted just before the equations that decompose exp(-iH δt), and the hedge "not likely" is flattened into a categorical denial. Neither misleads on its own, but both tighten claims the English deliberately keeps loose.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I found no inverted condition, swapped quantity, dropped caveat or hallucinated claim; the Trotterization derivation, the non-commuting-operator caveat, the $N=20$ / $N=70$ setups, and the closing hardware-vs-MPS comparison all track the English exactly, and the EN typo "matrix product space simulators" is even carried over faithfully as "행렬 곱 공간 시뮬레이터". What a native technical editor would still change is internal term consistency: "magnetization" is rendered two ways — 자화 (§1, "자화값 $+1$과 $-1$") but 자기화 everywhere it matters later ("자기화 연산자", "자기화(자기화 연산자의 기댓값)를 모니터링"); and "ground state" is 바닥 상태 in the 20-qubit Activity but 기저 상태(ground state) in the identical 70-qubit Activity 3 sentence — 기저 is doubly unfortunate here because 계산 기저 is already used for "computational basis" in the same file. There is also a 양자 Circuit / 양자 회로 split between the two otherwise-parallel "Prepare the quantum circuit 2" headings, and one stiff calqued sentence ("...서론의 근사식으로 구성됩니다"). None of these mislead; the concepts stay identifiable.

examples.source: These spins can have two orientations … which correspond to a magnetization of +1 and −1 … / a *magnetization operator*
examples.translation: 각각 자화값 $+1$과 $-1$에 해당합니다 … *자기화 연산자* … 자기화(자기화 연산자의 기댓값)를 모니터링합니다
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering for magnetization and use it throughout — 자화 is the conventional physics term (자화 / 자화 연산자 / 자화율)
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency: the same quantity is 자화 in the model-setup section and 자기화 in every later section, so a learner may wonder whether the observable being plotted is the same quantity introduced with the Ising spins.

examples.source: We will start from the ground state, which is a ferromagnetic state (all up or all down).
examples.translation: 강자성 상태(모두 위 또는 모두 아래)인 바닥 상태에서 시작하겠습니다. (§ 20-qubit) / 기저 상태(ground state)인 강자성 상태(모두 위 또는 모두 아래)에서 시작할 것입니다. (§ Activity 3)
examples.suggested: Use 바닥 상태 in both places (the sentences are otherwise identical in the English)
examples.why: Two renderings of 'ground state' in the same file, and 기저 상태 collides with 계산 기저 (computational basis) used earlier in §1; the parenthetical English gloss keeps it recognizable, so it is a consistency slip rather than a false concept.

examples.source: A first-order formula consists of the approximation stated in the introduction, where the matrix exponential of a sum is approximated by a product of matrix exponentials:
examples.translation: 1차 공식은 합의 행렬 지수를 행렬 지수들의 곱으로 근사하는 서론의 근사식으로 구성됩니다:
examples.suggested: 1차 공식은 서론에서 소개한 근사, 즉 합의 행렬 지수를 행렬 지수들의 곱으로 근사하는 식을 사용합니다:
examples.why: Calqued English clause order stacks a long relative clause in front of 서론의 근사식; the parallel sentence at Activity 4 (line ~451, '위에서 설명한 근사, 즉 …') already uses the natural Korean pattern, so this one reads stiffer than its own twin.
