examples.source: Prepare the quantum circuit 2 (Single circuit for time evolution)
examples.translation: 양자 Circuit 준비하기 2 (시간 진화를 위한 단일 Circuit) / 양자 회로 2 준비하기 (70-큐비트 문제의 단일 시간 진화 Circuit)
examples.suggested: Use the same head noun in both parallel headings (whichever convention the locale keeps)
examples.why: The two parallel section headings split between 양자 Circuit and 양자 회로 (and 20-Qubit vs 20-큐비트 in the body), which weakens the intended 20-qubit ↔ 70-qubit parallel structure of the lesson.

editor_note: The translation is substantively faithful — the QUBO→Hamiltonian derivation, the QAOA pattern steps, the ⟨Z⟩ = p₀ − p₁ explanation and the "기저 상태가 비용 함수를 최소화하는 해에 대응" property all carry the English meaning intact, and no hallucinated claims appear. What a native technical editor would still change: (1) "prefactor" is rendered 전치인수, which in a paragraph that has just used 전치 for "transpose" (x^T는 벡터 x의 전치) reads as "transpose factor"; the intended 1/4 factor is only recoverable from the next paragraph, which correctly says "1/4 인수". (2) "minimum eigenvalue" is consistently 최솟값 고유값, a stiff calque where Korean technical writing says 최소 고유값. (3) Within-file inconsistencies: "cut" is 컷 in §3.5 (최적 컷, 컷의 값) but 절단 in the Sampler note (그래프의 최적 절단); "primitive" appears as 프리미티브 (§3.4), bare primitive (§실행하기, "primitive는 …"), and 회로 shows up for circuit in two §3.4 paragraphs where the rest of the file keeps Circuit. (4) Two small claim shifts: the intro relocates "less scalable" from VQE onto quantum chemistry (확장성이 낮은 양자 화학), and the final cut comment hedges the English assertion "The solution is not optimal due to noise" into 해가 최적이 아닐 수 있습니다. (5) One humble-form slip, 보여 드리기 위해, in the reformulation lead-in. None of these would make a learner form a false belief about VQE or QAOA.

examples.source: Now if we define $b_i=-\sum_{j}(Q_{ij}+Q_{ji})$, remove the prefactor, and the constant $n^2$ term, we arrive at the two equivalent formulations of the same optimization problem.
examples.translation: 이제 $b_i=-\sum_{j}(Q_{ij}+Q_{ji})$로 정의하고, 전치인수와 상수항 $n^2$을 제거하면, 동일한 최적화 문제의 두 가지 동등한 정식화에 도달합니다.
examples.suggested: 이제 $b_i=-\sum_{j}(Q_{ij}+Q_{ji})$로 정의하고, 앞의 계수(1/4)와 상수항 $n^2$을 제거하면, 동일한 최적화 문제의 두 가지 동등한 정식화에 도달합니다.
examples.why: 전치인수 collides with 전치 = transpose, which the file uses two paragraphs earlier for $x^T$. The reader can only recover that the 1/4 factor is meant from the following paragraph ('1/4 인수'). 앞의 계수 / 비례 계수 is the conventional rendering of prefactor.

examples.source: VQE has many applications (like quantum chemistry) in which it is less scalable.
examples.translation: VQE는 확장성이 낮은 양자 화학과 같은 다양한 응용 분야를 가지고 있습니다.
examples.suggested: VQE는 양자 화학처럼 확장성이 상대적으로 떨어지는 응용 분야를 다수 가지고 있습니다.
examples.why: The Korean relative clause attaches 확장성이 낮은 to 양자 화학, so the learner reads 'quantum chemistry has low scalability' rather than 'VQE scales less well in those applications' — the property moves from the algorithm to the field.

examples.source: And calculate the value of the cut. The solution is not optimal due to noise (the cut value of the optimal solution is 5).
examples.translation: 그리고 컷의 값을 계산합니다. 노이즈로 인해 해가 최적이 아닐 수 있습니다 (최적 해의 컷 값은 5입니다).
examples.suggested: 그리고 컷의 값을 계산합니다. 노이즈로 인해 이 해는 최적이 아닙니다 (최적 해의 컷 값은 5입니다).
examples.why: The English asserts the solution is not optimal; 아닐 수 있습니다 hedges it into a possibility. The parenthetical caveat survives, so the learner is not misled about the optimum being 5, but the claim strength is softened.

examples.source: since it is the probability distribution of bitstring measurements which correspond to the optimal cut of the graph / Visualize best cut / the value of the cut
examples.translation: 그래프의 최적 절단에 해당하는 비트스트링 측정의 확률 분포 … 최적 컷 시각화 … 컷의 값
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering — 컷 throughout (그래프의 최적 컷에 해당하는 …).
examples.why: The same max-cut concept is 절단 in one place and 컷 in the neighbouring section headings and prose; the concept stays identifiable, but the split is the kind of thing an editor normalizes.

examples.source: Computing the minimum eigenvalue of a simple Hamiltonian / We will compute the minimum eigenvalue of Pauli $Z$ matrix with VQE.
examples.translation: 간단한 해밀토니안의 최솟값 고유값 계산 / VQE로 Pauli $Z$ 행렬의 최솟값 고유값을 계산합니다.
examples.suggested: 간단한 해밀토니안의 최소 고유값 계산 / VQE로 Pauli $Z$ 행렬의 최소 고유값을 계산합니다.
examples.why: 최솟값 고유값 stacks two nouns ('minimum-value eigenvalue') and reads as a calque; Korean physics/QC writing uses 최소 고유값. Consistent throughout, so recognizable — a polish item, not a comprehension problem.

examples.source: To demonstrate how the QAOA problem can be rewritten in this way, first replace the binary variables $x_i$ …
examples.translation: QAOA 문제를 이런 방식으로 재작성하는 방법을 보여 드리기 위해, 먼저 이진 변수 $x_i$를 …
examples.suggested: QAOA 문제를 이런 방식으로 재작성하는 방법을 보여 주기 위해, 먼저 이진 변수 $x_i$를 …
examples.why: 드리- is the humble form; the rest of the file holds the plain 합니다체 instructional register (보여 주겠습니다, 설명합니다). A single slip, worth normalizing.

editor_note: Both delta entries are the two section headings, and both are faithful and idiomatic: "The Sampler primitive" → "Sampler 프리미티브" and "The Estimator primitive" → "Estimator 프리미티브" keep the API class names in English (matching the `Sampler`/`Estimator` code spans in the body at lines 45 and 65) and render "primitive" with the standard Korean transliteration 프리미티브, dropping the English article as Korean headings normally do; no drift, no added or lost meaning, anchors intact.

Meaning is fully faithful throughout — the exam facts (20문제, 최소 16문제 정답, 두 번의 시도에서 합격 점수를 받지 못하면 일시적으로 잠깁니다), the maintenance notice, and the entire Credly/개인정보 paragraph all match the English with no drift, softening or hallucination. Two editorial slips remain. (1) "course" is rendered inconsistently within the file: the heading and body use 강좌 ("강좌 후 설문조사", "이 강좌의 학습 및 활동을") but the survey paragraph switches to 코스 twice in one sentence ("이 코스를 완료하신 것을 축하합니다 … 저희 코스를 개선하는 데"); one of the two should be picked, and 강좌 matches the heading. (2) The register mixes 해요체 with 하십시오체: 받으세요/확인하세요 sit alongside 축하합니다 and 주시기 바랍니다 in the survey paragraph, which also drops the English's "take a moment" softener. Neither would mislead a learner.

examples.source: Congratulations on completing this course! Please take a moment to help us improve our course …
examples.translation: 이 코스를 완료하신 것을 축하합니다! 다음 [간단한 설문조사]를 작성하여 저희 코스를 개선하는 데 도움을 주시기 바랍니다.
examples.suggested: 이 강좌를 완료하신 것을 축하합니다! 잠시 시간을 내어 다음 [간단한 설문조사]를 작성해 저희 강좌를 개선하는 데 도움을 주세요.
examples.why: 'course' is 강좌 in the heading (강좌 후 설문조사) and in line 18 (이 강좌의 학습 및 활동을) but 코스 twice here — a within-file inconsistency a native editor would unify. The rewrite also restores the dropped 'take a moment' softener.

examples.source: Please take a moment to help us improve our course …
examples.translation: … 도움을 주시기 바랍니다.
examples.suggested: … 도움을 주세요.
examples.why: 해요체 is the file's convention elsewhere (받으세요 in the description, 확인하세요 in line 22); 주시기 바랍니다 is a 하십시오체 slip in the one paragraph that also carries 축하합니다.

editor_note: All three delta entries are semantically faithful — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat. Entry 65 ("이제 시뮬레이터를 사용하여 알고리즘을 테스트하겠습니다") and entry 86 ("비용 함수의 최솟값(-1.857...)은 하트리 단위로 나타낸 H2 분자의 바닥 상태 에너지입니다") are exact and natural; "in units of hartrees" is correctly rendered as "하트리 단위로 나타낸", matching the "-1.83 하트리 / -1.85 하트리" usage later in the file. The one editorial slip is in entry 66: "statevector overlap" is rendered "상태 벡터 중첩", and 중첩 is the standard Korean term for *superposition*, so "상태 벡터 중첩에 대한 페널티" can be misread as a penalty on superposition rather than on state overlap. The same file already renders this concept as 오버랩 elsewhere ("오버랩 계산을 추가합니다", "오버랩 Circuit과 패널티 항"), so the split is also a within-file inconsistency; a native editor would harmonize on 오버랩 (or 겹침). Entry 66's other terms are right: "tolerance on the classical optimizer" → "고전 최적화기의 허용 오차", "approximation error and global phase" → "근사 오차와 전역 위상(global phase)". editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout, including the demanding last 40% — the geometric-reflection section ((2t+1)θ ≈ π/2, the over-rotation caveat "반복 횟수가 너무 많으면 |A_1⟩을 지나쳐 … 다시 감소하기 시작합니다"), the Minesweeper parity argument ("XOR은 홀짝성 연산이므로 … *짝수* 개(구체적으로 두 개)가 참이기를 원하므로 $\lnot$로 부정합니다"), and all T/F and MC options are accurate; no drift, no hallucination, no inverted condition. The defects are completeness and consistency. One whole source paragraph is left in raw English (line 111, "Often, the marking gate $Z_f$ and the diffusion layers … only a single repetition of the Grover operator is shown."), together with its image alt text at line 110 — a Korean-only reader loses the definition of the term "Grover operator" that the rest of the page then uses. Delta entry 76 is faithful and idiomatic: "어떤 계산 기저 상태 중첩이 모든 홀수 이진수에서 피크를 갖는 QFT에 대응할까요?" keeps the question's direction (state → its QFT), the "every odd binary number" quantifier, and 해요체; spelling out EN's shorthand "computational state" as 계산 기저 상태 matches the page's own convention and the following answer block (상태 $\psi = |0\rangle - |N/2\rangle$의 QFT ... 홀수 이진수 상태에서 피크).

Meaning in all seven rewritten entries is faithful — the no-cloning statement keeps "원본을 보존하면서" (preserving the first copy), the 5-bits-per-letter arithmetic in the (a) answer is exact ("5비트마다 한 글자에 이동을 적용"), and the 50-50/≈10-bits expectation and the 9·11 / 4·15 spread are all correct; nothing here would mislead a learner. Both delta entries are faithful: "ground state energy" → 바닥 상태 에너지 (the standard Korean term, used consistently across the file), and the closing note renders the exothermic caveat intact — 반응 에너지가 음수 값 → 에너지가 방출되며, 생성된 분자가 두 개의 단일 원자보다 더 낮은 에너지 상태에 있음 — with the sign, the direction of energy release, and the "lower than two single atoms" comparison all preserved, followed by the mirrored "6. 결론" line.

Stub index page whose only prose is the title and two link labels: "Modules"→모듈, "Computer Science"→컴퓨터 과학, "Quantum Mechanics"→양자 역학 — all standard Korean renderings, nothing dropped or added, and no misleading content is possible here (양자 역학 vs. the closed-up 양자역학 is a defensible spacing choice, not a defect).

All three rewritten entries are semantically faithful — no drift, no hallucination: entry 32 correctly keeps the spin-1 setup's reversal ("반정렬이 아니라 정렬된 스핀을 가져야 합니다") and the $+y$/$+y$ correlation, entry 28 preserves both questions (same-result vs. different-result experiments) without inverting them, and entry 9 renders "uncertainty" with the correct QM term 불확정성. The two remaining problems are consistency, not meaning. (1) The rewrites split "option" two ways within the delta set itself: entry 28 says 선택지 (matching the defined headings "__선택지 1__ (아인슈타인)" / "__선택지 2__ (보른)") while entry 32 says "두 옵션 중 어느 쪽" — a reader meets 선택지 and 옵션 for the same defined term in adjacent paragraphs. (2) Entry 9 transliterates the presenter as 케이티 매코믹 while the immediately preceding entry 8 keeps "Dr. Katie McCormick" in Latin script, so the same person is named two ways one line apart. Neither misleads; both are one-word fixes.

examples.line_approx: entry 32 (Accordion answer, 'Check your understanding' after Our options)
examples.source: As before, this could result from either option.
examples.translation: 이전과 마찬가지로, 이는 두 옵션 중 어느 쪽에서도 나올 수 있는 결과입니다.
examples.suggested: 이전과 마찬가지로, 이는 두 선택지 중 어느 쪽에서도 나올 수 있는 결과입니다.
examples.why: The page defines the two positions as "__선택지 1__ (아인슈타인)" and "__선택지 2__ (보른)", and the sibling delta entry 28 also uses 선택지. Rendering the same defined term as 옵션 here forces the reader to re-map the label mid-argument. Concept stays identifiable, so MINOR.

examples.line_approx: entry 9 (IBMVideo title, right after the walkthrough link)
examples.source: <IBMVideo title="Katie McCormick explores Bell's theorem using a real quantum computer. …"/>
examples.translation: 케이티 매코믹이 실제 양자 컴퓨터를 사용해 벨의 정리를 탐구합니다. …
examples.suggested: Katie McCormick 박사가 실제 양자 컴퓨터를 사용해 벨의 정리를 탐구합니다. …
examples.why: The line directly above (entry 8) keeps the name in Latin script — "Dr. Katie McCormick의 모듈 해설 영상" — so the video caption names the same presenter in a different script one line later. Purely a consistency slip; the sentence itself is accurate and idiomatic.

examples.source: …a measurement of the other particle along the $y$ axis must also yield $+y$, and so on.
examples.translation: …다른 입자를 $y$ 축을 따라 측정한 결과도 반드시 $+y$가 되어야 하며, 이런 식으로 계속됩니다.
examples.suggested: …다른 입자를 $y$ 축을 따라 측정한 결과도 반드시 $+y$가 되어야 하고, 다른 축에서도 마찬가지입니다.
examples.why: "이런 식으로 계속됩니다" is a literal reading of "and so on" that suggests a temporal sequence rather than "likewise for the other axes". Defensible as written and not misleading — noted only as a polish point, not counted among the two issues.

editor_note: All 8 delta entries are faithful and idiomatic 해요체: the three Qiskit-patterns headings now read 1단계/2단계/4단계 (matching the pre-existing 3단계 heading), entry 37 renders "especially simple case of post-processing" as "이것은 특히 간단한 후처리 사례로, 단순히 카운트를 시각화합니다", and the (a)/(b)/(c) prompts correctly preserve the English's expect-vs-obtain split ("불확정도가 0이 되는 상태는 무엇이라고 예상하나요?" vs "기댓값 $\langle Y \rangle$가 0이 되는 상태는 무엇인가요?"). Terminology is consistent with the rest of the page (uncertainty→불확정도, expectation value→기댓값, post-processing→후처리); no drift, no dropped caveat, no hallucination. (Out of delta scope, for the record: the intro bullet list still mixes "Step 1/Step 2/Step 4" with "3단계" — the reworked headings are the consistent side of that split, not its cause.)

The SWAP-decomposition "Check your understanding" block is structurally broken: the exercise prompt ("Verify that the combination of CNOTs above results in a SWAP gate…") is missing from the question slot, which instead repeats the preceding narration paragraph almost verbatim ("여기서 Circuit 다이어그램에서 여러 게이트가 어떻게 표시되는지 처음으로 확인할 수 있습니다…"), while the prompt itself has been pushed inside the <AccordionItem title="Answer"> and the source's own answer lead-in "With matrix multiplication:" (행렬 곱셈으로) is dropped entirely. A learner opening "Answer" is told to go verify something rather than shown the verification, and the exercise section poses no exercise — the pedagogical unit no longer matches its setup. Secondary, non-misleading slips: "target qubit" is rendered three ways within the file (표적 Qubit at the CNOT section, 목표 큐비트 in the Toffoli section, 대상 Qubit in the half-adder mapping section); "half-adder" splits between 반가산기 (earlier) and 절반 가산기 (Conclusion and the paragraph before it); the Toffoli truth table and the SWAP-verification table keep untranslated "Input | Output" / "Input" headers while every other table uses 입력/출력; and the otherwise consistent 합니다체 register breaks once with "살펴봤어요" in the Conclusion. Everything else — 중첩/얽힘/계산 기저 상태/리틀 엔디언/유니터리/Transpiler/Sampler/오류 억제 및 완화 — is accurate, conventional and consistent, and the physics passages (global vs relative phase, measurement collapse probability, reversibility of quantum gates) are faithful.

examples.source:
### Check your understanding

Verify that the combination of CNOTs above results in a SWAP gate. You can do so with matrix multiplication or any other method.

<AccordionItem title="Answer">

examples.why: The exercise prompt is displaced into the Answer body and the question slot is filled with a near-duplicate of the immediately preceding paragraph (ko 460), while the source's answer lead-in "With matrix multiplication:" is dropped. The section presents no question and the "Answer" opens with an instruction, so the exercise no longer matches its setup.

examples.source: target qubit
examples.translation: 표적 Qubit (CNOT section) / 목표 큐비트 (Toffoli section) / 대상 Qubit (half-adder mapping and its answer)
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering (대상 큐비트 or 표적 큐비트) and use it throughout; likewise use 큐비트 or Qubit consistently rather than switching in the Toffoli paragraph only.
examples.why: Three different renderings of the same core term inside one teaching file; recognizable but a native technical editor would unify them, especially since the Toffoli paragraph is the only place that switches to 큐비트.

examples.source: half-adder
examples.translation: 반가산기(half-adder) … 양자 반가산기 … then *양자* 절반 가산기 / 고전 절반 가산기
examples.suggested: 반가산기 everywhere (양자 반가산기 / 고전 반가산기).
examples.why: 반가산기 is the established Korean term and is used for most of the file; the Conclusion-area switch to the literal 절반 가산기 reads as a different concept to a student skimming for the term.

examples.source: We looked at the classical half-adder circuit and then showed you how to adapt the circuit to run with qubits on a quantum computer.
examples.translation: 고전 절반 가산기 Circuit을 살펴본 뒤, 이를 양자 컴퓨터에서 Qubit으로 실행할 수 있도록 변환하는 방법을 살펴봤어요.
examples.suggested: …변환하는 방법을 살펴보았습니다.
examples.why: Single 해요체 sentence in an otherwise uniformly 합니다체 document (the surrounding sentences in the same paragraph end in ~되었습니다/~설계되었습니다), so it reads as an unedited slip rather than a deliberate register choice.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination anywhere: the Open Plan free-time comparison ("무료 시간보다 훨씬 짧은 시간 안에"), the simulator fallback caveat, and the linear-algebra/Python prerequisites all match the English exactly, and domain terms are right (uncertainty→불확정성, superposition→중첩, 학부 양자역학 강의). Two things a native technical editor would change. (1) The instructor sentence splits the single English clause "can request … by filling out this survey" into two coordinated predicates that both end in 요청할 수 있— ("…노트북을 요청할 수 있으며, … 설문을 작성하여 요청할 수 있습니다"), a calqued, visibly redundant construction; Korean would fold it into one ("…설문을 작성하면 정답 키와 배치 안내가 포함된 노트북 버전을 받을 수 있습니다"). (2) "Some Python familiarity" is rendered 어느 정도의 Python 숙련도 — 숙련도 means proficiency/skill level and slightly overstates mere familiarity; 친숙함 or 기본적인 이해 is the right register for a prerequisite that the same bullet then says is optional. Neither would mislead a learner. Register is 합니다체 throughout, consistent with the rest of the ko corpus (991 습니다 / 642 합니다 in this module tree), so it is not treated as a slip.

examples.source: Instructors can request versions of these notebooks with answer keys and guidance on placement in common curricula by filling out this quick survey on how the notebooks are being used.
examples.translation: 강사는 정답 키와 일반 커리큘럼에 배치하기 위한 안내가 포함된 버전의 노트북을 요청할 수 있으며, 노트북이 어떻게 활용되고 있는지에 대한 이 간단한 설문을 작성하여 요청할 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 강사는 노트북이 어떻게 활용되고 있는지에 대한 이 간단한 설문을 작성하면, 정답 키와 일반 커리큘럼 내 배치 안내가 포함된 노트북 버전을 요청할 수 있습니다.
examples.why: The single English clause is split into two coordinated predicates that both end in '요청할 수 있—', so the same verb is stated twice within one sentence. Meaning is preserved but the sentence reads as calqued MT; a Korean technical writer would make the survey a conditional/means clause and keep one main predicate.

examples.source: Some Python familiarity, though most notebooks can simply be run as written
examples.translation: 어느 정도의 Python 숙련도, 다만 대부분의 노트북은 작성된 그대로 실행할 수 있습니다
examples.suggested: Python에 대한 어느 정도의 친숙함(다만 대부분의 노트북은 작성된 그대로 실행하면 됩니다)
examples.why: 숙련도 denotes proficiency/skill level, which is a stronger prerequisite than 'familiarity' — and the same bullet immediately says the notebooks can just be run as written, so the strengthened noun works against the sentence's own concession. 친숙함 or 기본적인 이해 matches the English weight.

editor_note: Meaning is fully faithful — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat: every table row maps 1:1 to the English (circuit cutting → "게이트와 와이어를 커팅하여 회로 폭과 깊이를 줄입니다", SQD → "기저 상태 추정을 위한 샘플 기반 양자 대각화", OBP → "회로 깊이를 줄이기 위한 연산자 역전파", MPF → "향상된 해밀토니안 시뮬레이션을 위한 다중 곱 공식", PNA → "오류 완화를 위한 전파 잡음 흡수"), and the Binder/Jupyter sentence keeps both execution options. Two cosmetic slips a native technical editor would still touch: the closing line "API 문서는 ... 개별 애드온 저장소를 방문하세요" pairs the topic marker 는 on "API 문서" with a transitive 방문하다 on a different object, which reads loose — "API 문서를 보려면 ... 저장소를 방문하세요" is the idiomatic form; and "addon" is rendered two ways inside the same short file (heading "사용 가능한 Addons" / table header "Addon" vs. body "각 애드온", "개별 애드온 저장소"). Neither could mislead a learner. Register is consistent 합니다체 with a 하세요 imperative, i.e. standard Korean technical-doc voice rather than 해요체, with no 하십시오체/드리 honorific slips.

examples.source: For API documentation, visit the individual addon repos on GitHub.
examples.translation: API 문서는 [GitHub](...)의 개별 애드온 저장소를 방문하세요.
examples.suggested: API 문서를 보려면 [GitHub](...)의 개별 애드온 저장소를 방문하세요.
examples.why: The topic-marked 'API 문서는' does not govern the transitive 방문하다, whose object is 저장소를; a Korean technical writer would use a purpose clause (…를 보려면) or switch the verb (…에서 확인하세요). Grammatical enough to parse, but it reads as a calque of the English fronted prepositional phrase.

examples.source: Addon / addon
examples.translation: 사용 가능한 Addons (heading), Addon (table header), 각 애드온 / 개별 애드온 저장소 (body)
examples.suggested: Pick one surface form for the common noun — either 애드온 throughout the prose and headings, or keep Addon everywhere except the product name 'Qiskit Addons'.
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency: the same common noun alternates between transliterated 애드온 and bare Addon across heading, table and prose. The concept stays perfectly identifiable, so this is cosmetic, but it is exactly the kind of split a native editor would normalize.

editor_note: All five rewritten headings are faithful and natural against their English: "1단계. 문제 매핑", "클러스터 수준 리소스", "a. 노이즈율 학습", "b.i. 실제로 학습한 노이즈율로 병합된 경계 업데이트", and "b.ii. 하드웨어 실행을 위한 `local_scales` 계산" (code identifier correctly left as-is, 해요체 body register intact).

Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat; the two load-bearing definitions (CVaR = "α 비율의 최선 샷들의 평균", α=1 → 기댓값 / α=0 → 최솟값, and the cut criterion "고유값 = -1일 때 컷에 속합니다") all survive intact, and the last 40% (Step 3/4, the H_C derivation, the gray/purple partition plot) tracks the English sentence for sentence. What a native technical editor would change is consistency and two register slips: section headings are half-localized ("### 1단계:" / "## 3단계:" but "### Step 2:" / "## Step 4:" left in English); CVaR is named "조건부 위험값" at line 43 and "조건부 위험 가치" at line 716; "expectation value" is spelled 기댓값 (43, 44) then 기대값 (720); "vertex" is 꼭짓점 (100) then 정점 (1015). Line 1096 "이 연구가 흥미로우셨다면" applies subject honorific -시- to an inanimate subject (사물존대), and "다음 자료도 관심 가질 수 있습니다" is a calque of "you might be interested in". None of this misleads a learner.

examples.source: ### Step 2: Optimize problem for quantum hardware execution / ## Step 4: Post-process and return result in desired classical format
examples.translation: ### Step 2: 양자 하드웨어 실행을 위한 문제 최적화 / ## Step 4: 결과를 원하는 고전적 형식으로 후처리하여 반환하기
examples.suggested: ### 2단계: 양자 하드웨어 실행을 위한 문제 최적화 / ## 4단계: 결과를 원하는 고전적 형식으로 후처리하여 반환하기
examples.why: Steps 1 and 3 are already localized as "1단계:" and "3단계:" in the same file; leaving 2 and 4 as "Step" makes the four-step walkthrough look like two different documents in the sidebar and page body.

examples.source: the Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) … / a Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) cost function
examples.translation: 조건부 위험값(CVaR) … / 조건부 위험 가치(Conditional Value at Risk, CVaR) 비용 함수
examples.suggested: Pick one expansion (조건부 위험가치, CVaR) and use it at both places.
examples.why: The term is introduced in Background under one Korean name and re-introduced in Step 3 under another, so a reader may not realize the second occurrence is the same quantity already defined.

examples.source: If you found this work interesting, you might be interested in the following material:
examples.translation: 이 연구가 흥미로우셨다면 다음 자료도 관심 가질 수 있습니다:
examples.suggested: 이 내용이 흥미로우셨다면 다음 자료도 함께 살펴보세요:
examples.why: "연구가 … 흥미로우셨다면" attaches the subject honorific -시- to an inanimate subject (사물존대), which native editors treat as an error, and "관심 가질 수 있습니다" is a word-for-word calque of "might be interested" that no Korean technical writer would produce.

examples.source: This process allows the problem to be mapped to a more optimal initial state for a specified SWAP strategy
examples.translation: 이 과정을 통해 문제를 지정된 SWAP 전략에 맞는 최적의 초기 상태로 매핑할 수 있으며
examples.suggested: … 지정된 SWAP 전략에 더 적합한 초기 상태로 매핑할 수 있으며
examples.why: The English comparative "more optimal" becomes the superlative "최적의" (the optimal one), promising an optimality the SAT binary search does not guarantee; a dropped qualifier rather than a false claim, so minor.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner: every number (24%/36%, 6–25 및 26–50 Qubit, 깊이 4/8, 10-Qubit·26-Qubit 케이스), the depth-vs-gate-count trade-off, the mirror-circuit noise-floor limitation, and the closing "특정 커플링 맵에서만 사용 가능" caveat all survive intact, and 해요체/합니다체 register is consistent with no honorific slips. What a native technical editor would still change: (1) "negative values indicate the default was better" became "음수 값은 기본값이 더 나았음을 나타냅니다" — 기본값 reads as "default *value*", not the default transpiler (elsewhere correctly 기본 Transpiler); (2) "at the cost of roughly 9% higher gate count" became "약 9% 더 높은 Gate 수를 희생합니다", which is not idiomatic Korean (one does not 희생하다 a *higher* count) and is briefly ambiguous about which direction gate count moves; (3) the Step 2 sentence drops the causal frame "Local simulation later stays tractable because…", leaving only the mechanism, so the pedagogical "why this matters" is flattened; (4) "SABRE does match or beat it on individual circuits" is softened to a mere possibility ("낼 수도 있습니다"). Also minor: 트랜스파일 vs "Transpile 시간" are mixed within the file, and "경향을 … 강화합니다" (reinforce) is a calque a Korean writer would render 뒷받침합니다/재확인해 줍니다.

examples.source: Positive values indicate the AI-powered transpiler produced better results; negative values indicate the default was better.
examples.translation: 양수 값은 AI 기반 Transpiler가 더 나은 결과를 냈음을, 음수 값은 기본값이 더 나았음을 나타냅니다.
examples.suggested: 음수 값은 기본 Transpiler가 더 나았음을 나타냅니다.
examples.why: ‘기본값’ means “default value” (a number), not “the default transpiler”. The same referent is rendered 기본 Transpiler everywhere else in the file (lines 25, 320, 434, 622), so this is both wrong and inconsistent.

examples.source: the AI-powered transpiler achieves roughly 16% lower two-qubit depth on average, but at the cost of roughly 9% higher gate count
examples.translation: 평균적으로 약 16% 낮은 두 Qubit 깊이를 달성하지만, 약 9% 더 높은 Gate 수를 희생합니다
examples.suggested: 평균적으로 두 Qubit 깊이가 약 16% 낮아지지만, 그 대가로 Gate 수가 약 9% 늘어납니다
examples.why: ‘~를 희생하다’ takes the thing given up as its object, so “약 9% 더 높은 Gate 수를 희생합니다” is a calque of “at the cost of” that a Korean engineer would never write, and momentarily leaves the direction of the gate-count change unclear.

examples.source: Local simulation later stays tractable because the simulation step uses `remap_to_contiguous` to relabel each transpiled circuit onto only its active qubits, so Aer simulates just those qubits instead of the entire device.
examples.translation: 시뮬레이션 단계에서는 `remap_to_contiguous`를 사용하여 각 트랜스파일된 Circuit을 활성 Qubit에만 다시 레이블링하므로, Aer는 전체 디바이스 대신 해당 Qubit만 시뮬레이션합니다.
examples.suggested: 이후의 로컬 시뮬레이션이 감당 가능한 규모로 유지되는 것은, 시뮬레이션 단계에서 `remap_to_contiguous`로 …
examples.why: The English states the payoff first (local simulation stays tractable) and gives the mechanism as the reason; the Korean keeps only the mechanism, so the learner is told what the helper does but not why it is needed.

examples.source: the improvement is visible across most circuit sizes, though SABRE does match or beat it on individual circuits
examples.translation: 대부분의 Circuit 크기에서 개선이 보이지만 개별 Circuit에서는 SABRE가 동일하거나 더 나은 결과를 낼 수도 있습니다
examples.suggested: …개별 Circuit에서는 SABRE가 동일하거나 더 나은 결과를 내기도 합니다
examples.why: The English asserts this as an observed fact about the plotted data (“does match or beat”); ‘낼 수도 있습니다’ demotes it to a hypothetical possibility, softening a caveat the plot actually shows.

examples.source: transpilation time
examples.translation: ‘Transpile 시간’ (line 25) vs ‘트랜스파일 시간’ (lines 334, 624)
examples.suggested: 파일 전체에서 ‘트랜스파일 시간’으로 통일
examples.why: The same metric name is written two ways within one document; the learning-outcomes bullet uses the English stem while the analysis sections use the Korean transliteration.

editor_note: Judged entry 37 only: "The Hamiltonian is as follows:" → "해밀토니안은 다음과 같습니다:" (line 130) is exact, idiomatic, and uses the same 해밀토니안 rendering and 합니다-form colon lead-in as the parallel sentence "전체 Trotter 회로는 다음과 같습니다:" earlier in the file, so nothing drifts and nothing a native editor would change.

Meaning is faithful throughout — the mirror-circuit rationale, the barrier/transpiler caveat, the little-endian note, the five-job accumulation (DD → TREX → Twirling → ZNE) and the ZNE "larger error bar" trade-off all survive intact, and no claim is hallucinated or inverted. What a native technical editor would change: (1) "identity operator" is rendered 단위 연산자 in the mirror-circuit section; the conventional Korean term is 항등 연산자, and 단위 연산자 risks being read as "unitary" in exactly the section where unitary_overlap appears. (2) Three within-file inconsistencies: 워크플로 (Background) vs 워크플로우 (Large-scale section); 동적 디커플링 in the Learning-outcomes/analysis prose vs bare "Dynamical decoupling" in the Background and Step-3 bullet lists; 영잡음 외삽법 throughout vs 영잡음 외삽 in the final bullet. (3) "does not come for free" is calqued as 무료로 얻어지는 것이 아니며 (무료 = "no charge"), where Korean technical prose would say 공짜로 얻어지는 것은 아니며 / 그만한 대가가 따르며, and the English causal "because" is flattened into a mere 며 coordination. (4) The 50-qubit DD bullet turns an observation about this run ("might have worsened performance") into a general rule (추가하면 … 나빠질 수 있습니다), slightly loosening the tie to the measured result. Register is consistent and correct (참조하세요/유의하세요/살펴보세요; no 드리 or 하십시오 forms). None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: The resulting circuit implements the identity operator, which can trivially be simulated.
examples.translation: 결과 Circuit은 단위 연산자를 구현하므로 간단히 시뮬레이션할 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 결과 Circuit은 항등 연산자를 구현하므로 손쉽게 시뮬레이션할 수 있습니다.
examples.why: 항등 연산자 is the conventional Korean rendering of 'identity operator'. 단위 연산자 is ambiguous and, in a paragraph built around unitary_overlap, invites confusion with 유니터리(unitary) 연산자.

examples.source: you will scale up the workflow to 50 qubits / you've developed and tested our workflow on a 10-qubit circuit
examples.translation: 마지막에는 워크플로를 50 Qubit으로 확장합니다 … 10-Qubit Circuit으로 워크플로우를 개발하고 테스트했으니
examples.suggested: Use 워크플로 in both places (and likewise pick one of 동적 디커플링 / Dynamical decoupling for the bullet lists at lines 21, 35, 219, and one of 영잡음 외삽법 / 영잡음 외삽 at lines 41 and 422).
examples.why: The same term is spelled two ways within one file; the concept stays identifiable, so this is cosmetic, but it is exactly what an editor would normalize.

examples.source: However, note that this improvement does not come for free, because the ZNE result also has a larger error bar.
examples.translation: 단, 이 개선은 무료로 얻어지는 것이 아니며, ZNE 결과의 오차 막대도 더 크다는 점에 유의하세요.
examples.suggested: 단, 이 개선에는 대가가 따릅니다. ZNE 결과는 오차 막대가 더 크기 때문입니다.
examples.why: 무료 means 'free of charge' and reads as a literal calque here; the English 'because' is also flattened into a neutral 며 clause, so the causal link between the cost and the wider error bar is weaker than in the source.

examples.source: The addition of dynamical decoupling might have worsened performance compared to the no-mitigation case.
examples.translation: 동적 디커플링(Dynamical Decoupling)을 추가하면 완화 없음 경우에 비해 성능이 오히려 나빠질 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 동적 디커플링을 추가한 경우, 완화를 적용하지 않은 경우보다 성능이 오히려 나빠졌을 수 있습니다.
examples.why: The English reports what this particular 50-qubit run showed; the Korean states a timeless general rule, so the reader loses the link to the plotted result. Also 완화 없음 경우 is stiff — 완화를 적용하지 않은 경우 is what a native writer would use.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — every caveat in the mirror-circuit passage (대리체, Gate 수 두 배, 노이즈 효과 과장, 대칭 상쇄 시 과소평가) and the whole analysis/recommendations block survive intact, and the metric claims (SABRE=Gate 수·런타임, AI=2-Qubit 깊이) are correctly assigned. Four editorial defects: (1) "near-term quantum devices" is rendered "근거리 양자 디바이스" (line 43) — 근거리 is spatial "short-range", not the temporal "근시일 내/단기" the field means; (2) core terms split within the file — Circuit is kept in English everywhere but becomes 회로 in "회로별 표" (553) and "역 회로" (881), and Gate becomes 게이트 in "기저 게이트" (125); (3) a softened claim at line 877, "AI 기반 Transpiler는 거의 빠르지 않습니다" ("is rarely fast") for EN "is rarely the quickest" — the English is about who wins, the Korean about absolute speed; (4) register is mixed — imperatives alternate between 하십시오체 ("유의하십시오" 885, "유념하십시오" 1075/1402) and 해요체 ("참조하세요" 52/58). Plus one calque, "요약 표도 동일한 분리를 반영합니다" (1388) for "reflects the same split". None of these would mislead a learner about the physics or the benchmark result.

examples.source: both of which directly impact the quality of results on near-term quantum devices
examples.translation: 이 두 가지는 모두 근거리 양자 디바이스에서의 결과 품질에 직접적인 영향을 미칩니다
examples.suggested: 이 두 가지는 모두 근시일 내에 사용할 양자 디바이스(near-term)에서의 결과 품질에 직접적인 영향을 미칩니다
examples.why: 'near-term' is temporal (the NISQ-era devices available soon); 근거리 means 'short-range/nearby distance'. A Korean reader gets a spatial adjective where a time-horizon qualifier belongs.

examples.source: The per-circuit table shows … / we append its inverse $U^\dagger$ / basis gates
examples.translation: 회로별 표는 … / 역 회로 $U^\dagger$를 추가하여 … / 기저 게이트를 결정합니다
examples.suggested: Circuit별 표는 … / 역 Circuit $U^\dagger$를 추가하여 … / 기저 Gate를 결정합니다
examples.why: The file's convention keeps Circuit and Gate in English (Circuit 깊이, Gate 수, SWAP Gate, 미러 Circuit), but three places switch to 회로/게이트 — an in-file inconsistency for the two most frequent domain terms.

examples.source: SABRE and Rustiq are each fastest on about half the circuits, while the AI-powered transpiler is rarely the quickest.
examples.translation: SABRE와 Rustiq는 각각 약 절반의 Circuit에서 가장 빠르지만, AI 기반 Transpiler는 거의 빠르지 않습니다.
examples.suggested: … AI 기반 Transpiler가 가장 빠른 경우는 드뭅니다.
examples.why: The English is a statement about which method wins the runtime comparison; the Korean drops the superlative and asserts the AI transpiler is almost never fast in absolute terms — a softened/shifted claim, though the surrounding text keeps the reader on track.

examples.source: However, note the following caveats: … / Keep in mind that these results are for a single circuit.
examples.translation: 다만 다음 주의 사항에 유의하십시오: … / 이러한 결과는 단일 Circuit에 대한 것임을 유념하십시오.
examples.suggested: 다만 다음 주의 사항에 유의하세요: … / 이러한 결과는 단일 Circuit에 대한 것임을 유념하세요.
examples.why: 하십시오체 imperatives sit next to 해요체 ones used elsewhere in the same file (자세한 내용은 …을 참조하세요, 설치되어 있는지 확인하세요), so the instructional voice shifts register mid-document.

examples.source: The summary table reflects the same split:
examples.translation: 요약 표도 동일한 분리를 반영합니다:
examples.suggested: 요약 표에서도 같은 구도가 나타납니다:
examples.why: '분리를 반영합니다' is a word-for-word calque of 'reflects the same split'; 분리 in Korean technical prose reads as physical separation, not a division of wins between two methods.

editor_note: No semantic drift: the ZZ-parity/ancilla explanation (odd-parity |01⟩/|10⟩ phased, even-parity unchanged; measure 0 → ZZ(θ), measure 1 → ZZ(θ+π) corrected by Z), the "measure_2 is not supported on all backends" partial negation, the commuting-ZZ/measurement-depth-1 argument, and the closing cost/benefit sentence ("SWAP보다 짧은 2-Qubit Gate 깊이 … 그 대신 추가적인 앙실라 Qubit와 고전 피드포워드 연산을 도입합니다") are all faithful. What a native editor would change is consistency and two word choices: "observable" is rendered three ways — 관측값 (l.27, l.235), 관측량 (l.463), Observable (l.1056, l.1191) — and 관측값 literally means "observed value", not the operator; "magnetization" alternates 자화 (l.27) / 자기화 (l.1191, l.1228); "mid-circuit measurement" appears as 미드-Circuit 측정 (l.19), 중간 회로 측정 (l.459) and 중간 Circuit 측정 (l.818); "honeycomb" as 허니콤 (l.104) / 벌집 (l.259, l.284) / 허니컴 (l.1325) and "ancilla" as 보조 큐비트 / 앤실라 Qubit (l.601) / 앙실라 Qubit (l.1325). Two phrasings are stiff enough to misparse: "유니터리 이상 Circuit" (l.1228) for "unitary ideal circuits" (이상 reads as "abnormal/or more") and "원하는 duration으로 해석됩니다" (l.461) for "resolved at compile time" (해석 = interpreted, not resolved/determined). None of these would teach a false concept.

examples.source: Hence, we construct the following observable: … the observables `observables_unitary` or `observables_dynamic` we constructed earlier.
examples.translation: 따라서 다음의 관측값을 구성합니다 … 앞서 구성한 Observable `observables_unitary` 또는 `observables_dynamic`으로 …
examples.suggested: 관측량(observable)으로 통일 — 「따라서 다음의 관측량을 구성합니다」
examples.why: 'observable' is a Hermitian operator; 관측값 means the observed/measured value, so l.27 and l.235 name the wrong object. The file also splits the term three ways (관측값 / 관측량 / Observable), so a reader cannot tell they are the same concept. Recognizable from context, hence minor.

examples.source: We plot both the pre-computed MPS simulation results for the unitary ideal circuits, together with the experimental results from the following:
examples.translation: 유니터리 이상 Circuit에 대한 사전 계산된 MPS 시뮬레이션 결과와 다음의 실험 결과를 함께 플롯합니다:
examples.suggested: 이상적인 유니터리 Circuit에 대한 사전 계산된 MPS 시뮬레이션 결과와 …
examples.why: '유니터리 이상' is a word-order calque of 'unitary ideal'; in Korean 이상 after a noun reads as '이상(abnormality)' or '~ 이상(or more)'. A native writer would put the modifier first: 이상적인 유니터리 회로.

examples.source: The duration variables specified by `stretch` are resolved at compile time into desired durations that satisfy a certain constraint.
examples.translation: `stretch`로 지정된 duration 변수는 컴파일 시점에 특정 제약을 충족하는 원하는 duration으로 해석됩니다.
examples.suggested: … 컴파일 시점에 특정 제약을 충족하는 값으로 결정(확정)됩니다.
examples.why: 'resolved' here means the compiler fixes a concrete value; 해석되다 means 'is interpreted/parsed', which understates the compile-time resolution the `stretch` section is teaching. Meaning is still inferable, so minor.

examples.source: mid-circuit measurements … the mid-circuit measurement and the classical feedforward operations … mid-circuit measurements
examples.translation: 미드-Circuit 측정 (l.19) / 중간 회로 측정 (l.459) / 중간 Circuit 측정 (l.818)
examples.suggested: 중간 회로 측정 (mid-circuit measurement) 한 가지로 통일
examples.why: The same core concept is rendered three different ways within one tutorial; the transliterated 미드-Circuit in the opening paragraph is the odd one out and is the reader's first encounter with the term.

examples.source: they are mid-circuit measurements followed by classical logic operations that determine quantum operations conditioned on the classical output
examples.translation: 미드-Circuit 측정 후 고전적 논리 연산이 뒤따르며, 이 연산은 고전적 출력에 조건부로 양자 연산을 결정합니다
examples.suggested: … 이 연산이 고전적 측정 결과에 따라 수행할 양자 연산을 결정합니다
examples.why: '고전적 출력에 조건부로 … 결정합니다' is a literal transfer of 'conditioned on'; Korean technical writers use '~에 따라' / '~를 조건으로'. Grammatical but reads as machine-shaped.

examples.source: honeycomb (also called hexagonal) lattice … ancilla qubits
examples.translation: 허니콤 격자 (l.104) / 벌집 격자 (l.259, l.284) / 허니컴 격자 (l.1325); 보조 큐비트 (l.263~) / 앤실라 Qubit (l.601) / 앙실라 Qubit (l.1325)
examples.suggested: 격자는 '허니콤(육각형) 격자'로, ancilla는 '보조 큐비트'로 파일 전체 통일
examples.why: Two more within-file splits, including two different transliterations of the same English word (앤실라/앙실라). Each rendering is individually acceptable, so this is a consistency defect rather than a comprehension one.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the teleportation-correction logic (m₁₂=1 → qubit 3에 X, m₂₁=1 → qubit 0에 Z), the MSE definition and its 0-for-perfect / →1-for-random reading, and the CDF axis description (x축 MSE 임계값 / y축 해당 MSE 이하인 qubit 쌍의 비율) all match the English exactly; no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat. What a native technical editor would still fix: (1) a grammatical typo with a doubled object particle in the Background section — "이상적인 Bell 상태에 더 가깝게 도달했음을(충실도가 더 높음)을 의미하며"; (2) "quantify" is rendered two ways in the same document — 정량화 in the learning outcomes and in Step 4 ("MSE를 사용하여 편차를 정량화합니다") but 수량화 in the Background ("이 최종 얽힌 쌍의 품질을 수량화하기 위해"), 정량화 being the conventional physics term; (3) "edge qubits" splits between 에지 Qubit (Background) and 가장자리 qubit (Step 1 bullet); (4) two dropped quantifiers — "all linearly-connected chains of four qubits" loses 모든 ("선형으로 연결된 네 qubit 체인을 프로그래밍 방식으로 탐색합니다") and "much better ... than others" loses the comparison target ("훨씬 더 적합하다"); (5) minor stiffness/calque: the prerequisite bullet "…에 대한 친숙함" and "무거운 최적화" for "heavy optimizations". None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: A lower MSE means the two qubits achieved a Bell state closer to ideal (higher fidelity), whereas a higher MSE indicates more error.
examples.translation: MSE가 낮을수록 두 Qubit이 이상적인 Bell 상태에 더 가깝게 도달했음을(충실도가 더 높음)을 의미하며, MSE가 높을수록 더 많은 오류가 있음을 나타냅니다.
examples.suggested: MSE가 낮을수록 두 Qubit이 이상적인 Bell 상태에 더 가깝게 도달했음(충실도가 더 높음)을 의미하며, MSE가 높을수록 더 많은 오류가 있음을 나타냅니다.
examples.why: Doubled object particle 을 … 을 — a straightforward grammatical typo a Korean writer would not produce; the parenthetical was inserted without removing the first particle.

examples.source: To quantify the quality of this final entangled pair … / We quantify the deviation using the MSE
examples.translation: 이 최종 얽힌 쌍의 품질을 수량화하기 위해 … / MSE를 사용하여 편차를 정량화합니다
examples.suggested: 이 최종 얽힌 쌍의 품질을 정량화하기 위해 …
examples.why: The same verb 'quantify' is rendered 수량화 in one place and 정량화 in two others (learning outcomes and Step 4); 정량화 is the conventional term in Korean physics writing, so the file should settle on it.

examples.source: We programmatically search the device coupling map for all linearly-connected chains of four qubits.
examples.translation: 장치 커플링 맵에서 선형으로 연결된 네 qubit 체인을 프로그래밍 방식으로 탐색합니다.
examples.suggested: 장치 커플링 맵에서 선형으로 연결된 모든 4-Qubit 체인을 프로그래밍 방식으로 탐색합니다.
examples.why: 'all' is dropped, so the exhaustive-search point (reinforced two sentences later by '길이 4의 가능한 모든 경로를 식별함으로써') is weakened on first mention. Not misleading, but a lost qualifier.

examples.source: edge qubits
examples.translation: 두 에지 Qubit … (Background) / 가장자리 qubit 얽기 (Step 1 bullet)
examples.suggested: Pick one — e.g. 가장자리 Qubit throughout (or 에지 Qubit throughout).
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency for a term the reader must track across the whole protocol description; the concept stays identifiable, so this is minor.

examples.source: Familiarity with dynamic circuits … / perform any heavy optimizations that could alter the circuit structure
examples.translation: [동적 Circuit](…)에 대한 친숙함 / Circuit 구조를 변경할 수 있는 무거운 최적화를 수행하지
examples.suggested: 동적 Circuit(…)에 익숙할 것 / Circuit 구조를 변경할 수 있는 대규모 최적화를 수행하지
examples.why: '…에 대한 친숙함' is a noun-for-noun calque of the English bullet that Korean prerequisite lists do not use, and 무거운 최적화 is a literal rendering of 'heavy optimizations' where 대규모/과도한 is idiomatic.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the RZZ range ($0<\theta<\pi/2$), the "assign parameters before transpilation" requirement, the v0.47.0 known-issue caveat, the negative-RZZ→positive + extra X gates result, and the "QPU usage times are almost identical" conclusion all survive intact, and core terms are right (fidelity→충실도, feature map→특징 맵, non-local→비국소, unitary overlap→유니터리 오버랩). What a native technical editor would still change: (1) "당신은 특정 유니터리를 …" (§Fractional gates on IBM QPUs) is a bare calque of English "you" — Korean technical prose drops the pronoun; (2) "non-local gates" is 비국소 게이트 in the learning-outcomes list and Step 2 but 비지역 Gate in "깊이, 실행 시간, 충실도 비교"; (3) "workflow" alternates 워크플로우 (intro, §대규모 하드웨어 예제) and 워크플로 (§분수 게이트 없는 워크플로 및 Circuit 비교, §고급 주제); (4) the transpiler's `constructor-beta` translation stage is rendered "번역 방법", the natural-language sense of the word rather than the transpiler 변환/translation stage; (5) "potentially improving performance" loses its hedge in "전체 Gate 수를 줄이고 성능을 향상시키는 데 의미 있는 이점을 제공할 수 있습니다". None of these would mislead a learner. Register is consistent 합니다체 with two humble "보여드립니다" slips (§RZZ 각도 제약 조건에 대한 워크플로우 접근 방식, §분수 RX Gate로 U Gate 최적화하기).

examples.source: By leveraging the native interactions between physical qubits, you can implement certain unitaries more efficiently on hardware.
examples.translation: 물리적 qubit 간의 네이티브 상호작용을 활용함으로써, 당신은 특정 유니터리를 하드웨어에서 더 효율적으로 구현할 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 물리적 qubit 간의 네이티브 상호작용을 활용하면 특정 유니터리를 하드웨어에서 더 효율적으로 구현할 수 있습니다.
examples.why: '당신은' is a literal calque of English 'you'; Korean technical writing omits the second-person pronoun entirely. Grammatical, but it reads as machine translation.

examples.source: we compare the number of non-local gates and the fidelities between circuits with and without fractional gates
examples.translation: 분수 Gate가 있는 Circuit과 없는 Circuit 간의 비지역 Gate 수와 충실도를 비교합니다
examples.suggested: … 비국소 Gate 수와 충실도를 비교합니다
examples.why: 'non-local gate' is 비국소 게이트 in the learning-outcomes list and in Step 2, but 비지역 Gate here — the same metric plotted in the same section under two names. Recognizable, so MINOR, but inconsistent within one file.

examples.source: we apply the transpiler using `constructor-beta` translation provided by the `qiskit-basis-constructor` package
examples.translation: `constructor-beta` 번역 방법을 사용하여 Transpiler를 적용합니다
examples.suggested: `constructor-beta` 변환(translation) 방법을 사용하여 …
examples.why: 'translation' here is the transpiler's basis-translation stage (`translation_method=`), not natural-language translation; 번역 is the literal-but-off word. The code line disambiguates it, so the learner is not misled.

examples.source: by reducing the overall gate count and potentially improving performance
examples.translation: 전체 Gate 수를 줄이고 성능을 향상시키는 데 의미 있는 이점을 제공할 수 있습니다
examples.suggested: 전체 Gate 수를 줄이고 성능을 향상시킬 가능성이 있어 의미 있는 이점을 제공할 수 있습니다
examples.why: The English hedges only the performance claim ('potentially improving'); the Korean folds it into the sentence-level '~할 수 있습니다', so the performance gain reads slightly firmer than the source. A dropped qualifier, not a false claim.

examples.source: in this tutorial, we demonstrate it through an example inspired by the quantum kernel method
examples.translation: 이 튜토리얼에서는 양자 커널 방법에서 영감을 받은 예제를 통해 이를 보여드립니다
examples.suggested: … 예제를 통해 이를 보여줍니다
examples.why: '보여드립니다' uses the humble 드리- form against the file's otherwise plain 합니다체 (e.g. '살펴봅니다', '시연합니다'). Two isolated slips only.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the oracle/open-control explanation, the "two marked states out of eight in a three-qubit space" setup, the optimal-iteration ratio, and the entire Discussion (exponential 2Q-depth growth, O(sqrt(2^n)) iteration growth, error correction enabling deep circuits) all match the English, with no drift or hallucination in the closing sections. The one real term error is "near-term", rendered twice as 근거리 ("short-distance", a spatial word) in the Next-steps block — "근거리 예제" and "근거리 알고리즘"; Korean quantum writing uses 단기 / 근시일 내 (or NISQ 시대). Secondary: "gate" is split within a single sentence between English Gate and Korean 게이트 ("다중 제어 Z Gate는 … 2-Qubit 게이트로 분해됩니다", and the heading "2-Qubit 게이트 깊이"), and the concluding sentence of the Discussion is a calque of "This makes X impractical" whose modifier attaches awkwardly ("매우 작은 문제 크기를 넘어서는 Grover 알고리즘을 비실용적으로 만듭니다"). None of these would mislead a learner about Grover's algorithm itself.

examples.source: give near-term examples of optimization with quantum computers
examples.translation: 양자 컴퓨터를 이용한 최적화의 근거리 예제를 제공합니다
examples.suggested: 양자 컴퓨터를 이용한 최적화의 단기(near-term) 활용 예제를 제공합니다
examples.why: 근거리 means physical short distance; "near-term" is a time horizon. Korean quantum docs use 단기 / 근시일 내 / NISQ 시대.

examples.source: For a more in-depth look at near-term algorithms
examples.translation: 근거리 알고리즘에 대한 더 깊은 이해를 위해
examples.suggested: 단기(near-term) 알고리즘을 더 깊이 살펴보려면
examples.why: Same spatial-for-temporal error repeated; "근거리 알고리즘" is not a recognizable Korean term and reads as "short-distance algorithms".

examples.source: The multi-controlled Z gate ... decomposes into a number of two-qubit gates
examples.translation: 다중 제어 Z Gate는 ... 2-Qubit 게이트로 분해됩니다
examples.suggested: Use one form for "gate" throughout (either Gate or 게이트), e.g. 다중 제어 Z Gate ... 2-Qubit Gate로 분해됩니다
examples.why: The same word appears as English Gate and Korean 게이트 inside one sentence (and the section heading uses 게이트); a native editor would unify it.

examples.source: This makes Grover's algorithm impractical on current noisy quantum hardware beyond very small problem sizes.
examples.translation: 이는 현재의 잡음이 있는 양자 하드웨어에서 매우 작은 문제 크기를 넘어서는 Grover 알고리즘을 비실용적으로 만듭니다.
examples.suggested: 따라서 아주 작은 문제 크기를 넘어서면 Grover 알고리즘은 현재의 잡음 있는 양자 하드웨어에서 실용적이지 않습니다.
examples.why: Calqued "makes X impractical" causative, and "매우 작은 문제 크기를 넘어서는" attaches to 알고리즘 rather than to the condition; a Korean technical writer would recast as a conditional clause.

editor_note: The one delta entry — the OpenInLabBanner description "이 튜토리얼은 doQumentation을 위해 작성되었습니다." — renders "This tutorial was created for doQumentation." exactly, with the brand name kept and the plain declarative -습니다 style used consistently throughout the rest of the page (e.g. "`StatevectorSampler`를 사용합니다", "무료 IBM Quantum 계정이 필요합니다"); no drift, no added claim, nothing an editor would change.

The physics and workflow prose is faithful and the domain terminology is correct and consistent (implicit/explicit solvent → 암묵적/명시적 용매, dielectric medium → 유전 매질, ground-state energy → 바닥 상태 에너지, PCM → 분극 연속체 모델, SQD → 샘플 기반 양자 대각화, mean field → 평균장, Hamiltonian → 해밀토니안), so nothing here teaches a false concept. Three things a native technical editor would still change. (1) The attribution clause at line 47 inserts a subject the English does not have: "이 연구는 … 전체 워크플로우를 공개하고 … 이를 확장합니다" makes the cited Kaliakin 2025 paper the thing that exposes the full workflow and adds the Heartwood algorithm, geometry optimization and automatic qubit-layout selection, whereas in the English those extensions are what *this tutorial* contributes on top of the Cleveland Clinic research (the tutorial body demonstrates exactly those three). (2) Register: the file uses the humble 드리 form "보여드립니다/보여드린" six times (lines 36, 40, 399, 1400) where the ko corpus norm is 보여줍니다 (73 occurrences vs 9 for 보여드립니다 across all ko tutorials, six of them in this one file), and line 36 repeats it four times in a single paragraph, which reads monotonous rather than like written Korean technical prose. (3) Cleveland Clinic is transliterated 클리블랜드 클리닉 at lines 47 and 1410 but left as "Cleveland Clinic" in the Admonition at line 106 — same entity, two renderings in one file. Minor calques: "메인 노트북 프로그램 바로 옆에" for "exactly next to the main notebook program" (a Korean writer would say 같은 디렉터리에), and the "을(를)" dual-particle hedge in the two Accordion titles.

examples.source: This tutorial is inspired by and based upon research conducted at Cleveland Clinic, as described in [Kaliakin, Danil, et al. ...], exposing the full workflow for implicit solvent calculations and extending it with iterative solvent self-consistency ("The Heartwood Algorithm", M. Motta, T. Pellegrini, 2025), geometry optimization, and automatic qubit layout selection.
examples.translation: 이 튜토리얼은 [Kaliakin, Danil, et al. ...]에서 설명된 클리블랜드 클리닉의 연구에서 영감을 받아 이를 기반으로 작성되었으며, 이 연구는 암묵적 용매 계산의 전체 워크플로우를 공개하고 반복적 용매 자기 일관성("The Heartwood Algorithm", M. Motta, T. Pellegrini, 2025), 기하 최적화, 자동 qubit 레이아웃 선택으로 이를 확장합니다.
examples.suggested: …클리블랜드 클리닉의 연구에서 영감을 받아 이를 기반으로 작성되었으며, 암묵적 용매 계산의 전체 워크플로우를 공개하고 반복적 용매 자기 일관성(…), 기하 최적화, 자동 qubit 레이아웃 선택으로 이를 확장합니다.
examples.why: The inserted subject 이 연구는 hands the extensions to the cited 2025 JPCB paper; in the English the participles attach to the tutorial, which is what actually adds the Heartwood loop, the geomeTRIC optimization and get_zigzag_physical_layout. A learner would credit the paper for work this tutorial contributes.

examples.source: In this tutorial, we demonstrate how a quantum algorithm … We compare … and demonstrate close agreement … We showcase a quantum-centric supercomputing architecture in miniature … The code also demonstrates parallelization …
examples.translation: … 어떻게 적용할 수 있는지 보여드립니다. … 밀접하게 일치함을 보여드립니다. … 아키텍처를 보여드립니다. … 병렬화도 보여드립니다.
examples.suggested: … 살펴봅니다. … 일치함을 확인합니다. … 아키텍처를 보여줍니다. … 병렬화도 보여줍니다.
examples.why: 보여드립니다 is the humble 드리 form the ko convention avoids, and it lands four times in one paragraph; the rest of the ko tutorial corpus uses 보여줍니다 (73×) almost exclusively. Not misleading, but it reads as unvaried and over-deferential for teaching prose.

examples.source: (jointly developed by Cleveland Clinic and IBM)
examples.translation: (Cleveland Clinic과 IBM이 공동 개발)
examples.suggested: (클리블랜드 클리닉과 IBM이 공동 개발)
examples.why: Lines 47 and 1410 transliterate the same organization as 클리블랜드 클리닉; only this Admonition keeps the English name. Within-file inconsistency for one entity.

examples.source: Create a directory exactly next to the main notebook program called `source_files`.
examples.translation: 메인 노트북 프로그램 바로 옆에 `source_files`라는 디렉터리를 만드세요.
examples.suggested: 메인 노트북 프로그램과 같은 디렉터리에 `source_files`라는 디렉터리를 만드세요.
examples.why: 바로 옆에 is a literal calque of "exactly next to" and reads spatially rather than as a filesystem location; Korean technical writing says 같은 디렉터리에/같은 위치에. Same paragraph's Accordion titles also carry the sloppy 을(를) dual-particle hedge.

editor_note: No semantic drift and no hallucination: every prose paragraph (verifiability definition, depth-inefficient scaling of fault-tolerant algorithms, error-mitigation-without-full-fault-tolerance, shot-by-shot error detection) tracks the English faithfully, and 해요체 imperatives (배워보세요 / 시작하세요 / 실험해 보세요) hold throughout with no 하십시오체 or 드리 forms. What a native technical editor would still change is terminology: "observable" is rendered 관측값 ("measured value") in the section title 관측값 추정, in 관측값을 측정하여 and in 관측값 역전파, where the field's convention is 관측가능량 / 옵저버블 — recognizable but it blurs the operator/value distinction that 기댓값 (correctly used for expectation value) depends on. "Advantage" splits within the file between 어드밴티지 (heading 어드밴티지를 향한 워크플로 탐색) and 우위 (계산 우위, 양자 우위), and 워크플로 / 워크플로우 alternate. Two link titles drop "field": transverse-field Ising → 횡단 이징 모델 and tilted-field Ising → 2D 기울어진 이징 (expected 횡자기장 / 기울어진 자기장), and "implicit solvent" is 암묵적 용매 rather than the chemistry-standard 암시적 용매. None of these would teach a false concept.

examples.source: Observable estimation … measuring observables … backpropagating observables
examples.translation: 관측값 추정 … 관측값을 측정하여 … 관측값 역전파
examples.suggested: 관측가능량 추정 … 관측가능량을 측정하여 … 관측가능량 역전파 (or 옵저버블)
examples.why: 관측값 means "measured/observed value", not the observable operator; the file already uses 기댓값 for expectation value, so the operator-vs-value distinction collapses. Recognizable, hence MINOR.

examples.source: workflows toward advantage … computational advantage … quantum advantage
examples.translation: 어드밴티지를 향한 워크플로 탐색 … 계산 우위 … 양자 우위
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering of "advantage" (양자 우위 / 계산 우위 throughout, incl. the heading)
examples.why: The same concept appears as a transliteration in the heading and as 우위 in the body of the very next sentence; within-file inconsistency only.

examples.source: Transverse-Field Ising Model … Simulate 2D tilted-field Ising with the QESEM function
examples.translation: 횡단 이징 모델 … 2D 기울어진 이징 시뮬레이션
examples.suggested: 횡자기장 이징 모델 … 2D 기울어진 자기장 이징 시뮬레이션
examples.why: "Field" is dropped in both; 횡단 reads as "traversal/crossing" rather than "transverse field". The model is still identifiable from context, so MINOR.

examples.source: Implicit solvent calculations using Qiskit Serverless
examples.translation: Qiskit Serverless를 사용한 암묵적 용매 계산
examples.suggested: 암시적 용매 계산
examples.why: 암묵적 means "tacit/unspoken"; computational chemistry uses 암시적 용매 (모델) for implicit solvent.

examples.source: the latest and most advanced techniques … problem-specific quantities … physically meaningful quantities
examples.translation: 최신 고급 기법 … 문제별 수량 … 물리적으로 의미 있는 수량
examples.suggested: 최신의 가장 진보된 기법 … 문제별 물리량(양) … 물리적으로 의미 있는 양
examples.why: 수량 is a counting word ("quantity/amount of items"); Korean physics prose uses 양/물리량 for quantities like cost-function values or energies. "latest and most advanced" is also flattened to a single 최신 고급.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination found — every quantitative claim, condition and caveat matches the English (the τ/shift derivation, "reps=8에서 0.045 … 단순 순서와 짝수-후-홀수 순서는 0.075", and the appendix caveat "단일 여기 섹터 내에서의 바닥 상태 … 전역 바닥 상태가 아님" are all faithful). What a native editor would change: (1) eight prose segments are left untranslated in English, including a full explanatory sentence — line 433 "Such matrices where the elements depend on the index differences … are called *Toeplitz*…", line 73 "where the denominator normalizes the state.", line 989 "where $d=2^n$ is the dimension of the Hilbert space.", plus stranded connectives at 734/756/794/1291/1331. (2) "evolution" is 전개 through the Background (49, 52, 126, 127: "실시간 전개된 상태") but 진화 from the Setup on (458, 1272, 1649, 2038), and 전개 is simultaneously used in its normal physics sense of "expansion" at 2054 and 2136 — so 전개 carries two meanings in one file. (3) "overlap" alternates 겹침 행렬 (24, 105) and 중첩 (574, 768, 853, 1650) while 중첩 also renders "superposition" at 503. Also: 기준 상태 (51–367) vs 참조 상태 (444 onward) for "reference state"; a few stiff calques ("에너지 고유 상태 |E_m⟩와 함께 말입니다", "KQD를 조작적으로 제시했습니다", "대응하는 스펙트럼 필터의 대응물"); and mixed heading/register style (1단계/4단계 vs "Step 2:"/"Step 3:", 유의하세요 at 124 vs 유의하십시오/상기하십시오 at 2209/2264).

examples.source: The KQD method builds a Krylov subspace from real-time evolved states,
examples.translation: KQD 방법은 실시간 전개된 상태로부터 Krylov 부분공간을 구성합니다.
examples.suggested: KQD 방법은 실시간 시간 진화된 상태로부터 Krylov 부분공간을 구성합니다.
examples.why: 전개 is the standard Korean word for 'expansion' (and the file itself uses it that way at 2054 'this eigenbasis에서 전개' and 2136 'filter를 전개'), while the second half of the same file correctly renders time evolution as 진화 (458, 1272, 1649). One word doing both jobs makes the Background section read as 'real-time expanded states'.

examples.source: Such matrices where the elements depend on the index differences in this manner are called *Toeplitz* and can be reconstructed from first-row elements indexed by $d=\ell-k$.
examples.translation: Such matrices where the elements depend on the index differences in this manner are called *Toeplitz* and can be reconstructed from first-row elements indexed by $d=\ell-k$.
examples.suggested: 이처럼 원소가 인덱스 차이에만 의존하는 행렬을 *퇴플리츠(Toeplitz)* 행렬이라고 하며, $d=\ell-k$로 인덱싱되는 첫 번째 행의 원소들로부터 전체를 재구성할 수 있습니다.
examples.why: Untranslated. This is the sentence that justifies estimating only the first row — the whole point of the following circuit construction — so the Korean reader loses the reasoning. Same problem at 73, 989 ('where $d=2^n$…') and the stranded 'Then,'/'Here,'/'and'/'where'/'Therefore,' at 734, 756, 794, 1291, 1331.

examples.source: The contribution from $T$ is reconstructed classically using the already measured overlap matrix element $\mathcal{S}_{0d}$.
examples.translation: $T$로부터의 기여는 이미 측정된 중첩 행렬 요소 $\mathcal{S}_{0d}$를 사용하여 고전적으로 재구성됩니다.
examples.suggested: $T$로부터의 기여는 이미 측정된 겹침 행렬 요소 $\mathcal{S}_{0d}$를 사용하여 고전적으로 재구성됩니다.
examples.why: 'overlap' is 겹침 행렬 in the learning outcomes (24) and the definition (105) but 중첩 from 574 on, and 중첩 is also the word used for 'superposition' at 503 ('두 가지 branch의 코히런트 중첩'). Pick 겹침 for overlap throughout so the two concepts stay distinct.

examples.source: with energy eigenstates $|E_m\rangle$.
examples.translation: 에너지 고유 상태 $|E_m\rangle$와 함께 말입니다.
examples.suggested: 여기서 $|E_m\rangle$은 에너지 고유 상태입니다.
examples.why: A literal rendering of the trailing English 'with …' clause; '…와 함께 말입니다' is a sentence tail no Korean technical writer would produce. Same class of stiffness at 2038 ('조작적으로 제시했습니다' for 'presented operationally') and 2274 ('대응하는 … 대응물입니다').

examples.source: Note that this is the ground state within the single-excitation sector … / Recall that the learned filter is a trigonometric polynomial …
examples.translation: … 전역 바닥 상태가 아님에 유의하십시오. / … 삼각 다항식임을 상기하십시오.
examples.suggested: … 전역 바닥 상태가 아니라는 점에 유의하세요. / … 삼각 다항식임을 기억하세요.
examples.why: The file addresses the reader with 유의하세요 at 124 but switches to the formal imperative 하십시오체 in the appendix; the same drift shows in the headings ('1단계:' / '4단계:' vs untranslated 'Step 2:' / 'Step 3:'). Consistency only, meaning unaffected.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the protocol steps (Bell 쌍 체인 → 얽힘 교환 → 게이트 텔레포테이션), the parity/feedforward mapping (ZZ 패리티→타겟에 X, XX 패리티→제어에 Z), the stabilizer argument for ⟨XX⟩=⟨ZZ⟩=+1, the crossover discussion and the 2,280 ns / 68 ns comparison all land correctly, so nothing here misleads. The main defect is terminology: "unitary" is rendered 유니터리 for the whole first half but switches to 단일 ("single") from the batching paragraph onward — 단일(unitary) 방법, 단일 Circuit, 직접 단일 구현 — a literal-but-wrong word that only stays recoverable because the English gloss is repeated at first use in each of those paragraphs; it should be 유니터리 everywhere. Two lesser splits: 동적 회로 vs 다이나믹 회로 (lines ~431, 446, 594, 607) and 유니터리 vs 유니타리 (line ~155) inside the same file. Finally, the Key-points bullet drops the hedge in "not necessarily improved fidelity", asserting flatly 충실도 향상이 아닌 — a slightly strengthened claim, though the surrounding paragraph already states the nuance.

examples.source: the LRCX did not consistently outperform the direct unitary implementation … the depth of the unitary circuit grows linearly with the distance between qubits
examples.translation: LRCX는 직접 단일(unitary) 구현보다 일관되게 우수한 성능을 보이지 않았습니다 … 단일 Circuit의 깊이는 qubit 간 거리에 따라 선형적으로 증가하는 반면
examples.suggested: LRCX는 직접적인 유니터리 구현보다 … 유니터리 회로의 깊이는 큐비트 간 거리에 따라 선형적으로 증가하는 반면
examples.why: 단일 means "single", not "unitary"; the same concept is 유니터리 in the first half of the file (lines 45, 81, 96, 367, 484, 541). Bare later uses (단일 방법, 단일 구현, 단일 Circuit) lose the English gloss and read as "a single circuit".

examples.source: The main present-day motivation is reduced *two-qubit depth*, not necessarily improved fidelity.
examples.translation: 오늘날 주요 동기는 충실도 향상이 아닌 *2-Qubit 깊이* 감소입니다.
examples.suggested: 오늘날 주요 동기는 반드시 충실도 향상이라기보다 *2-Qubit 깊이* 감소입니다.
examples.why: "not necessarily" is a hedge; 아닌 turns it into a flat denial that fidelity improvement is a motivation, strengthening the claim beyond the English.

examples.source: just like we did for the dynamic circuits above / the newer version of dynamic circuits
examples.translation: 위에서 다이나믹 회로에 대해 했던 것과 마찬가지로 … 새로운 버전의 다이나믹 회로
examples.suggested: 위에서 동적 회로에 대해 했던 것과 마찬가지로 … 새로운 버전의 동적 회로
examples.why: The file's own established rendering is 동적 회로 (title, 학습 목표, 배경, and every later paragraph); 다이나믹 회로 appears only in four transition sentences, an unnecessary within-file split of the central term.

examples.source: reducing depth compared to a purely unitary implementation … its unitary equivalent
examples.translation: 순수 유니타리 구현에 비해 깊이(depth)를 줄임으로써 … 그에 상응하는 유니타리 버전
examples.suggested: 순수 유니터리 구현 … 그에 상응하는 유니터리 버전
examples.why: 유니타리 vs 유니터리 spelling split within the same document; the rest of the file uses 유니터리.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the three approximations (약결합 극한, 전역 평균 플럭스, Trotter화), the n_l/(n_l+1)→1 argument, the differential meson−vacuum protocol, and the atol trade-off paragraph (8.5시간, 1e-12/1e-6/1e-3) all match the English with no inverted conditions, swapped quantities or dropped caveats, and the last 40% (PPM section, 잘라내기 임계값, 다음 단계) is as accurate as the opening. The defects are terminological: 'gauge-singlet' is rendered 게이지 특이 ('gauge-singular/peculiar') instead of the standard 게이지 단일항, so the singlet idea behind 하드론 is lost in that gloss; and three core words are split within the file — coherent is 코히런트한 in the title/sidebar but 결맞은 in the body, noise is 노이즈 (title, StatevectorEstimator and PPM paragraphs) but 잡음 (하드웨어 잡음, 저잡음 큐비트 체인), and evolution is 진화 in the Learning-outcomes bullet ('시간 진화 회로') but 전개 everywhere else ('시간 전개 연산자', '진공 전개'). None of these would mislead a learner, but a native technical editor would unify them.

examples.source: hadrons (gauge-singlet fermion pairs at a site)
examples.translation: 하드론(한 사이트에서의 게이지 특이 페르미온 쌍)
examples.suggested: 하드론(한 사이트의 게이지 단일항 페르미온 쌍)
examples.why: 'singlet' is rendered 특이 ('singular/peculiar'), confusing singlet with singular. The conventional Korean particle-physics term is 단일항; as written the reader cannot recover the gauge-invariance idea that makes every LSH basis state physical.

examples.source: robust and coherent non-Abelian hadron dynamics … isolates the coherent hadron signal
examples.translation: 견고하고 코히런트한 비아벨 하드론 동역학 … 결맞은 하드론 신호를 분리합니다
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering — e.g. 결맞은 in both title and body
examples.why: The key adjective from the paper title appears two ways in one file, so the reader may not connect the body's 결맞은 신호 with the title's 코히런트한 동역학.

examples.source: Trotterized time-evolution circuits … time-evolution operator … subtracts the vacuum evolution
examples.translation: Trotter화된 시간 진화 회로 … 시간 전개 연산자 … 진공 전개를 뺍니다
examples.suggested: Fix on one: 시간 전개 / 진공 전개 throughout (or 시간 진화 throughout)
examples.why: 'evolution' is split between 진화 and 전개 within the same tutorial, including the Learning-outcomes bullet versus the Approximation-3 paragraph describing the very same operator.

examples.source: hardware noise … a low-noise chain of physical qubits … noiseless classical simulation … noisy quantum processors
examples.translation: 하드웨어 잡음 … 저잡음 물리적 큐비트 체인 … 노이즈 없는 고전적 시뮬레이션 … 노이즈가 있는 양자 프로세서
examples.suggested: Standardize on 노이즈 (노이즈 없는 / 저노이즈) or on 잡음 across title and body
examples.why: Mixing 잡음 and 노이즈 for the same concept on one page is a consistency slip a Korean technical editor would normalize; meaning is unaffected.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, swapped quantities or hallucinated claims; the delicate hardware-results bullets (k=6 essentially exact vs. the deeper k=10 baseline being worse, the ||x||_1=4.66 exact-static MPF being the worst estimator, t/k_min≲1 caveat) all land correctly. The defects are wording/consistency: "inverse powers of k_j" is rendered "$k_j$의 역제곱 급수" (line 74), which reads as "inverse-SQUARE series" rather than "역거듭제곱" — a dropped generality, though the η_n = 2χ+2n formula right below repairs it. Line 1108 contains a raw calque of "the Trotter-error cancellation it buys": "그것이 사는 Trotter 오차 상쇄 효과", where 사는 parses as "living/buying" and is not Korean a technical writer would write ("그 대가로 얻는 ~ 효과"). Core-term consistency also slips within the file: "시간 전개" is used for *time evolution* while the same word 전개 is used two paragraphs later for *series expansion* ("급수로 전개합니다", line 107) and again in "전개기 팩토리" for evolver factory — 시간 진화/발전 would disambiguate (the frontmatter itself says "시간 진화"); Trotter steps switch from "Trotter 스텝" (lines 54–371) to "Trotter 단계" (lines 760, 1114, 1120); noise switches 잡음 (Background) → 노이즈 (hardware sections); error switches 오차 (body) → 오류 (frontmatter/learning outcomes, "오류 완화"); Frobenius switches 프로베니우스 노름 (line 82) → Frobenius-노름 (lines 483, 567); and observable is 관측량 in the body but 관측값 in the frontmatter description. Headings are half-localized too ("1단계:" vs "Step 2/3/4:"). Register (합니다체 + ~하세요) is consistent and correct, with no 하십시오체/드리 slips.

examples.source: expanding the Trotter error in inverse powers of $k_j$ leads to constraint equations of the form
examples.translation: $k_j$의 역제곱 급수로 Trotter 오차를 전개하면 다음 형태의 제약 방정식이 도출됩니다
examples.suggested: $k_j$의 역거듭제곱(음의 거듭제곱) 급수로 Trotter 오차를 전개하면
examples.why: 역제곱 means 'inverse square', narrowing 'inverse powers' (1/k^{η_n} for a family of exponents) to a single power; the following η_n = 2χ+2n discussion limits the damage, so it is a dropped generality rather than a misleading claim.

examples.source: amplifies the residual gate noise, decoherence, and ZNE error on each ⟨A⟩_{k_j} by roughly the same factor, overwhelming the Trotter-error cancellation it buys
examples.translation: 거의 같은 배율로 증폭시켜, 그것이 사는 Trotter 오차 상쇄 효과를 압도합니다
examples.suggested: 거의 같은 배율로 증폭시켜, 그 대가로 얻는 Trotter 오차 상쇄 효과를 압도합니다
examples.why: 'it buys' is calqued literally as 사는, which in Korean reads as 'living/buying' and is not idiomatic; no native technical writer would phrase the trade-off this way.

examples.source: time-evolution operator … expands each individual [S(t/k_j)]^{k_j} as a series in t/k_j … approximate evolver factory
examples.translation: 시간 전개 연산자 … $t/k_j$의 급수로 전개합니다 … 근사 전개기 팩토리
examples.suggested: 시간 진화(발전) 연산자 … 급수로 전개합니다 … 근사 시간 진화 팩토리
examples.why: 전개 is made to carry both 'time evolution' and 'series expansion' within a few paragraphs, so '전개 시간' (evolution time) can be misread as 'expansion time'; the frontmatter already uses 시간 진화, so the file contradicts itself.

examples.source: Trotter steps k_j
examples.translation: Trotter 스텝 (small-scale sections) / Trotter 단계 (large-scale sections, Next steps)
examples.suggested: Pick one — e.g. Trotter 스텝 — throughout
examples.why: The core countable quantity of the whole tutorial is rendered two ways depending on section; recognizable, but a reader comparing the two halves sees two labels for k_j. Same pattern for 잡음/노이즈 and 오차/오류.

examples.source: Use multi-product formulas in observable estimation to reduce Trotter error
examples.translation: 다중 곱 공식을 관측값 추정에서 사용하여 트로터 오류를 줄이거나
examples.suggested: 다중곱 공식을 관측량(옵저버블) 추정에 사용하여 Trotter 오차를 줄이거나
examples.why: 관측값 means 'observed value', not 'observable' (the body correctly uses 관측량); the description also uses 트로터 오류 while the body uses Trotter 오차, and 다중 곱 vs the body's 다중곱.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the GEM protocol steps, the 21×12=252 circuit count, the ~0.3π noiseless critical angle, the raw-vs-decoded magnetization argument and the final `critical_angle = 0.5000` caveat all survive intact, and there is no hallucinated claim. What a native editor would still change: (1) "two-point correlation" is rendered "이점 상관" (ll. 27, 335, 447), where 이점 collides with the everyday word for "advantage/merit" — the field convention is "2점 상관 (함수)" or "두 점 상관"; (2) "constant-depth" is split within the file between "상수 깊이" (ll. 25, 365) and "일정 깊이" (ll. 44, 447); (3) l. 351 renders "as long as the critical point occurs below 0.5π" as "0.5π 이하에서 발생하는 한", i.e. ≤ instead of a strict <, which sits awkwardly beside l. 443 where the peak sitting exactly at 0.5π is presented as the transition being unresolvable; (4) l. 443 calques "resolve" as "해결할 수 있는" (solve) where the measurement sense requires 분해/식별; (5) l. 447 drops the "only" of "This feat is only possible due to … mid-circuit measurements" ("덕분에 가능합니다"). None of these would build a false concept, so this stays MINOR. Register is consistent ~습니다 with 하세요-form imperatives, which is the normal Korean technical-doc voice here.

examples.source: the average two-point correlation $f$ / the two-point correlation and the normalized variance
examples.translation: 평균 이점 상관 $f$ / 이점 상관과 정규화된 분산
examples.suggested: 평균 2점 상관 함수 $f$ / 2점 상관과 정규화된 분산
examples.why: "이점" is the everyday Korean word for "advantage/benefit"; used bare before the formula it reads as "advantage correlation". The domain convention is 2점 상관 (함수) or 두 점 상관. Recognizable from the defining formula, so MINOR, not a false concept.

examples.source: constant-depth circuits / circuits of only constant depth
examples.translation: 상수 깊이 Circuit (ll. 25, 365) vs 일정 깊이의 Circuit (ll. 44, 447)
examples.suggested: pick one — 상수 깊이 Circuit throughout
examples.why: The same key term of art for the protocol's headline property is rendered two ways in the same file, including once inside the Learning outcomes and once in the Conclusion restating it. Both are recognizable, so this is within-file inconsistency only.

examples.source: the phase transition is still observed as long as the critical point occurs below $0.5 \pi$
examples.translation: 임계점이 $0.5 \pi$ 이하에서 발생하는 한 상전이는 여전히 관찰됩니다
examples.suggested: 임계점이 $0.5 \pi$ 미만에서 발생하는 한 …
examples.why: "이하" is ≤, but the English is a strict "below". The looser boundary contradicts the later hardware paragraph (l. 443), where the peak landing exactly at 0.5π is described as the transition being at the edge of what the sweep can resolve. A dropped strictness qualifier, not a reversed claim.

examples.source: so the transition is at the edge of what this sweep can resolve
examples.translation: 전이는 이 스윕이 해결할 수 있는 한계에 있습니다
examples.suggested: 전이는 이 스윕으로 분해(식별)할 수 있는 한계에 있습니다
examples.why: "resolve" in the measurement sense is 분해/식별, not 해결 (to solve a problem). The calque makes a Korean reader parse "the limit of what this sweep can solve", which is not what the sentence is about.

examples.source: This feat is only possible due to the protocol's use of mid-circuit measurements.
examples.translation: 이 성과는 프로토콜의 중간 Circuit 측정 사용 덕분에 가능합니다.
examples.suggested: 이 성과는 프로토콜이 중간 Circuit 측정을 사용하기 때문에 비로소 가능합니다.
examples.why: The exclusivity of "only possible" — the pedagogical punchline of the conclusion, that mid-circuit measurement is what makes constant depth achievable — is softened to a plain "is possible thanks to". A dropped qualifier.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the tricky passages all land correctly (the QWC-group stop condition "여덟을 초과하면 역전파를 중단", the anti-commuting IZ example, the "exact transformation on a noiseless statevector simulator" paragraph, and the budget caveat "노이즈 감소 효과가 잘라내기 근사 오차에 압도되지 않도록"). What a native technical editor would change: "observable" is rendered two ways with a clean split at the section boundary — 관측 가능량 through the small-scale example, then 관측량 for the whole large-scale section (lines 316/319/321) — and "qubit" likewise alternates between 큐비트 (lines 186, 319) and bare Qubit (lines 104, 198). The truncation-introduction sentence in the large-scale section is circular: EN defines truncation as eliminating small-coefficient terms (which is what reduces the term count), while the Korean makes the term-count reduction the means and the elimination the end ("잘라내기를 통해 ... 항 수를 줄임으로써 계수가 작은 관측량 항을 제거할 수 있습니다"), and it drops "a practice called". The concept still survives because the very next sentence restates it correctly, so this stays MINOR rather than misleading. A few calqued clauses (the embedded "where L is the number of slices" in line 186, the subject mismatch in line 51) read as translationese.

examples.source: observable (throughout)
examples.translation: 관측 가능량 (lines 33-247) → 관측량 (lines 316, 319, 321)
examples.suggested: 관측 가능량 everywhere (or 관측량 everywhere), including 회로-관측 가능량 쌍 at line 316
examples.why: Within-file split of the file's single most-repeated domain term, cleanly aligned with the small-scale/large-scale section boundary, so a reader may wonder whether 관측량 denotes something different from 관측 가능량.

examples.source: Therefore, we can eliminate observable terms with small coefficients using a practice called truncation. While truncation allows more propagation by reducing the number of terms in the updated observable, it also introduces some approximation.
examples.translation: 따라서 잘라내기를 통해 업데이트된 관측량의 항 수를 줄임으로써 계수가 작은 관측량 항을 제거할 수 있습니다. 잘라내기는 항 수를 줄여 더 깊은 전파를 가능하게 하지만 일부 근사를 도입합니다.
examples.suggested: 따라서 계수가 작은 관측량 항을 제거하는 잘라내기(truncation)라는 기법을 사용할 수 있습니다. 잘라내기는 업데이트된 관측량의 항 수를 줄여 더 깊은 전파를 가능하게 하지만, 그 대가로 일부 근사가 introduced됩니다.
examples.why: Means and end are swapped — the English defines truncation as dropping small-coefficient terms (the term-count reduction being its consequence), while the Korean makes reducing the term count the method for dropping them, producing a circular definition that then repeats itself in the next sentence. Not misleading, because the following sentence states the causality correctly.

examples.source: a linear chain CouplingMap of 10 qubits / N being the number of qubits
examples.translation: 10개의 Qubit으로 이루어진 선형 체인 `CouplingMap` / $N$은 Qubit의 수입니다
examples.suggested: 10개의 큐비트로 이루어진 … / $N$은 큐비트의 수입니다
examples.why: Same term appears as 큐비트 elsewhere in the file (lines 186 '2-큐비트 관측 가능량', 319 '50큐비트'); mixing the Latin-script form into Korean prose is inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: Therefore, backpropagation might increase the number of terms in the observable, leading to a higher number of circuit executions. / the number of terms in the operator will generally approach 2^L quickly, where L is the number of slices
examples.translation: 따라서 역전파는 관측 가능량의 항 수를 늘려 더 많은 회로 실행이 필요할 수 있습니다. / 역전파 중 연산자의 항 수는 일반적으로 $L$이 슬라이스 수일 때 $2^L$에 빠르게 근접합니다.
examples.suggested: 따라서 역전파는 관측 가능량의 항 수를 늘려 회로 실행 횟수를 증가시킬 수 있습니다. / 역전파 중 연산자의 항 수는 일반적으로 $2^L$에 빠르게 근접합니다. 여기서 $L$은 슬라이스의 수입니다.
examples.why: First: the subject 역전파는 does not agree with the predicate 필요할 수 있습니다 (a Korean writer would keep 역전파 as the agent of an increase). Second: the English relative 'where …' clause is inlined as a mid-sentence conditional, which a native technical writer would split into a following 여기서 sentence, as this same file already does at line 41.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I found no semantic drift, no inverted condition, no dropped caveat and no hallucination; the technically dense passages (barren-plateau "초다항식적 내성", the ceiling-function note, the tanh loss + regularization definition with β=1/2 and ν=|E|/2+(m−1)/4, and the single-bit swap post-processing at the very end) all match the English exactly, and core terms are conventional and correct (ansatz→앤사츠, Hamiltonian→해밀토니안, expectation value→기댓값, variational→변분, mutually-commuting→상호 가환). What a native technical editor would change is consistency: "partition" is 분할 in the first half (lines 116/152/156/252) but 파티션 in the post-processing half (lines 438/465/477), and "edge" is 간선 in lines 116/252/263 but 에지 in line 477 — the same file names each concept two ways, and the switch lands exactly where the reader needs to connect the loss function to the decoded result. Second, the step headings are half-translated: "1단계:"/"2단계:" for steps 1–2 but the English "Step 3:"/"Step 4:" is left in place at lines 318/436. Third, line 45 keeps the English em-dash as a sentence joiner, fusing "…상관관계 행렬로 나타냅니다 — 노드의 색상은…" into a run-on where Korean would take a period. None of these mislead. Register is the standard Korean doc convention (합니다체 declaratives with ~하세요/~해 보겠습니다 imperatives) and holds consistently; no 하십시오체 or 드리 forms.

examples.source: The sign of the expectation value of the Pauli string indicates the partition of the node. … The partitions of the nodes are determined by evaluating the sign of the expectation values…
examples.translation: …해당 노드의 분할을 나타냅니다. … 노드의 파티션은 … 기댓값 부호를 평가하여 결정됩니다.
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering for "partition" and use it everywhere — 분할 throughout (or 파티션 throughout), e.g. line 438 → "노드의 분할은 노드를 인코딩하는 Pauli 문자열의 기댓값 부호를 평가하여 결정됩니다."
